events.title: The Commons Camping Retreat
events.location: Willits, CA
events.description:
🌲 The Commons Camping Retreat
September 24–27, 2026 · Shimmerback Ranch, near Willits, CA
🌿 About Event
What happens when we take The Commons out of the city and into the woods?
For four days, we’re heading north to Shimmerback Ranch—nearly 150 acres of forest, creek, trails, and gathering spaces about 2.5 hours from San Francisco—to experiment with a slower, more communal rhythm of life.
Think of it as a temporary Commons village: waking up among the trees, cooking and eating together, swimming in the creek, making things with our hands, sharing skills and ideas, tending the land, and having the kind of long, wandering conversations that become possible when nobody has somewhere else to be in an hour.
During the day, we’ll invite members to offer workshops, creative practices, facilitated conversations, crafts, music, and whatever else they’d like to share. Some time may also be devoted to hands-on stewardship projects around the property—an opportunity to learn practical skills while giving something back to the land hosting us.
And when evening arrives? We’ll gather around food and fire, make music, and—far from our usual sound-sensitive neighbors—perhaps finally answer the important civic question: what does a Commons rave look like in the middle of the woods? ✨🌲🔊
This retreat is an experiment in community beyond the walls of 540 and 550: a chance to rest, play, collaborate, and discover what becomes possible when we have a little more time and space with one another.
🕰 Flow / Schedule
This will be a Thursday–Sunday retreat, with plenty of spacious, unscheduled time built in.
Thursday, September 24
Arrival, camp setup, orientation, shared dinner, and settling into the land.
Friday & Saturday
🌲 Slow mornings and shared meals
🛠 Member-led workshops and skill-sharing
🎨 Art, crafting, building, and creative projects
🌿 Optional land stewardship projects
💧 Creek swimming and time to explore or simply rest
🍲 Communal cooking and meals
🎶 Music, jams, dancing, and nighttime gatherings
Sunday, September 27
A final morning together, shared cleanup and stewardship of the space, packing up, and heading home.
A more detailed schedule—and opportunities to propose workshops—will be shared as the retreat takes shape.
👥 Facilitators
The retreat is being organized by Cody Hasty and The Commons, with the weekend itself shaped collaboratively by the members who attend.
Rather than bringing in a fixed program of teachers, we’re imagining something closer to a community unconference: Commons members sharing the skills, practices, questions, and creative pursuits they care about.
Want to teach something, facilitate a conversation, DJ a set, lead a craft, cook for the group, organize a game, or contribute another offering? We’d love for you to help shape the weekend.
💫 Who This Is For
This retreat is for Commons members who want to spend meaningful time together outside the rhythms of everyday city life.
You do not need to be an experienced camper, outdoorsperson, workshop facilitator, or wilderness mystic. 🌿
Come if you’re excited to:
deepen friendships and make new ones
learn and share skills
create things alongside other people
spend a few days surrounded by nature
contribute to communal meals and shared responsibilities
dance, play, rest, swim, wander, talk, or simply exist around a campfire together
The heart of the weekend is participation rather than performance. You can offer a workshop or just show up ready to lend a hand.
🎒 What to Bring (Optional)
A detailed packing list will be shared with attendees before the retreat.
For now, plan for several days of camping and outdoor life, including warm layers for evenings, sturdy shoes, personal toiletries, a flashlight or headlamp, and whatever you need to sleep comfortably.
If you have camping equipment, musical instruments, games, art supplies, crafting tools, or something you’d enjoy sharing with the group, you’re welcome to bring them.
Please do not store food or other bear attractants inside tents. We’ll coordinate safe food storage on-site.
Don't own camping gear? Don't let that stop you from expressing interest—we'll see what we can share and coordinate as a community.
💛 Suggested Donation / Exchange
Our goal is to make the retreat as financially accessible as possible.
The maximum anticipated land cost is approximately $130 per person for the full Thursday–Sunday retreat ($32.50/day). Depending on attendance, Commons support, and opportunities to exchange volunteer stewardship projects for part of the cost, your actual price may be lower—or potentially free.
We’ll confirm the final contribution once we have a reliable headcount.
For those who would rather not sleep in a tent, a limited number of upgraded accommodations—including a bunkhouse, tiny houses, an RV, and glamping options—may be available for an additional cost.
🏛 About The Commons
The Commons is a civic temple for wisdom, belonging, and beauty in San Francisco—a place to practice community rather than simply talk about it.
We believe belonging grows through shared experience: learning together, making things together, caring for spaces together, celebrating together, and showing up for one another.
This retreat takes that experiment beyond our walls. For a few days, instead of simply gathering at The Commons, we get to practice building a little commons of our own.
🚪 Arrival Info
📍 Shimmerback Ranch · near Willits, California
🚗 Approximately 2.5 hours north of San Francisco
Exact directions, arrival instructions, transportation coordination, campsite information, lodging assignments, and a packing guide will be sent to confirmed attendees before the retreat.
Because this is an offsite retreat rather than an event at our usual San Francisco home, please RSVP rather than simply showing up.
We’ll also coordinate carpools and transportation as the group comes together.
🌲 Come for the woods. Bring something to share. Help us build the village for a weekend.

events.title: GearBox Gallery presents, FUTURE VISION with Caleb Dowdell & TaVee McAllister Lee
events.location: Gearbox Gallery, 770 West Grand Avenue, Oakland
events.description: Future Vision brings together the work of Caleb Dowdell and TaVee McAllister Lee, two artists looking at the forces that shape the world we imagine and the world we create. Opening reception, Saturday, September 26th, 2-5pm, with Caleb Dowdell performance at 4:30pm Caleb Dowdell’s Our Prism of Dreams is a kinetic, five-sided plexiglass prism featuring hand-painted portraits of people whose lives have expanded what others might believe possible appear together as examples of persistence, courage, and possibility. Painted with layers of translucent acrylic, the portraits shift and overlap as the prism moves, suggesting that one person’s accomplishments can become another person’s starting point. TaVee McAllister Lee approaches the future from a different direction. Her floating paper collages are assembled from torn magazine images and fragments of text, bringing together scenes of desire, consumption, achievement, violence, environmental damage, displacement, and everyday life. Images that once belonged to advertising and mass media are removed from their original contexts and placed into new, often uneasy relationships. Together, the works ask us to consider what we carry forward. Lee examines the competing interests and consequences of our collective and individual choices. Dowdell points to inspiration in individuals who light the way toward who we can be and what we can do. Future Vision does not offer a single picture of what lies ahead, instead, it places hope, aspiration, responsibility, and uncertainty alongside one another—and leaves room for us to consider what kind of future we are helping to make.

events.title: What Should Stay Human When Agents Join the Team?
events.location: 540 Laguna St, San Francisco + 540 Cafe
events.description:
Your team works with AI agents now, and nobody has agreed what the agents get to decide. So everyone draws their own line. One person lets the agent send the client email. Another rewrites everything it touches. Someone hides how much they use it. None of it gets said out loud, and slowly the team stops trusting the work, and each other.
This workshop is where a team draws the line together: which calls stay human, which go to the agents, and which the agent drafts and a human decides. What you leave with is a one-page agreement your team wrote, and a monthly practice to keep it current as the work changes.
WHO IT'S FOR: Founders and team leads bringing AI agents into a team, and anyone on a team that already works with them. Heads of HR / People & Culture who want a way to do this across teams.
LEAVE WITH: A one-page team agreement: what stays human, what goes to the agents, what needs a human check. A 45-minute monthly version you can run with your own team.

events.title: The Color of Care: Race and Bias in Modern Medicine
events.location: Alta Vina, 420 3rd St, Oakland, CA 94607, USA
events.description:
🩺 What if a math formula could determine whether you receive life-saving medical care?
For years, hospitals across the United States have quietly used race-based adjustments in medical calculations, influencing everything from kidney transplant eligibility to lung function assessments and childbirth risk. These formulas were built on outdated assumptions about biological differences between races, yet they continue to shape who gets treated, believed, and prioritized in the healthcare system.
In this lecture, Dr. Jennifer Tsai, emergency medicine physician and UC Berkeley public health educator, explores how race-based medical algorithms became embedded in modern healthcare and why many experts are now fighting to remove them.
Through real-world examples, she examines how a single number can delay treatment for Black patients, how bias becomes hidden inside “objective” medical tools, and what happens when we begin questioning the systems behind life-and-death decisions.⚕️

events.title: What Poetry Can Teach Us About Being Human
events.location: The Sycamore, 2140 Mission St, San Francisco, CA 94110, USA
events.description:
📖 What can poems teach us about living through wreckage and wonder?
We spend our lives shuttling between mundane duties and the biggest questions of existence: how to love, how to grieve, how to stay curious in a difficult world. For centuries, poets have turned to verse to sit with those questions rather than rush past them, and in this talk, poet and critic Dean Rader argues that poetry is not a luxury but a way of paying attention to what it means to be alive.
Dean Rader is a San Francisco based poet, essayist, and professor at the University of San Francisco, whose debut collection won the T. S. Eliot Poetry Prize and who later received a Guggenheim Fellowship in Poetry. He is also the creator of the popular web series Poems that Changed Me.
In this talk, Dean will guide us through accessible poems from the 20th and 21st centuries that explore love, death, doubt, belief, regret, and awe. You do not need any background in literature to follow along. He will show how poems can help us live inside hard questions instead of chasing tidy answers, and why the biggest ideas in life often arrive in just a few lines. ✨

events.title: Dread Scott: The Body Politic
events.location: YBCA, 700 Howard St, San Francisco, CA 94103
events.description:
Dread Scott: The Body Politic brings together work that reflects Dread Scott’s longtime commitment to art that confronts political issues and interrogates American patriotism.

On view in the exhibition are two newly commissioned projects, as well as a selection of pre-existing works. Defending the Flag (2026) is a durational performance piece in which a guard dressed in military uniform stands in front of a U.S. flag on a flagpole while holding a military rifle, crystallizing social power dynamics in the form of a charged encounter between the state and the public. The piece will be performed each week on Wednesdays from 4pm–8pm, and Saturdays from 1–5pm.

The second commissioned piece is a monumental work on canvas made up of dozens of layered body prints. Created with the participation of community members, the piece is an immense yet ethereal representation of civil society. These new pieces will be complemented by existing works, including a large-scale screenprint Imagine a World Without America (Green Land) (2025), a series of modified photographs of governmental seats of power, and a selection of pre-existing body prints.

The exhibition draws on the urgency of the present moment, inviting viewers to consider their own positions within the systems his work lays bare.

Dread Scott: The Body Politic is curated by René Morales.
sources: Yerba Buena Center for the Arts

events.title: Rael San Fratello: Prototypes and Provocations
events.location: YBCA, 700 Howard St, San Francisco, CA 94103
events.description:
Prototypes and Provocations is the most comprehensive presentation to date of the award-winning work of Oakland-based architecture and design studio Rael San Fratello.

Founded by Virginia San Fratello and Ronald Rael in 2002, this mid-career survey traces Rael San Fratello’s evolution from their early experiments merging clothing and construction, to a series of bold projects centered on the U.S.-Mexico border, to their trailblazing work fusing 3D printing with traditional earthen materials. Among them is the studio’s acclaimed 2019 project Teeter-Totter Wall , a set of bright pink seesaws installed along the infamous border wall. Inviting playful, transnational exchange, the work garnered widespread attention as a powerful symbol of the possibility for connection across a deeply contested divide.

One of the centerpieces of the exhibition is a new, large-scale commission titled Sanctuary . 3D printed entirely onsite using only soil, straw, and water, the cylindrical structure offers visitors a quiet space for reflection, while serving as a demonstration of the ecologically-sound building techniques that Rael San Fratello have developed. Alongside this work, a massive table will display a selection of 3D printed objects made from a wide array of materials either sustainable, upcycled, or rescued from the waste stream (including salt, chardonnay grape skins, salt, coffee grounds, clay, sawdust, and ash collected in the aftermath of California wildfires).

The work of Rael San Fratello insists that architecture is not merely a backdrop for social life, but a medium through which power is both articulated and contested. By the same token, the studio challenges the discipline to imagine more equitable, adaptive, and humane ways of inhabiting the world.

Rael San Fratello: Prototypes and Provocations is curated by René Morales.
sources: Yerba Buena Center for the Arts

events.description: King Lear by William Shakespeare Directed by Michael Socrates Moran Music composed by Paul Dresher Presented by Oakland Theater Project & New Performance Traditions In the twilight of his rule, a king sets out to divide the kingdom among his three daughters. But in mistaking flattery for love, Lear’s foolish choices usher in a new reign of domination, cruelty and collapse. As a self-styled “bastard” sets out to upend the ruling order, Lear must confront his own part in the kingdom’s downfall. Can he transform in time to reclaim what is sacred before the clown show becomes the new order? Ritual and spectacle collide in Michael Socrates Moran ’s bold, contemporary staging of Shakespeare’s epic tragedy, featuring a cast of 30, including the “irrepressible” ( SF Chronicle ) J Jha ( Angels in America, Mahābhārata ) as Lear; renowned performer, singer, and writer Rinde Eckert ( Ghost Quartet ) as The Fool; and music composed by Paul Dresher and performed live by the Dresher | Davel Invented Instrument Duo .

events.description: Pianist and composer Jahari Stampley has emerged as one of the most electrifying young artists in modern jazz, blending breathtaking virtuosity with deep emotional expression and fearless stylistic range. Raised in Chicago in a profoundly musical family, Stampley developed his artistry through gospel, jazz, classical music, and Black creative traditions, building a voice that feels both rooted and radically contemporary. His international breakthrough came after winning the prestigious Herbie Hancock Institute of Jazz International Piano Competition, where his dazzling technique, originality, and compositional brilliance announced the arrival of a major new talent. Beyond his acclaim as a pianist, Stampley has become known for adventurous collaborations spanning jazz, hip-hop, R&B, and experimental music, working with Stanley Clarke, Derrick Hodge, Keyon Harrold, and others. He’s released a pair of albums including 2025’s What A Time . With the Family Soul Trio, featuring his mother, GRAMMY-nominated multi-instrumentalist D-Erania Stampley , and drummer Miguel Russell , Jahari brings his music into an intimate and deeply personal space. The ensemble channels family legacy, spiritual connection, and rhythmic vitality into performances that move fluidly between jazz, soul, gospel, and improvisation. Together, they create music that feels celebratory, searching, and profoundly human, highlighting the communal spirit at the heart of Black American music.

events.description: Mollusk presents: DOLPHIN MARKET This is Issue 2 of Memory: "Dolphin Market" and it features Kevin Dickson from Seal Beach; people like to call him the best surfer you've never heard of haha. He's super low key and rips on anything. For the music I got Brian, of Monde UFO, into my studio last summer and filmed him playing an improv noise set consisting of stand up bass and saxophone. And we have our buddy Jeff (Dismal) reading poetry at moments throughout the film. These 3 together in this film capture something special creatively and I'm really excited to share it with the public. The entire film was shot on minidv, vhsc, and hi8 over the past year and a half. Dolphin Market is an old market in Seal Beach that has been closed for as long as we all can remember and Kev lives right next door to it, so that being the title of the film only made sense. with opening live music from April Magazine April Magazine combines the talents of a handful of Bay Area indie pop notables into a collective that releases fragile and noisy songs that land right in the sweet spot between Velvet Underground hum and Pastels warble with a heavy dose of slowcore static in the mix. A string of digital singles primed listeners for the group's sound; late 2021 brought both a collection of said releases -- If the Ceiling Were a Kite, Vol. 1 -- and their first LP, Sunday Music for an Overpass. Bandcamp Monde UFO Monde UFO is Ray Monde and Kris Chau. We are sometimes graced with the presence of our Drummer Joe Lyle. Ray Monde concepted Monde UFO as a way to synthesize his foundations in Jazz and Punk. In a warehouse on Skid Row while playing in other projects, he started creating what would become the first Monde UFO album 7171. He used the influence of Bossa Nova for the vocal stylings and experimental Sound Healing as a guide to navigate through the saturated Music Industry. Kris Chau is a visual Artist with no formal musical training. Ray decided adding a newcomer to music would allow Monde UFO to channel a fresh energy into the music and performance. Kris Chau looks to other Art Rock Luminaries such as Brian Eno and Yoko Ono for her guidance. For the live performance she utilizes Qi Gong, sound healing, and folk dances inspired by Shamans and Shrine Maidens. Joe Lyle is an generational talent. When he doesn’t bless us with his presence he is playing with Chris Cohen, Cass McCombs, Mac Demarco, and has played with Solange as well as many incredible talents of the Music industry. If you see him tell him how much you liked his drumming in Monde UFO. Please. Bandcamp | IG DOORS at 7:00 PM | MUSIC at 7:30 PM | FILM at 9:30 PM Tickets

The ensemble channels family legacy, spiritual connection, and rhythmic vitality into performances that move fluidly between jazz, soul, gospel, and improvisation. Together, they create music that feels celebratory, searching, and profoundly human, highlighting the communal spirit at the heart of Black American music.

events.title: In Color
events.location: The Independent, 628 Divisadero St, San Francisco, CA 94117
events.description:
In and of itself, chemistry may be quiet, but you see, hear, and feel its impact. Such close chemistry drives the interplay of In Color. The Nashville band—Holden Clontz, Matthew Hastings, Val Hoyt, and Miles Laderman—lean on a silent bond sealed by years of friendship and a collective passion for pushing boundaries. They bring dimension to alternative pop, threading unshakable melodies through multi-layered soundscapes.

After buzzing with millions of streams independently, the group simply transfix and invigorate on their 2025 debut EP, Snow Day [Big Loud Rock].

“To us, there’s definitely an unspoken vision for what In Color is,” observes Holden. “We don’t talk about it a lot. It comes from being friends for so long and listening to the same music. We’re all different in our own ways, but it works so well.”

“It’s a special thing, because we trust each other’s instincts,” agrees Val. “We enjoy writing together. So, we’re able to authentically create and put out music that feels like we’re putting ourselves on the line.”

Though the members’ paths had crossed over the years, you can trace the band’s genesis back to a particularly brutal snowstorm in early 2024. Val and Miles first met at an Atlanta middle school, attended the same high school, made their way to Belmont University, and lived together for a handful of years in Nashville. Holden had moved to Music City at 19-years-old and linked up with Matt through his roommate, hitting it off and “becoming best friends.” By way of this friend group, Matt eventually moved in with Val. Not to mention, the guys had separately played in various bands or released solo music.

However, it took a blizzard to unlock the potential among them.

“The four of us were hanging out every day,” says Matt. “Val and I lived together. Once the snow started, everybody just decided to stay over at our place. Musically, we had been doing different things, but getting snowed in was the catalyst we needed. A few days later, Val sent everyone a text, and it was a picture of all of us. He was like, ‘We would look really cool as a band’. That’s all it took!”

“We all secretly wanted to be a part of something bigger,” notes Holden. “We had lived life as friends, so why not do this?”

For the next year, the band operated “in private,” as they like to say. Under the radar, the guys got together, jammed, wrote songs, and tightened up a collective approach. They drew on inspirations as diverse as Coldplay, Kings of Leon, Switchfoot, The Beatles, U2, and Michael Jackson, cultivating a signature style. With the sound dialed in, the group started to record.

“When you listen to the music, it’s multi-faceted,” says Miles. “We don’t abide by any confines of genre. We look and feel like a ‘rock band’, but it’s not traditional.”

Powered by this perspective, In Color instantly resonated by threading timeless pop songcraft into an airy ever-evolving sonic fabric. Released on Valentine’s Day 2025, their debut “Headlights” surpassed 4.5 million Spotify streams followed by standouts such as “Liar” and “Is There Anyone?”

Elsewhere, “Time” rides out of the gate on a steady beat, warm bassline, and delicate vocals. Keys glimmer, and a palm-muted riff boosts the refrain, “Over again, the sun is turning around. I won’t pretend that I don’t need you now. I’d fall in love with you forever, oh we don’t have enough time.”

“We were thinking of seasons, and it aligns with the leaves changing colors and a new start,” adds Miles. “It fit this mindset.”

The EP single “I Want You” strikes a balance between a bouncy hip-hop-esque cadence and nineties alternative ambition. Simultaneously, it delivers a straightforward, albeit impactful message.

“It’s a simple love song that truly encapsulates the feeling of wanting someone,” notes Holden. “It was a great way to close out this introductory chapter.”

Ultimately, In Color pull a vibrant sound from their union as collaborators and friends. It’s natural, and that’s why it resonates.

“We had all been around the music industry for years, and when we chose to start this, it was like we were unlearning everything before,” smiles Matt. “We found our people, and everything made sense.”

“Having each other has allowed us to be the best individual versions of ourselves,” concludes Miles. “You’re constantly thinking, ‘How can I show up for the guys in this moment?’ All I need to do is be myself so I can be part of this with the guys and build it up. That’s what we’re doing.”

events.title: Being Here: Weekly Silent Sitting & Dharma Talk with Milo
events.location: 540 Laguna St, San Francisco + 540 Cafe
events.description:
Being Here is a weekly gathering guided by Dharma Teacher Milo Burn, who has led multiple three-month silent retreats and teaches from a background grounded in Zen and Theravada practice. The gathering is to celebrate silence and stillness, study, practice and realize Buddhist teachings, and dynamic inquiry into mindfulness, freedom, and compassion in daily life.
So much of our lives are oriented toward becoming. Being Here offers a regular space to pause that momentum and explore what becomes possible when we give our attention to simply being here. Through meditation, heart teachings, and conversation, we practice bringing this quality of being into the rest of our lives.
The emphasis is on direct experience rather than technique. Think: less following a recipe and more hanging out in your grandma’s kitchen! Come to practice, listen, ask questions, or spend time in a space devoted to being.
For more about Milo, including extended biography, upcoming retreats, and in depth 1-1 guidance visit www.boundlessness.org
🕰 Schedule
10:30 AM: Arrive and settle in
Brief sitting instruction
35 minutes: Silent sitting meditation
35 minutes: Dharma teachings from Milo, followed by question and response
10 minutes: Closing and announcements
Stay afterward for informal conversation and connection, if you like
💫 Who This Is For
Open to Commons members and the wider community
People curious about meditation, Dharma, Buddhist teachings, mindfulness, or nonduality
Those beginning a practice and those with years of experience
Anyone looking for a place to deepen their practice in community
Anyone drawn to exploring how meditation and Dharma meet ordinary daily life
🤲 Participation Norms
RSVP on Luma or drop in
No formal membership or prior experience required
Questions, reflections, and inquiry are encouraged
🎒 What to Bring
Bring a zafu if you prefer this to the provided chairs and pillows
💛 Suggested Donation / Exchange
Being Here is offered on a dana basis, as an expression of generosity and shared responsibility. Contribute according to your means and inspiration.
🏛 The Commons
Being Here creates a weekly place at The Commons to practice being alongside becoming. It is part of the larger rhythm of rituals, relationships, and creative life that make The Commons a civic hearth for personal becoming and creative actualization in San Francisco. Membership sustains the space and makes this ongoing community life possible. If you feel drawn to being part of that rhythm, we welcome you to explore membership, with no pressure. Learn more or join us at thesfcommons.com or ask at the front desk.
🚪 Arrival Info
Please arrive by 10:30 AM so you have time to settle in before the sitting begins.

events.title: Artist’s Reception – William Rhodes: Fear Not
events.location: Transmission Gallery, 770 West Grand Ave., Suite A, Oakland
events.description: William Rhodes: Fear Not September 17 – October 31, 2026 Artist’s Reception: Saturday, September 26th from 1-4 pm All are welcome! Please join us for the Artist’s Reception for William Rhodes’ solo exhibition, Fear Not, in conjunction with the reception for concurrent exhibition, Ellen Bepp: The Ghosts We Carry. Greet the artists, check out the exhibitions and enjoy the light refreshments and lively conversations. Look for the “ART” Building at 770 West Grand Ave and come upstairs to Transmission Gallery for this event. Free street parking on West Grand Ave and in the neighborhood south of West Grand. More about Fear Not: William Rhodes’s sculptures on view incorporate objects that have been used, inherited, discarded, or found with elements he has carved himself. Trained early on as a furniture maker, he combines hand carved figures, flames and snakes with objects collected from a family home, photographs, hardware, tools, and other remnants of everyday life. Neon words signal from some pieces. The resulting works resemble shrines or memorials, but they remain grounded in the ordinary. Religious symbols appear alongside household objects. A photograph might be surrounded by carved waves, tools, hardware, animals, or religious symbols. A suitcase can become an architectural space. A toilet becomes the base of an unexpected monument. Things with little apparent value are carefully incorporated into elaborate constructions, their histories becoming part of the work. ​ Rhodes is equally interested in people; family, mentors, and leaders, as well as those who have been overlooked or treated as disposable, recognizing and elevating their presence in his work. By giving attention to these lives, enshrining and revering them, he considers how value is assigned and who gets remembered. The title Fear Not appears in the work as both a phrase and a kind of instruction. It can be read in relation to the religious imagery that runs throughout the sculptures, but it also takes on a morepersonal meaning. To look closely at lives and objects that are easily dismissed is, in its own way, an act of resistance to that dismissal.

events.title: Jahari Stampley Family Soul Trio
events.location: SFJAZZ Center, 201 Franklin St, San Francisco, CA 94102 — Joe Henderson Lab
events.description: Pianist and composer Jahari Stampley has emerged as one of the most electrifying young artists in modern jazz, blending breathtaking virtuosity with deep emotional expression and fearless stylistic range. Raised in Chicago in a profoundly musical family, Stampley developed his artistry through gospel, jazz, classical music, and Black creative traditions, building a voice that feels both rooted and radically contemporary. His international breakthrough came after winning the prestigious Herbie Hancock Institute of Jazz International Piano Competition, where his dazzling technique, originality, and compositional brilliance announced the arrival of a major new talent. Beyond his acclaim as a pianist, Stampley has become known for adventurous collaborations spanning jazz, hip-hop, R&B, and experimental music, working with Stanley Clarke, Derrick Hodge, Keyon Harrold, and others. He’s released a pair of albums including 2025’s What A Time . With the Family Soul Trio, featuring his mother, GRAMMY-nominated multi-instrumentalist D-Erania Stampley , and drummer Miguel Russell , Jahari brings his music into an intimate and deeply personal space. The ensemble channels family legacy, spiritual connection, and rhythmic vitality into performances that move fluidly between jazz, soul, gospel, and improvisation. Together, they create music that feels celebratory, searching, and profoundly human, highlighting the communal spirit at the heart of Black American music.

events.description: King Lear by William Shakespeare Directed by Michael Socrates Moran Music composed by Paul Dresher Presented by Oakland Theater Project & New Performance Traditions In the twilight of his rule, a king sets out to divide the kingdom among his three daughters. But in mistaking flattery for love, Lear’s foolish choices usher in a new reign of domination, cruelty and collapse. As a self-styled “bastard” sets out to upend the ruling order, Lear must confront his own part in the kingdom’s downfall. Can he transform in time to reclaim what is sacred before the clown show becomes the new order? Ritual and spectacle collide in Michael Socrates Moran ’s bold, contemporary staging of Shakespeare’s epic tragedy, featuring a cast of 30, including the “irrepressible” ( SF Chronicle ) J Jha ( Angels in America, Mahābhārata ) as Lear; renowned performer, singer, and writer Rinde Eckert ( Ghost Quartet ) as The Fool; and music composed by Paul Dresher and performed live by the Dresher | Davel Invented Instrument Duo .

events.title: Devin Gray Quartet
events.location: Bird & Beckett Books & Records, 653 Chenery Street, San Francisco
events.description: Darren Johnston, trumpet; Liberty Ellman, guitar; Lisa Mezzacappa, bass; Devin Gray, drums/compositions The Devin Gray Quartet is an ensemble of forward-thinking improvisers operating at the intersection of modern jazz, contemporary composition, and fluid, exploratory group dynamics. The quartet brings together four distinct voices from the contemporary jazz vanguard. Together, the quartet delivers a captivating blend of intricate polyrhythms, rich harmonic interplay, and spontaneous collective dialogue—delivering music that is as intellectually engaging as it is emotionally vibrant. New York-based guitarist Liberty Ellman is well known since his quarter century collaboration, since 2001, in Henry Threadgill’s ensemble Zooid, and makes a rare San Francisco appearance. Trumpeter Darren Johnston and bassist Lisa Mezzacappa are among the top musicians in the Bay Area avant garde/improvised music ecosystem. Berlin/NYC-based, Devin is a drummer driven by velocity, imagination and an unshakeable commitment to the unknown. Rooted in jazz but propelled by an expansive curiosity, Gray moves fluidly between forward-leaning composition, high-intensity improvisation, and genre-agnostic experimentation; establishing himself as a vital and unpredictable presence in contemporary creative music. His work with artists such as Kris Davis, Luke Stewart, Gerald Cleaver, Ellery Eskelin, Michael Formanek, Dave Liebman, and Ralph Alessi ranges from precision-built ensembles to volatile, moment-to-moment collaborations highlighted by a drummer who treats the kit as both engine and instrument of color and microscopic detail. What ultimately sets Gray apart is not just his formidable technique or restless versatility, but a compositional mind with a bandleader’s vision giving each musical situation its own internal logic. With Gray behind the drums, expectation is irrelevant-the only certainty is forward motion. Gray’s discography as a leader showcases his versatility and commitment to pushing musical‬‭ boundaries. His debut album, “Dirigo Rataplan” (2012), featured notable artists Ellery Eskelin,‬ ‭Dave Ballou, and Michael Formanek, and was praised for its complex and intimate compositions.‬‭ He continued this trajectory with “RelativE ResonancE” (2015), collaborating with Chris Speed,‬‭ Kris Davis, and Chris Tordini, further establishing his reputation as a forward-thinking composer.‬ ‭In 2021, Gray released “Melt All the Guns” a politically charged trio album featuring trumpeter‬‭ Ralph Alessi and pianist Angelica Sanchez, addressing the pressing issue of gun violence in the‬ United States. The following year, he presented “27 Licks,” a duet with fellow drummer Gerald‬‭ Cleaver, highlighting his adventurous spirit and deep musical rapport.‬‭ In 2023 Gray released “Most Definitely” as his first solo drum recording showcases his innovative‬‭ approach to percussion, blending acoustic drumming with electronic elements to create a dynamic‬‭ and immersive listening experience.‬‭ The album’s strength lies in its eloquent orchestration of blended electronics balanced‬‭ with Gray’s high-level improvisational performances pushing‬‭ the boundaries of percussion and improvisation.‬ ‭Gray’s most recent project, “Melt All the Guns II” (2024), continues his exploration of socially‬‭ conscious themes, this time featuring Ralph Alessi and French pianist Myslaure Augustin. The‬‭ album comprises tracks like “East Berlin 2024” and “Audre Lorde Straße, “reflecting his‬‭ engagement with contemporary issues and global perspectives.‬ ‭Throughout his career, Gray has maintained a dynamic presence in the international jazz scene,‬ performing at venues and festivals worldwide including Jazzfest Berlin 2024. His collaborations span a wide range of artists,‬‭ including Sylvie Courvoisier, Tim Berne, Michael Formanek, Zoh Amba, and Micah Thomas, among‬‭ others. events.title: LIVE MUSIC: Mildred, Charlie Bishop (Presented by THROWIN' BO'S)
events.location: 4-Star Theater, 2200 Clement St, San Francisco, CA 94121
events.description: Throwin’ Bo’s presents: Mildred Mildred is a band from Oakland, CA of four equal parts. They don’t have a lead singer, no one person writes the songs. The songs that make up Fenceline come together as a group with their genesis sprouting from any one of their members - Henry Easton Koehler (vocals, guitar), Jack Schrott (vocals, guitar), Matt Palmquist (vocals, bass, woodwinds) or Will Fortna (drums, production) - each time. The songs are often wrestled from the lead writer by the other three, a lyric might have been mumbled absentmindedly for a few days before one of the other three grabs at it. If you ask any Mildred member what their favourite part of Fenceline is, it will never be something they wrote. If you pin them down and ask them what their favourite part of something they did write was, it will always be something somebody else added to it. This is what makes Mildred - in many ways a timeless four piece - so special. This wonderfully easy bond between four friends just hanging out and writing songs is so palpable its intoxicating. Summed up neatly by Clash Magazine saying, “imagine if Pavement went Americana and you’d be close”, Mildred make music that is pure and poetic, gently addictive and never overwrought. They describe the creation of the band as being born from “deciding that playing/talking about/thinking about music together is fun and something we want to structure our lives around as best we can”. Mildred is a vehicle for these four people to continue to spend time in each other’s company. Most bands are formed so they can get out of whatever diy space they start out playing in, Mildred was formed so they can spend more time there. The space in question for Mildred is a house. The Ward St. house in Berkeley to be exact, already a landmark in Mildred lore. When Fenceline began taking shape Henry, Jack, Matt, and occasionally Will were living there together; Matt hunkered in an “extra-legal” room in the attic where he bathed on his knees and Henry and Will would have to stoop to visit. Jack and Henry shared a wall in adjacent shoeboxes on the middle floor, Henry staring directly out at an old walnut tree they nicknamed Walter. Will was away studying in the desert but would stay whenever he was in town. While living on Ward St. they would write songs in the porous space between the kitchen and the living room after dinner, before they even knew they were a band. After that they would go up to the roof - beautifully painted by Jack for the cover of Fenceline -, Jones the cat often creeping up the stairs curiously behind, and talk the songs over some more, or just continue hanging out, talking about whatever. (The Mildred core belief system goes as follows: “talking about the weather is a legitimate and profound form of human discourse and exchange. So is talking about grocery stores and produce prices. Front lawns are too tidy, let them grow. Free associating is one of life's great pleasures. We believe in the reality of pathetic fallacy. The crunch wrap supreme is the pinnacle of modernity.”). This is what makes the songs on Fenceline hang together, naturally, as roommates do. These four people are very different in many ways. Jack is a PHD student, often working underground, studying the atom beyond any conceivable point. Will is an environmental lawyer. Matt is an architect, a job he took up properly after a year in a Benedictine monastery. Henry works in affordable housing, helps his dad grow beans, and plays a lot of basketball. The lyrics for their songs are written largely alone and often draw from their own individual lives and experiences but there’s a shared something there. “It makes sense when common threads emerge” they say, “because we do things together a lot as friends: cook, laze about on a weekend, listen to an album, go walkabout, read, go see movies etc. People will tell us after seeing us live that we’re, “like... a real band.” There’s maybe a shared rhythm and camaraderie in our lives that comes through in the music.” That shared something takes many forms: flaming pinecones floating down the river, scattered papers and dog-eared books, exhausting party conversation and Irish goodbyes, leaves the colour of UPS trucks. Songs often take place across whole days: long days working at Henry’s aunt and uncle’s farm, an afternoon down in San Francisco on the day the sailors come in and booze all day in their cracker-jack uniforms, one of those youthful afternoons that seemed to stretch forever. Others stem from a shared love of a good reference; breadcrumbs dropped from old favourite books, songs and poems, or Matt’s favourite little red book on architecture, waiting to be found by those who love to go over lyrics with a fine-toothed comb. Strikingly literal or intriguingly oblique, Mildred have a remarkable way with lyrics that lodge themselves in your head softly but with such determination that they begin to feel like shimmering memories from your own life. Fenceline is a collection of songs that you want to hold close and delve into, and yet play to everyone you know. Mildred were eventually turfed out of Ward St. and the songs were fleshed out in Matt’s new abode - the garage of a handsome but fragile 97-year-old ex-lawyer/taxi driver who likes to chat about baseball - and for recording, the band took a week off work and decamped to Luke Temple’s studio in Echo Park, LA, having all been carried through the pandemic by his 2019 album Both-And. There was one exception to this recording setup. While in Bristol with a free afternoon, Mildred took ‘Fish Sticks’ to a friend, Jack Ogborne aka Bingo Fury (The Cindys, Naima Bock), to give it another go in his studio in the basement of a centuries-old pub across the street from what used to be a prison, with a secret passageway connecting the two. It’s not easy to tell that ‘Fish Sticks’ has a very different recording setup as it settles so comfortably in with the rest of Fenceline; but the change of scenery gave it new life and a final product - an endlessly repayable distillation of the Mildred sound with a central guitar line for the ages and irresistible harmonies - that they all liked so much it became the lead single. A bit of tinkering, overdubs and a beautifully cohesive final mix from Will followed by mastering from GRAMMY nominee Jason Mitchell, and Fenceline was finished. events.description:
Having already placed his indelible mark on the future direction of rock with Hüsker Dü, Bob Mould teamed with bassist David Barbe and drummer Malcolm Travis to found Sugar in late 1991, making their live debut early the next year at Athens, GA’s famed 40 Watt Club. Named by NME as its 1992 “Album of the Year,” Sugar’s now-classic debut album, Copper Blue, immediately proved a sensation, earning worldwide acclaim and landmark status for the melodic strength and intensely cathartic popcraft of songs like “A Good Idea,” “Helpless,” and the alternative rock radio hit and MTV favorite, “If I Can’t Change Your Mind.” The trio quickly found themselves performing on increasingly larger stages, including a legendary show-stealing set at London’s Great X-pectations Festival in Finsbury Park.

With the wind at their back, Sugar unleashed Beaster in 1993, making a momentous debut at #3 on the UK’s Official Albums Chart as well as at #4 on Billboard ’s “Heatseekers” chart in the US. Though recorded during the same sessions that yielded Copper Blue , the six-song mini-album evinced a more visceral energy and dark melancholy than its predecessor, highlighted by such pulverizing expressions of sacrilegious fury as “Judas Cradle” and “JC Auto.” 1994’s second full-length LP, File Under: Easy Listening once again made an explosive arrival among the top 10 on the UK Official Albums Chart, this time landing in the upper reaches of the overall Billboard 200. The album saw Sugar pushing boundaries yet again on songs like the country-flavored “Believe What You’re Saying” and the incendiary “Gee Angel,” tackling a wider range of musical approaches without sacrificing their signature intensity and unrestrained power. Despite their successes, Sugar called it a day following a Japanese tour in early 1995. A series of live recordings, reissues, and anthologies served to magnify the band’s legacy over the three decades since, confirming Sugar as incontrovertible masters of high-volume guitar-fueled rock for the ages.

events.title: Jahari Stampley Family Soul Trio
events.location: SFJAZZ Center, 201 Franklin St, San Francisco, CA 94102 — Joe Henderson Lab
events.description: Pianist and composer Jahari Stampley has emerged as one of the most electrifying young artists in modern jazz, blending breathtaking virtuosity with deep emotional expression and fearless stylistic range. Raised in Chicago in a profoundly musical family, Stampley developed his artistry through gospel, jazz, classical music, and Black creative traditions, building a voice that feels both rooted and radically contemporary. His international breakthrough came after winning the prestigious Herbie Hancock Institute of Jazz International Piano Competition, where his dazzling technique, originality, and compositional brilliance announced the arrival of a major new talent. Beyond his acclaim as a pianist, Stampley has become known for adventurous collaborations spanning jazz, hip-hop, R&B, and experimental music, working with Stanley Clarke, Derrick Hodge, Keyon Harrold, and others. He’s released a pair of albums including 2025’s What A Time . With the Family Soul Trio, featuring his mother, GRAMMY-nominated multi-instrumentalist D-Erania Stampley , and drummer Miguel Russell , Jahari brings his music into an intimate and deeply personal space. The ensemble channels family legacy, spiritual connection, and rhythmic vitality into performances that move fluidly between jazz, soul, gospel, and improvisation. Together, they create music that feels celebratory, searching, and profoundly human, highlighting the communal spirit at the heart of Black American music.

events.description:
🎉 Public Hours at the Commons 🎉
Every Sunday, the Commons opens to the public — no membership required. Come co-work, connect, create, or just explore the space at your own pace. ✨
🕘 When: Every Sunday, 9 AM – 10 PM
📍 Where: 540 Laguna St, San Francisco (corner of Hayes & Laguna, basement level)
RSVP and we'll email you your entry code ahead of time — so you can let yourself straight in when you arrive.
──────────────────────────────
🧭 A self-guided day
Public Hours are self-guided — come in, settle in, and make the space your own. Weekends are usually unstaffed, so there's no check-in desk or guided tour. Our members are glad to answer questions about the space; for anything else — including guided tours, which we don't offer as drop-ins — email hello@thesfcommons.com ahead of time.
──────────────────────────────
🔭 Getting in
Your entry code comes by email. Once you RSVP, we'll send you a personal QR code — that's your key for the day. Keep it handy on your phone (and check spam if you don't see it).
Find us. We're at 540 Laguna St, on the corner of Hayes & Laguna. Head down the stairs beside Earthbody to the basement level — that's the Commons.
Scan your QR code at the reader to unlock the door. Hold your phone just below the Kisi reader by the door and it'll let you in.
Your access stays active all day, 9 AM – 10 PM, so you can come and go freely.
Can't find your code on the day? No problem — scan the QR posted on the door to check in and get a fresh one on the spot.
We're shoes-off 🧦 — please clean up after yourself, including dirty dishes and mugs, and use only the front entrance. Trouble getting in? Email hello@thesfcommons.com.




The Commons is a modern-day town square for communal meaning-making, personal discovery, and self-expression in the heart of San Francisco. Apply to become a member here__.

events.title: LIVE MUSIC: Fog Lamp, Eraser, Blue Zero (Presented by TALENT MOAT)
events.location: 4-Star Theater, 2200 Clement St, San Francisco, CA 94121
events.description: Talent Moat presents: Fog Lamp Fog Lamp sound like Killing Joke and Big Black got together to record a soundtrack for a John Carpenter movie. Bandcamp | IG Eraser Philadelphia’s No-Wavers Eraser erupted onto the East Coast punk scene like a shattering disco ball. The group’s members Sonam, Kat, Juliette and Pier united in 2023 through their love of DIY music and their overlapping experiences in the Philly scene playing in former and con-current bands Drill, Amanda X, Corey Flood, and Privacy Issues. Since forming, Eraser has built a unique sound informed by legendary punk bands like The Slits, Malaria, and Liquid Liquid- as well as by their palpable sense of humor, and their raw, experimentally elastic approach to songwriting. Eraser have continued to grow their following by contributing a single on the comp No Occupation, and by releasing their debut EP Hideout with art rock stalwarts Siltbreeze Records. With their debut LP, Hideout, Eraser has established a diverse palette using angular fuzz-guitar, tunneling basslines, motorik drums, discordant synth, and melodic, percussive vocals. The EP is made up of 5 diverse, yet cohesive tracks. The release starts with a suspenseful intro and quickly breaks into “Talk To Me”- which features a linear jam with hyper-infectious hooks accented by cool near-blasé vocals. Other standouts include “Simon Says” with its hilariously damaged homage to the childhood game, and Dinner Roll with its piercing synth line and wonky guitar riffage. In the past year Eraser has provided direct support for Special Interest, Protomartyr, Tropical Fuck Storm, Tommy Wright the III, Pylon, W.I.T.C.H, Wombo, Famous Mammals, Poison Ruin and Puppet Wipes. Eraser also played two music festivals in 2025: Sled Island in Calgary and Gonerfest in Memphis, TN. Eraser will be releasing their second full-length album in September 2026 on Siltbreeze. Bandcamp | IG Blue Zero The Bay Area has long been a fertile landscape for arty DIY rock innovators to fashion together some of the best music to come out of the US- the local musicians pushing the boundaries of pop and counterculture aesthetics. In the middle of this creative oasis you’ll find multi-instrumentalist songwriter Chris Natividad making iridescent waves with his many projects including Marbled Eye, Public Interest, Aluminum, and now- Blue Zero. What started as a few outlier demos cultivated in Chris’ studio has now fully bloomed into a live band featuring members Lauren Melton of SUCKER and Rick Altieri of Blue Ocean, and a forthcoming LP titled Colder Shade Blue. The songs on the record harmoniously tow the line of warm and meditative artrock and fuzzy, damaged grunge a là Lily’s, Sonic Youth, and My Bloody Valentine. While Blue Zero pays homage to their predecessors, the music is wholly unique with its mesmerizing big hooks and blown-out radiating psychedelic atmosphere- a tonal yin yang. events.title: From Pain to Resource: Embodied Awareness, Posture & Movement
events.location: 550 Laguna St, San Francisco + Full Studio
events.description:
Join me for a gentle exploration of the body, guided by functional anatomy and embodied awareness.
I’ll share some of my own journey from experiencing my body as pain to discovering it as a reliable resource for grounding, rest, and guidance.
My work is rooted in the Alexander Technique and has evolved through ten years of self-practice and teaching, meditation, and emotional healing. Over the past two years, brain retraining for mold sensitivity and energy practices have further broadened my understanding and informed my approach.
Through experiential practices, we’ll explore how subtle holding patterns we may not notice can shape our posture and contribute to pain, and what can happen when we make contact with what is already there rather than trying to change it.
Depending on time and interest, I may demonstrate hands-on guidance with a volunteer. I’m also happy to offer brief hands-on guidance to anyone who would like to experience it, during the workshop or afterwards.
About Me
You can learn more about me and my work at witholivialin.com.

events.title: Builders Night
events.location: 540 Laguna St, San Francisco + 540 Cafe
events.description:
Builders Night is a weekly space where people show up with a project, work side by side, and leave with more momentum than they could have generated alone. It exists because building can be lonely, and the hardest part is often simply showing up consistently.
The tone is focused and warm. Mostly quiet during deep work, with moments of spontaneous connection when someone gets unstuck or discovers something worth sharing. This is not a networking event or a lecture. The work itself is the center of the night.
Flow
6:30–6:45 PM: Arrival and settling in
6:45–6:55 PM: Opening circle: name, what you're working on, one intention for the night
6:55–8:30 PM: Deep work sprint: quiet, side-by-side building
8:30–9:00 PM: Share-back: what you built, learned, or got stuck on. Make an ask, offer what you know, and support each other.
Who This Is For
People working on software, hardware, businesses, creative projects, writing, design, research, art, anything you're trying to make real. Come if you want accountability, momentum, and the energy of working alongside others. First-timers and regulars both welcome.
What to Bring
Laptop, notebook, sketchbook, instrument, whatever tools your project requires. Come with something to work on, or come ready to figure out what that is.
Norms
Respect the deep work sprint by keeping conversation low during focused time. Share-back is how we learn from each other: share what you built, ask for what you need, and offer what you can. Everyone participates.
Rally (rallysf.com) is an AI builder community in SF.

events.title: Let's Talk About Social Anxiety
events.location: 540 Laguna St, San Francisco + 540 Cafe
events.description:
Hey, I'm Chelsea. I was diagnosed with depression and anxiety at 28 years old. I always struggled with meaningful connection and often shut down in social situations.
What I learned through finding support is that I don't have to feel this way and I can't do it alone.
In this interactive gathering, we'll have the space to explore what social anxiety feels like and how we can build tools to overcome it together.
While healing is a continuous journey and I am far from done, I have spent the last 10 years building spaces and collecting the tools that I wish I had when I was younger. Through that process, I obtained my Masters in Mental Health Counseling and have used that training to grow the You Aren't Alone Project, a nonprofit organization dedicated to facilitating & changing conversations around mental health for the safety and belonging of all.
The project started in Louisiana and I am excited to bring our programs to San Francisco and beyond.
I hope you'll join me for the first in our "Let's Talk About It" series on Sept. 29th. Location to be announced soon!

events.title: Sex, AI and the Future of Human Intimacy
events.location: Era Lounge, 386 S 1st St, San Jose, CA 95113, USA
events.description:
💘 What does authentic intimacy look like when AI can love you back?
Artificial intelligence is quietly reshaping who and how we love. AI companions, humanoid robots, and immersive sex tech are no longer science fiction premises, they are products people are using right now to seek connection, comfort, and desire.
Kaamna Bhojwani, a certified sexologist and researcher whose work spans psychology, sexuality, technology, and spirituality, studies what she calls the Intimacy Economy, a new landscape where trust and emotional connection are increasingly mediated by intelligent machines. She writes the Becoming Technosexual column for Psychology Today and hosts the Sex, Tech and Spirituality podcast.
In this provocative talk, Kaamna will introduce the concept of "digisexuality" and walk through the latest innovations in sex tech, from immersive pornography to AI powered companions. She'll share emerging research on how norms around intimacy are shifting in real time.
The talk poses a genuinely open question for the audience: as intimacy on demand becomes more available, what do we stand to gain, and what might we lose? 🤖

events.title: KALW Presents KALW's 85th Birthday Benefit KALW's 85th Birthday Benefit with Rozzi, DEATHX_XHEAD, DJ Wonway Posibul
events.location: The Warfield, 982 Market St, San Francisco, CA 94102
events.description:
This spring, BADBADNOTGOOD will be bringing their genre defying album, Mid Spiral suite: Chaos, Order and Growth, on the road, featuring a special performance with Baby Rose , of their joint EP, Slow Burn. The trio called on some of their closest friends and collaborators, BADBADNOTGOOD touring member Felix Fox-Pappas (keys) and a few key-players in the Toronto jazz scene including Kaelin Murphy (trumpet), Juan Carlos Medrano Magallenes (percussion) and LA musician Tyler Lott (guitar), for an intensive and productive one-week of recording at Valentine Studios in Los Angeles in February 2024. The result is the Mid Spiral suite: Chaos, Order and Growth , which will be performed along with live reinterpretations of their previous releases.

The Mid Spiral suite exploits instrumental jazz at its core allowing for BADBADNOTGOOD to continue to push the boundaries of how they integrate a limitless range of genres and musicianship into their compositions. For the Valentine sessions, the trio invited additional musicians to provide more voices of instrumentation, resulting in a deeply collaborative and expansive new sound. As the trio sifted through the weeks’ worth of material, it was clear that three distinct moods emerged, a deeper reflection of where the musicians are within their own personal lives, along with the state of the wider world: Chaos, Order, and Growth.

Since the release of their late-2021 acclaimed album Talk Memory , BADBADNOTGOOD has been steady at work. The alt-jazz ensemble also received their fifth GRAMMY nomination, this time for Best Remixed Recording for their remix of Turnstile’s “Alien Love Call,” taken from the New Heart Designs EP.

In January BADBADNOTGOOD released “ Take What’s Given ,” featuring emerging Houston vocalist reggie , which followed a string of one-off singles with collaborators including Charlotte Day Wilson on “ Sleeper ,” 1999 WRITE THE FUTURE, Westside Gunn plus Conway The Machine on “ MiNt cHoCoLaTe ” and Jonah Yano on “ the ordinary is ordinary because it ordinarily repeats. ” Further, BADBADNOTGOOD contributed to Daniel Caesar’s 2023 album Never Enough , worked with rising artist Elmiene on an edit of his single “ Marking My Time ” and contributed to the Talking Heads Stop Making Sense tribute album with a cover of “ This Must Be The Place (Naive Melody) ” with Norah Jones.

events.title: City Arts & Lectures @ Sydney Goldstein Theater - Leïla Slimani in conversation with Nadja Spiegelman
events.location: Sydney Goldstein Theater
events.description: Event location: Sydney Goldstein Theater, 275 Hayes St in San Francisco. Black Bird Bookstore will be the onsite bookseller at this event. Leïla Slimani, a critically acclaimed French-Moroccan novelist, celebrates I’ll Take the Fire, the last in her trilogy of novels based on her family’s roots in revolutionary Morocco. She weaves the brilliant story of one woman’s global search for freedom and purpose. Leïla Slimani is a critically acclaimed French-Moroccan novelist, journalist, and cultural figure whose work has made her one of the most influential voices in contemporary francophone literature. She is the author of The Perfect Nanny, for which she became the first Moroccan woman to win France’s most prestigious literary prize, the Goncourt. Her other books include Adèle, Sex and Lies, In the Country of Others, and Watch Us Dance, which are the first and second parts of a trilogy of novels based on her family’s roots in revolutionary Morocco. She is President Emmanuel Macron’s personal representative for the promotion of the French language and culture, and was the chair of the jury for the 2023 International Booker Prize. This year Leïla Slimani concludes her trilogy of novels with I’ll Take the Fire, the story of a woman who, after growing up in socially conservative Morocco, is looking for somewhere she can feel free to be herself. Against the backdrop of the fall of the Berlin Wall and 9/11, Slimani explores sexuality, freedom, and purpose in this brave and poetic novel. Nadja Spiegelman is the author of the memoir I’m Supposed To Protect You From All This and five books for children, including the award-winning Lost in NYC . She is currently a culture editor at The New York Times. Spiegelman previously worked as the editor-in-chief of Astra Magazine and the online editor of The Paris Review. Her writing has appeared in New York Review of Books, The New Yorker, NYT Book Review, The Cut, and more. This program was made possible by the generous support of Chula Reynolds & Sophia Collier Photo by Francesca Mantovani

events.title: Parallel Pursuits Circle
events.location: 550 Laguna St, San Francisco + South Studio
events.description:
🌿 About Event
This gathering is for people who experience the particular isolation of holding multiple serious pursuits in parallel—work and writing, analysis and art, professional roles and personal projects across different domains, all at once.
When you're the sole integrator of your own combination, the world around you often doesn't hold all of it. This circle creates space for that integration to be witnessed and met with understanding.
We'll spend 90 minutes in conversation with people who actually get it: the euphoria and the exhaustion, the contradictions you haven't resolved, why you're doing this work anyway, and what it means to find community around this particular condition.
🕰 Flow / Schedule
Please arrive by 6:30pm
6:30 – 6:45 Settling in + Opening meditation (breath work to ground the container)
6:45 – 7:45 Small group conversations on isolation, integration, and why you're doing this work
7:45 – 8:00 Group reflection + Closing
👥 Facilitator
Jia Hui Seow is a writer, survey data analyst, and researcher exploring measurement of psychedelic experience across cultures. She's interested in the architecture of working across domains and what becomes possible when that integration is witnessed.
💫 Who This Is For
This space is for people doing serious work across multiple domains in parallel—whether professional, creative, intellectual, or personal. You're welcome here if you:
Experience the isolation of holding multiple real pursuits at once
Are willing to share openly about your work and its challenges
Can hold contradictions without needing to resolve them
Are interested in listening to understand rather than debate.
No expertise required. Only honesty and curiosity.
💛 Suggested Donation
Suggested donation: $5–10 at the door to support space stewardship. No one will be turned away for lack of funds.
🏛 About The Commons
The Commons is a community-based "Fourth Place" that catalyzes each member's path to authenticity, full self-expression, and aliveness—rooted in the belief that community is essential to that journey. Located in the heart of San Francisco, we are redefining what it means to gather, work, and connect. By day, we're a playful co-working space; by night, a vibrant community meeting house.
🚪 Arrival Info
Please enter via the stairway at 550 Laguna St, San Francisco (corner of Hayes & Laguna).

events.title: Reclaiming our Democracy and Economy from AI moderated by Jackie Fielder
events.location: Medicine for Nightmares, 3036 24th St, San Francisco, CA 94110
events.description: Join moderator Supervisor Jackie Fielder for an evening exploring how we, as everyday people, can take back our economy and democracy from artificial intelligence. We will explore what we even mean when we talk about “AI,” whether we’re in an AI bubble, the impacts of AI, whether we should be afraid of AI, and who’s behind the AI hype. This panel is jam-packed with women authors whose books have inspired critical conversations about AI and the tech sector at large: Dr. Alex Hanna, co-author of The AI Con, Wendy Liu, author of Abolish Silicon Valley, and Tamara Kneese, author of Notes Toward a Digital Workers’ Inquiry. Wendy Liu made a career switch from software engineer to writer, a move that was sparked by reading lots of books at a time when her startup was tanking. Now she mostly writes about the horrors of Silicon Valley and why tech workers need to organise. She is the author of Abolish Silicon Valley. Dr. Alex Hanna is a writer and sociologist of technology, labor, and politics. She is the Director of Research at the Distributed AI Research Institute (DAIR). Her work examines how new computational technologies--such as AI and machine learning--exacerbate racial, gender, and class inequality through their data practices and effects on labor. With Emily M. Bender, Dr. Hanna is the co-author of The AI Con (Harper, 2025), a book about AI and the hype around it. They also run the Mystery AI Hype Theater 3000 series, playfully and wickedly tearing apart AI hype on their livestream and podcast. She also works in the area of social movements, focusing on the dynamics of anti-racist campus protest in the US and Canada. She holds a BS in Computer Science and Mathematics and a BA in Sociology from Purdue University, and an MS and a PhD in Sociology from the University of Wisconsin-Madison. Dr. Tamara Kneese is a Senior Research Scientist at Partnership on AI and a Practitioner Fellow at the University of Virginia's Environmental Institute. She is the author of Death Glitch: How Techno-Solutionism Fails Us in The Life and Beyond (Yale University Press 2023) and co-author (with Capacitor Collective) of Notes Toward a Digital Workers' Inquiry (Common Notions 2025). Supervisor Jackie Fielder is a Mission renter, public bank organizer, former city commissioner and educator, and climate and environmental justice advocate. Jackie got her start in the #NoDAPL movement by organizing for divestment from the Wall Street banks financing the Dakota Access Pipeline. In 2017, she co-founded the San Francisco Defund DAPL Coalition and the San Francisco Public Bank Coalition to start the nation’s first city-owned bank to support small businesses, affordable housing, and renewable energy. She’s the proud granddaughter of Mexican immigrants and Native American grandparents and a citizen of the Three Affiliated Tribes of North Dakota, with Two Kettle Lakota and Hidatsa descent. She graduated from Stanford University in 2016 with a Bachelors of Arts in Public Policy and a Masters of Arts in Sociology.

events.title: Night Watch // Gregory Rick
events.location: Johansson Projects, 2300 Telegraph Ave, Oakland
events.description: Johansson Projects presents Night Watch, a striking exhibition of paintings and works on paper by Gregory Rick that boldly reimagines history painting through the fractured lens of contemporary life. Apocryphal yet deeply referential and incisive, Rick’s compositions collapse past events with biblical and mythological imagery, art-historical allusions, and capitalist spectacle into hypersaturated scenes that are at once facetious and unsettling. A burning cross, a feline maw, a tree of serpents, and tigers charging toward machine-gun fire populate a world where violence–and communal acts of resistance–appear both ancient and immediate. Figures clad in Fila jackets, yellow Hokas, and other recognizable markers of contemporary consumer culture anchor these frenetic compositions in the present. As a veteran, citizen, and subject, Rick draws upon collective memory to confront the cognitive dissonance of navigating everyday life amid recurring cycles of violence, surveillance, and oppression. In works such as Night Watch (We Got Us), Rembrandt’s civic militia meets Picasso’s Guernica, transforming the historical tableau into a contemporary cry for help and vision of mutual aid. A few of the works are painted and collaged on silk mesh, their transparencies exposing the layers of their construction and underscoring history itself as an unstable, assembled narrative. In Night Watch, Rick contends with what it means to stay woke and on watch in the 2020s. Night Watch runs from September 30 to October 31, 2026 with an opening reception Friday, October 2 from 5-8pm.

events.title: ENTRE DIENTESJAWS[tiburón]— Bay Area Launch with translators Dora Prieto and Daniela Rodríguez Chevalier
events.location: Medicine for Nightmares, 3036 24th St, San Francisco, CA 94110
events.description: Something toothy is coming to Medicina. Join translators Dora Prieto and Daniela Rodríguez Chevalier, with special guests Román Luján and Hugo García Manríquez, for an evening of poetry with bite, celebrating Xitlalitl Rodríguez Mendoza’s JAWS [tiburón], translation out now from Cardboard House Press (2026). What happens when the shark gets tired of being the villain? When it splits into a chorus of workers who have bills to pay? When jaws starts sounding suspiciously like yo ? Moving between ocean and office, Hollywood horror and everyday survival, this darkly comic collection sinks its dientes into work, language, and the business of staying alive. Come for poems, stay until your teeth get pointy and a fin cuts the moon in two. DORA PRIETO is a Mexican and Canadian poet and translator whose life and work have an unruly relationship to geography. She is a 2025–27 Wallace Stegner Fellow at Stanford and has held residencies at Hedgebrook and the Banff Centre. She is the co-translator of JAWS [tiburón] by Xitlalitl Rodríguez Mendoza (Cardboard House Press, 2026). Her work has appeared in Best New Poets 2025 , Catapult , and Maisonneuve , and she won the 2025 Bronwen Wallace Award for poetry. She is a co-founder of El Mashup Collective, and her practice moves across poetry, translation, textiles, and visual forms. Daniela Rodríguez Chevalier Born in Cuernavaca, Mexico ✿ city of eternal Spring ✿ and raised in el Distrito Federal, Daniela Rodríguez Chevalier writes and translates from unceded Coast Salish territories (Vancouver, BC). Her work has appeared in PRISM International, Volume, Discorder and carte blanche. events.title: Live at inStudio
events.location: inStudio with Empowerment Avenue, 473 25th St., Suite A, Oakland
events.description: The Distance Between: Traveling Beyond Count Time Program & Event Overview Currently on view at Empowerment Avenue’s inStudio in Oakland, The Distance Between: Traveling Beyond Count Time brings together stories told through the work of Black currently and formerly incarcerated artists. Their work traces histories of enslavement and confinement alongside the realities of incarceration today, while carrying memory, endurance, and imagination toward something beyond them. Together, these works invite us to explore the space between captivity and liberation, to see differently, and to imagine a world beyond systems of punishment. Friday, October 2 | 1:00–9:00 PM 1:00 PM | Gallery Opens Empowerment Avenue’s inStudio will open its doors at 1:00 PM, inviting visitors to experience The Distance Between: Traveling Beyond Count Time and spend time with the work throughout the afternoon. Live at inStudio 6:00 PM | Panel Discussion: Black Yearning for Freedom At 6:00 PM, we will gather for a conversation exploring a continuing Black yearning for freedom and the ways artists carry memory, history, our bodies, and our imaginations onto canvas and paper. Moving between histories of enslavement and confinement and the realities of incarceration today, the conversation will consider art as a place to hold these experiences while also imagining beyond them. What does it mean to create from within systems of confinement without allowing confinement to define the limits of the imagination? What can Black creative practice teach us about freedom, possibility, and the worlds we have yet to make? The conversation will feature exhibition artists Ray Williams Jr. and Alvin Smith, alongside exhibition co-curator De’jon Joy. The discussion will be moderated by Milan Drake, Community Design Lead at the Hasso Plattner Institute of Design at Stanford University (the d.school). 7:00 PM | Live Performance by Inertia the Artist Following the conversation, Inertia the Artist will offer a live performance in the gallery. Inertia the Artist is an Oakland-based vocalist, loop artist, facilitator, and somatic psychotherapist whose soulful music and sound work center healing, transformation, and social change. The performance extends the evening’s exploration beyond the visual, bringing voice, sound, body, and collective experience into the exhibition space.

The artists in the exhibition engage in image-making, in a truly hands-on sense, to subvert (or amplify) the power attributed to photos as documentary evidence and bearers of truth. events.description: King Lear by William Shakespeare Directed by Michael Socrates Moran Music composed by Paul Dresher Presented by Oakland Theater Project & New Performance Traditions In the twilight of his rule, a king sets out to divide the kingdom among his three daughters. But in mistaking flattery for love, Lear’s foolish choices usher in a new reign of domination, cruelty and collapse. As a self-styled “bastard” sets out to upend the ruling order, Lear must confront his own part in the kingdom’s downfall. Can he transform in time to reclaim what is sacred before the clown show becomes the new order? Ritual and spectacle collide in Michael Socrates Moran ’s bold, contemporary staging of Shakespeare’s epic tragedy, featuring a cast of 30, including the “irrepressible” ( SF Chronicle ) J Jha ( Angels in America, Mahābhārata ) as Lear; renowned performer, singer, and writer Rinde Eckert ( Ghost Quartet ) as The Fool; and music composed by Paul Dresher and performed live by the Dresher | Davel Invented Instrument Duo .

events.title: City Arts & Lectures @ Sydney Goldstein Theater - Kyle MacLachlan in conversation with Jesse Hawthorne Ficks
events.location: Sydney Goldstein Theater
events.description: Event location: Sydney Goldstein Theater, 275 Hayes St in San Francisco. Black Bird Bookstore will be the onsite bookseller at this event. In his upcoming debut memoir Fictional Selves, cultural icon Kyle MacLachlan looks back at his off-beat journey in Hollywood. From his debut in David Lynch’s Dune, to his award-winning performance as as Special Agent Dale Cooper in Twin Peaks, to his recent viral social media stardom, MacLachlan reveals his complex relationship with fame, his relationships with iconic actors, and everything he learned along the way. Kyle MacLachlan has built a fascinating acting career, performing in everything from David Lynch’s Twin Peaks to the adaptation of the video game Fallout. In the process, he has become a beloved cultural icon. MacLachlan’s 1984 film debut was the starring role in Lynch’s Dune. He would go on to work with the experimental director on multiple projects, including the classic film Blue Velvet. For his performance as Special Agent Dale Cooper in Twin Peaks, MacLachlan won a Golden Globe and gained international fame. Over the next few decades, MacLachlan brought his unique talent to a wide variety of movies, including The Doors, Showgirls, and the live-action adaptation of The Flintstones. MacLachlan also became a sought after guest star for popular television shows, including How I Met Your Mother, Law & Order SVU, Sex and the City, and Portlandia. More recently, he has gained a new group of fans through his award-winning performance in the show Fallout and the crime comedy show The Lowdown. When not acting, MacLachlan co-founded the winery Pursued by Bear, co-created the podcasts What Are We Even Doing? and Varnamtown, and became a viral session on TikTok and Instagram. In his upcoming debut memoir Fictional Selves, MacLachlan looks back at his off-beat journey in Hollywood. Through beautiful storytelling, MacLachlan traces his many iconic roles, his relationship with fame, and his iconic artistic collaborators, revealing details of his career and the lessons he has learned over the past fifty years. Jesse Hawthorne Ficks is the Film History Coordinator at the Academy of Art University in San Francisco, a member of the San Francisco Bay Area Film Critics Circle, and has been a guest professor at Chapman University. He is Film Festival Critic for 48 Hills and is a frequent co-presenter with local festivals, including the San Francisco International LGBTQ+ Film Festival, hosted by Frameline. For 25 years, Ficks has curated and hosted MOViES FOR MANiACS, “a film series celebrating underrated and overlooked cinema, in a neo-sincere manner.” A limited number of tickets include a copy of MacLachlan’s new book, Fictional Selves. If your ticket comes with a book and you are unable to attend this event, please call Black Bird Bookstore at (415) 742-5203 to arrange for pick-up. Books are available for you to collect at 4541 Irving Street in San Francisco up to 7 days following the event. Photo by Sophy Holland
