events.title: inStudio: The Distance Between: Traveling Beyond Count Time
events.location: inStudio with Empowerment Avenue, 473 25th St., Suite A, Oakland
events.description: Program & Event Overview Currently on view at Empowerment Avenue’s inStudio in Oakland, The Distance Between: Traveling Beyond Count Time brings together stories told through the work of Black currently and formerly incarcerated artists. Their work traces histories of enslavement and confinement alongside the realities of incarceration today, while carrying memory, endurance, and imagination toward something beyond them. Together, these works invite us to explore the space between captivity and liberation, to see differently, and to imagine a world beyond systems of punishment. Saturday, October 3 | 12:00–5:00 PM 12:00 PM | Gallery Opens On Saturday, inStudio will reopen for an afternoon of art, conversation, and community. Open Flow: Community Dialogue Throughout the afternoon, exhibition co-curators De’jon Joy and Christine Lashaw will host an open-flow community dialogue inside the gallery. Rather than a traditional panel, the gathering will create space for visitors to move through the exhibition, ask questions, sit in conversation, and reflect together on the histories, ideas, and possibilities held within the work. Currently incarcerated participating artists will also call into the gallery at various points throughout the day, creating opportunities for visitors to hear directly from artists whose work they are encountering on the walls. The weekend invites audiences not simply to view the exhibition, but to spend time inside its questions: to consider what we have inherited, what we have normalized, and what becomes possible when Black artists are given space to imagine beyond captivity.

events.title: Artists’ Reception – Julie Engelmann, Amos Goldbaum, Liv Losee-Unger, Fernanda Martínez, & Deirdre Weinberg
events.location: Manna Gallery, 473 25th St., Oakland
events.description: Meet the artists of Big, Small, and Everything In Between and celebrate this group exhibition featuring five Bay Area muralists. Join us for an afternoon gathering and a closer look at how these artists bring the color, energy, and visual language of their public work into the gallery’s intimate setting. Free and open to the public. Julie Engelmann, based in Half Moon Bay, works across murals, paintings, and digital illustration. Using media ranging from acrylic on canvas to spray paint on large walls, she creates highly detailed and often surrealistic imagery, frequently drawing on historical themes and using color and composition to create new visual possibilities. Amos Goldbaum is a San Francisco–based visual artist known for his signature line drawings, which span canvases, large-scale murals, prints, and apparel. Inspired by the places and everyday scenes around him, his work combines multiple viewpoints, angles, and moments in time into cohesive compositions connected by a singular line. His murals can be found throughout the San Francisco Bay Area and in cities around the world, including New York, Los Angeles, Seattle, Tokyo, and Kathmandu. Liv Losee-Unger is a Bay Area muralist known for vibrant, nature-inspired, and community-centered art. With more than sixty public artworks completed across the United States and abroad, her detailed and colorful murals transform spaces through stories of flora, fauna, femininity, and human connection. Fernanda Martínez is an Oakland-based painter, muralist, and sculptor whose vibrant, expressive work draws from memories and observations of nature. Born and raised in Mexico City, she moved to the Bay Area in 2015, where she has developed an experimental and intuitive practice exploring the emotional depth of color, form, pattern, and texture. Her work spans painting, sculpture, murals, and public art, transforming her distinctive visual language across two- and three-dimensional forms. Martinez has exhibited her paintings and sculptures in galleries and has collaborated on numerous public art projects for businesses, nonprofit organizations, and community-focused and affordable housing developments. Deirdre Weinberg is a multidisciplinary artist with deep ties to the San Francisco Bay Area, working across murals, public art, and studio practice. Her evolving work currently focuses on climate change, using a limited black-and-white palette to explore landscapes, seascapes, and airscapes with a sense of urgency and starkness. Whether creating work in public spaces or the studio, Weinberg seeks to build community, connect with viewers, and inspire conversation, reflection, and new perspectives. events.title: Real Social Connections
events.location: 550 Laguna St, San Francisco + Full Studio
events.description:
🌿 Description
Beyond small talk, social scripts, and the pressure to be a certain way.
An immersive half-day exploration of movement, playfulness, touch, authentic relating, and meaningful conversation in a trauma-informed space.

🌿 About This Gathering
Meaningful connection rarely happens by accident. It tends to emerge when we feel safe enough to slow down, be ourselves, and meet one another with curiosity.
This gathering is an invitation to explore what helps genuine connection emerge - not by performing, saying the "right" thing, or following a script, but by creating the conditions where we can be more present, playful, and authentic with ourselves and others.
At the heart of this gathering is a simple idea: connection deepens when we feel safe enough to be seen and expressed -not just the polished parts of ourselves, but also the parts we might usually hide or hold back. Through movement, play, somatic awareness, and guided conversations, we'll explore what happens when we let ourselves show up more fully and meet one another more deeply.
This is an evolving exploration of connection, community, and play. I'm excited to create a deep experience together and to see what becomes possible when we give ourselves more space to be ourselves and meet one another more fully.
My hope is that you'll leave with a deeper sense of connection to yourself and others, and maybe even with a new friend or two.

🕰 Flow / Schedule


💫 Who This Is For
This gathering is for anyone who longs for more genuine connection. It’s especially for people who sometimes struggle to connect, fit in, or feel like they truly belong; for those who appreciate a slower pace when getting to know others; and for anyone curious about moving beyond small talk, social performance, or the feeling that they need to say the “right” thing or show up in a certain way.
Rather than trying to “get connection right,” we’ll explore what naturally allows connection to emerge—through presence, play, movement, and authentic conversation.
Whether you're outgoing, introverted, or somewhere in between, you'll be invited to participate at your own pace. No previous experience is needed: just come as you are.

👥 Facilitator
Simone Giacometti is a somatic practitioner, psychedelic integration guide, and facilitator passionate about helping people heal, grow, and connect more deeply with themselves and others.
Originally trained as a scientist, Simone spent years working at the intersection of biology, technology, and program management before transitioning into healing work. Today, he supports people through one-on-one sessions that weave together trauma-informed healing, somatic practices, inner exploration, and psychedelic integration work to help people reconnect with themselves and grow into greater authenticity.
His group facilitation draws on somatics, authentic relating, nervous system awareness, and play to create spaces where people can slow down, be themselves, and feel more at home with others. (This gathering is fully substance-free and centered on movement, conversation, and connection.)

Learn more about Simone and his work at healwithsimone.com

events.title: Fear Not – William Rhodes Artist’s Talk with Gospel Choir Performance
events.location: Transmission Gallery, 770 West Grand Ave., Suite A, Oakland
events.description: Please join us for William Rhodes’ talk with gospel choir performance by the Dr. George W. Davis Senior Center Choir, music conductor and leader Kenneth Little Saturday, Oct 3rd starting at 2 pm This is part of a series of NEXUS SFBay events including the Caleb Dowdell performance with his piece, Our Prism of Dreams, starting at 1:30 pm just downstairs at Gearbox Gallery, performance about 15 minutes. William’s talk starts at 2 pm upstairs with the Dr. George W. Davis Senior Center Choir closing out the event with a Gospel Choir performance. See one or both at that galleries at 770 West Grand Ave in Oakland. More about Fear Not, William Rhodes’ solo exhibition at Transmission Gallery: William Rhodes’s sculptures on view incorporate objects that have been used, inherited, discarded, or found with elements he has carved himself. Trained early on as a furniture maker, he combines hand carved figures, flames and snakes with objects collected from a family home, photographs, hardware, tools, and other remnants of everyday life. Neon words signal from some pieces. The resulting works resemble shrines or memorials, but they remain grounded in the ordinary. Religious symbols appear alongside household objects. A photograph might be surrounded by carved waves, tools, hardware, animals, or religious symbols. A suitcase can become an architectural space. A toilet becomes the base of an unexpected monument. Things with little apparent value are carefully incorporated into elaborate constructions, their histories becoming part of the work. ​ Rhodes is equally interested in people; family, mentors, and leaders, as well as those who have been overlooked or treated as disposable, recognizing and elevating their presence in his work. By giving attention to these lives, enshrining and revering them, he considers how value is assigned and who gets remembered. The title Fear Not appears in the work as both a phrase and a kind of instruction. It can be read in relation to the religious imagery that runs throughout the sculptures, but it also takes on a morepersonal meaning. To look closely at lives and objects that are easily dismissed is, in its own way, an act of resistance to that dismissal.

events.title: LIVE MUSIC: The Sleeves, Fred Frith
events.location: 4-Star Theater, 2200 Clement St, San Francisco, CA 94121
events.description: The Sleeves The Sleeves are the duo of Jack Cooper and Tara Cunningham, both likely known to you as one half of Modern Nature. Following an all-instrumental Mossy Tapes release last November, Cooper and Cunningham have recorded 10 new songs showcasing their vocal and guitar interplay with only the faintest echoes of prior efforts (individually or collectively), representing a fully realized leap forward from their largely improvised debut. 'The Sleeves' is a somewhat counter intuitive take on the guitar/vocal duo formula (provided you think there is such a thing) though it's not nearly as simplistic as "the space between the notes" -- it would be the height of exaggeration to say an album this simultaneously expansive and incandescent is unprecedented. But it doesn't happen nearly often enough, either. Bandcamp | IG Fred Frith Multi-instrumentalist, composer, and improviser Fred Frith has been making noise of one kind or another for more than 50 years, starting with the rock collective Henry Cow, which he co-founded with Tim Hodgkinson in 1968. Fred is best known as a pioneering electric guitarist and improviser, song-writer, and composer for film, dance and theater. Through bands like Art Bears, Massacre, Skeleton Crew, the Fred Frith Guitar Quartet, Cosa Brava, and the FF Trio he has stayed close to his roots in rock and folk music while branching out in many other directions. His compositions have been performed by ensembles ranging from Eclipse Quartet and the Bang on a Can All Stars to Concerto Köln and Galax Quartet, from the BBC Scottish Symphony Orchestra to the ROVA and Arte Sax Quartets, from Sleepytime Gorilla Museum and Ground Zero to the Glasgow Improvisers’ Orchestra. Film music credits include the acclaimed documentaries Rivers and Tides , Leaning into the Wind , and Tracing Light , directed by Thomas Riedelsheimer; The Tango Lesson , Yes and The Party by Sally Potter; Middle of the Moment by Nicolas Humbert and Werner Penzel; as well as Penzel’s Zen for Nothing , Peter Mettler’s Gods, Gambling and LSD , and the award-winning (and Oscar-nominated) Last Day of Freedom , by Nomi Talisman and Dee Hibbert-Jones. Composing for dance throughout his long career, Fred has worked with Rosalind Newman and Bebe Miller in New York, François Verret and Catherine Diverrès in France, and Amanda Miller and the Pretty Ugly Dance Company over the course of many years in Germany, as well as composing for two documentary films on the work of Anna Halprin. Theater credits include François Chat’s Setaccio and François-Michel Pesenti’s Théâtre du Point Aveugle in Marseille, where he spent six months in 1990 working with “jeunes rockers en chômage des quartiers défavorisés” on the opera Helter Skelter . Fred has performed works by and sometimes alongside composers John Luther Adams, Gavin Bryars, Sylvie Courvoisier, Alvin Curran, George Lewis, Annea Lockwood, René Lussier, Jose Maceda, Meredith Monk, Pauline Oliveros, Terry Riley, and Christian Wolff; improvised with Lotte Anker, Derek Bailey, Han Bennink, Peter Brötzmann, Lol Coxhill, Janet Feder, gabby fluke-mogul, Tim Hodgkinson, Joëlle Léandre, Phil Minton, Ikue Mori, Butch Morris, Bob Ostertag, Evan Parker, Zeena Parkins, Paula Sanchez, Susana Santos Silva and Camel Zekri, to name a few; collaborated with classical virtuosi Evelyn Glennie, Katia Labèque, Viktoria Mullova, and Werner Bärtschi; and—as session musician—recorded on albums by, for example, Brian Eno, The Residents, Robert Wyatt, The Swans, Violent Femmes, Material, Negativland, John Zorn, Matthew and the Unfortunates, and Half Japanese. He is currently performing solo and with Normal (home-made instrument duo with Sudhu Tewari) and Frelonia (with Lotte Anker and Núria Andorrà), as well as in countless combinations of his favorite co-conspirators. The recipient of Italy’s Demetrio Stratos Prize for his life’s work in experimental music and an honorary doctorate from the University of Huddersfield in his home county of Yorkshire, Fred taught for twenty years at the legendary epicenter of American experimental music, Mills College in Oakland, California; as well as co-directing (with Alfred Zimmerlin) the improvisation master’s program at the Musik Akademie in Basel, Switzerland. He is the subject of Nicolas Humbert and Werner Penzel’s much loved Step Across the Border , cited by Cahiers du Cinéma as one of the 20th century’s hundred most influential films. events.title: The Commons Public Hours ☕
events.location: 540 Laguna St, San Francisco + Full Space
events.description:
🎉 Public Hours at the Commons 🎉
Every Sunday, the Commons opens to the public — no membership required. Come co-work, connect, create, or just explore the space at your own pace. ✨
🕘 When: Every Sunday, 9 AM – 10 PM
📍 Where: 540 Laguna St, San Francisco (corner of Hayes & Laguna, basement level)
RSVP and we'll email you your entry code ahead of time — so you can let yourself straight in when you arrive.
──────────────────────────────
🧭 A self-guided day
Public Hours are self-guided — come in, settle in, and make the space your own. Weekends are usually unstaffed, so there's no check-in desk or guided tour. Our members are glad to answer questions about the space; for anything else — including guided tours, which we don't offer as drop-ins — email hello@thesfcommons.com ahead of time.
──────────────────────────────
🔭 Getting in
Your entry code comes by email. Once you RSVP, we'll send you a personal QR code — that's your key for the day. Keep it handy on your phone (and check spam if you don't see it).
Find us. We're at 540 Laguna St, on the corner of Hayes & Laguna. Head down the stairs beside Earthbody to the basement level — that's the Commons.
Scan your QR code at the reader to unlock the door. Hold your phone just below the Kisi reader by the door and it'll let you in.
Your access stays active all day, 9 AM – 10 PM, so you can come and go freely.
Can't find your code on the day? No problem — scan the QR posted on the door to check in and get a fresh one on the spot.
We're shoes-off 🧦 — please clean up after yourself, including dirty dishes and mugs, and use only the front entrance. Trouble getting in? Email hello@thesfcommons.com.




The Commons is a modern-day town square for communal meaning-making, personal discovery, and self-expression in the heart of San Francisco. Apply to become a member here__.

events.title: SFLives Livestream: Journalist Denise Sullivan in conversation with Dr. Saidah Leatutufu-Burch
events.location: Bird & Beckett Books & Records, 653 Chenery St, San Francisco, CA 94131
events.description: Independent reporter Denise Sullivan brings the SF Lives series to Bird & Beckett for a Sunday morning livestream. This month’s guest is Dr. Saidah Leatutufu-Burch. We expect a wide-ranging discussion on the legacy of local Black history, community organizing, economic justice and the November San Francisco ballot. Dr. Sai (Sy) is a Black and Sāmoan San Franciscan, organizer, cultural orator, economic mobility strategist, and liberationist. She is the Founder of Economic Emancipation LLC. and SLB Strategies—a social impact-focused consulting firm committed to equipping organizations with the tools and strategies necessary to drive sustainable change and achieve bold impact. Her work is guided by a core belief: “Liberate with love. Transform with power.” The SFLives Project, a series of candid conversations with San Francisco’s artists, activists and free thinkers, was conceived as a print media column by Denise Sullivan for the San Francisco Examiner where it ran from 2018-2022, then transitioned into a live-streamed conversation, produced by Jenna Littlejohn, for Bird & Beckett. Past editions are archived on the Bird & Beckett YouTube channel. https://denisesullivan.org/about/

events.description: FREE, $10-$15 suggested donation Sponsored by Yerba Buena Gardens Festival & Yerba Buena Partnership Media sponsorship by 48 Hills A part of the Litquake Out Loud series How is a tree like a stripper pole? Where do the poetics of physicality and ecology overlap? As digital spaces collapse into slop and surveillance, how can queer communities in the material world dig and twerk toward pleasure and liberation? Here, QTBIPOC writers Brandon Logans, Kevin Madrigal Galindo, May-Li Khoe, and Nnenna Loveth explore the sensuality, tenderness, and resilience of both body and earth. events.description: FREE, $10-$15 suggested donation Sponsored by Yerba Buena Gardens Festival & Yerba Buena Partnership Media sponsorship by 48 Hills A part of the Litquake Out Loud series If you’re looking for architects to dream up a new world, why not start with the folks who have already built one? As trans and gender non-confirming people, we are skilled at identifying what is meant to stifle and cage us, as well as envisioning what else is possible when we rage towards liberation. Trans people teach us what it means to transform the physical conditions of our world and show us what’s possible when our imaginations are freest and at their most feral. These Bay Area trans and non-binary artists will share work resisting erasure and conjuring prayers for the world we’re collectively building. events.title: Purpose Alignment Circle
events.location: 550 Laguna St, San Francisco + Full Studio
events.description:
Purpose Alignment Circle ⭕️
Navigating work right now can feel… confusing.
Layoffs, AI, economic uncertainty, and the pressure to constantly “figure out your career” can make it easy to lose touch with a more fundamental question:
What do I actually want?
If you've ever felt lost, restless or unsure whether your current path still fits - you're not alone.
Join us for Purpose Alignment Circle, a space for candid conversations about vocation, purpose, and what it means to build a career that actually feels aligned with who you are.
This isn't another networking event or career playbook with all the answers.

This is for you if: 💭
You're questioning whether your 9–5 is still working for you
You're considering a career pivot
You want to start your own company
You have a passion project you're exploring alongside your corporate job
You're thinking about taking a sabbatical
OR you just returned from a sabbatical and are figuring out what's next
You want to reconnect with a sense of purpose in your work
You don't have the answer yet - but you're curious enough to explore
This is NOT for you if: 🚫
You're looking for a step-by-step formula for finding your “dream job”
You want someone else to tell you what career you should pursue
You're only interested in optimizing your career for salary or title
You're looking for traditional networking or a transactional job-search event
You're not interested in reflecting on the why behind your work

Session 1: What Am I Actually Seeking? 📆
Explore what we want beneath titles, money, status, and expectations -
Agenda | 2:00–4:00 PM ⏰
2:00–2:10 — Welcome & Check-In
Arrive, settle in, and connect with the intention for the space.
2:10–2:25 — Introductions 👋
Who are you, what brings you here, and what question are you currently sitting with?
2:25–2:40 — Reflective Meditation
A guided reflection to slow down and look beneath the surface of our career goals.
2:40–3:00 — Big Group Conversation 🗣️
What are we actually seeking from our work?
Beyond titles, money, status, security, and other expectations.
3:00–3:30 — Small Group Breakouts
Go deeper in smaller groups and explore what's underneath your current career desires, questions, or uncertainty.
3:30–3:50 — Share Back & Collective Reflection
What surfaced? What surprised you? What are you noticing about what you actually want?
3:50–4:00 — Closing & Next Step
Identify one question or action you'll carry with you beyond the Circle.

What to expect
Guided reflection to slow down and arrive
Candid conversation about work, purpose, and uncertainty
Small-group connection with others navigating similar questions
Space to explore your own inner calling
Practical takeaways to help you move toward greater alignment
Good people, honest conversations, and no pressure to have it all figured out
Bring the question you're sitting with. You don't need to have the answer

Hosted by
Bernadette Lagman
Founder of CareerDette Coaching & Recruiting
Bernadette is a Senior Technical Recruiter who has spent 10+ years helping people navigate careers across companies including Amazon, Indeed and Qualtrics
Through CareerDette, she helps jobseekers close the gap between where they are and where they want to go with a focus on career alignment, authenticity

events.title: King Lear
events.location: Z Space's Steindler Stage
events.description: King Lear by William Shakespeare Directed by Michael Socrates Moran Music composed by Paul Dresher Presented by Oakland Theater Project & New Performance Traditions In the twilight of his rule, a king sets out to divide the kingdom among his three daughters. But in mistaking flattery for love, Lear’s foolish choices usher in a new reign of domination, cruelty and collapse. As a self-styled “bastard” sets out to upend the ruling order, Lear must confront his own part in the kingdom’s downfall. Can he transform in time to reclaim what is sacred before the clown show becomes the new order? Ritual and spectacle collide in Michael Socrates Moran ’s bold, contemporary staging of Shakespeare’s epic tragedy, featuring a cast of 30, including the “irrepressible” ( SF Chronicle ) J Jha ( Angels in America, Mahābhārata ) as Lear; renowned performer, singer, and writer Rinde Eckert ( Ghost Quartet ) as The Fool; and music composed by Paul Dresher and performed live by the Dresher | Davel Invented Instrument Duo .

She is moved by stories of resilence, whether in nature or in humanity. Her debut picture book, Daughter of the Light-Footed People , received multiple starred reviews and was praised for its lyrical voice and powerful storytelling. events.title: 🌙✍️ Monthly Reflection Jam [public]
events.location: 550 Laguna St, San Francisco + Full Studio
events.description:
On the first Sundays of every month, gather for an evening of guided journaling and sharing with others in community. This gathering is a space to slow down, honor your experiences of the past month, and connect with others in the neighborhood.
--> Watch this video about what happens at the Reflection Jam.
You'll honor your personal experiences of the past month with a series of reflections, inspired by the life of the monarchs:
Flourishing: What was a moment you felt closest to flourishing?
Encounter: What was a moment you encountered the limits of your human existence? (.e.g. loss, choice, suffering?)
Origins: What was a moment you felt, "This is what makes me who I am"?
Becoming: What was a moment you felt, "This is who I want to be?"
If you're in a social vibe, joining as a Mingling Muser will allow you to share reflections with a small group.
If you want to journal alone, joining as a Solo Sojourner will give you space alongside quiet company for a private reflection.
Come with something to write with/on. If you've come before, bring your pebble.  Invite a friend!
"A lovely way to spend a Sunday evening -- the jam gave me the chance to slow down and sit with the triumphs, disappointments, and transitions of a chaotic and difficult month.” —Justin
“It was a great way to reflect on my month and what I'd learned from my experiences, while meeting some new people and discussing deeper topics.” —Trevor
“Even though I opted for the solo track and was journaling to myself, I felt seen, connected, and celebrated.” —James
Suggested Donation
Please chip in any amount to help cover the costs of hosting and food. There will be a QR code you can scan at check-in.
Schedule:
Doors open at 4:45pm — Check your energy and join as a Mingling Muser or as a Solo Sojourner (you can also switch anytime).
Doors close at 5:15pm — We will create and hold a space for reflection.
Reflection Jam from 5:15pm–7pm
Optional Dinner afterward

Finding 550 Laguna
🚪 Finding The Commons: you can find The Commons at the corner of Hayes & Laguna St – head down the stairs to basement level under The Commons sign.
We are grateful to partner with The Commons to host this event in their incredible space. The Commons is a modern-day town square for communal meaning-making, personal discovery, and self-expression in the heart of San Francisco. Learn more about The Commons here.

Presented by the San Francisco Contemplarium, creating space in our city for honoring our human journey, through programming, physical installations, professional services, and community.

events.title: LIVE MUSIC: Color Green, Healing Potpourri (Presented by folkYEAH!)
events.location: 4-Star Theater, 2200 Clement St, San Francisco, CA 94121
events.description: (((folkYEAH!))) presents: Color Green For the California-based quartet Color Green, playing music together is all about stepping into the unknown. “When we play live, I don’t really know what’s going to happen,” says Noah Kohll, one of the band’s two guitarists and four vocalists. “You really have no idea what you’re going to get with this band, which keeps things fresh for us and maybe makes the live experience special.” In a very short time, they have developed a word-of-mouth reputation as a dynamic and unpredictable live act, grounding their cosmic jams in earthy melodies and drawing from ‘60s SoCal folk-r0ck, ‘70s classic rock, ‘80s underground rock, ‘90s psychedelic dance-rock, and any other sound that catches their ears. Adaptable onstage and off, Color Green has shared stages with a range of groups that reflect both the sophistication and the wild malleability of their sound, including Fuzz, Kikagaku Moyo, Circles Around the Sun, Hiss Golden Messenger, and the Brian Jonestown Massacre. Yet, because they see boundless possibilities from one note to the next, they anchor their music in the urgent present rather than the distant past. Color Green can be a million different bands without losing their essential hue. They capture that wild, mercurial quality on Fool’s Parade, a meditation on loss, grief, confusion, frustration, and the clarity to which they all lead. The album has the dynamic of a tight live set, full of ebbs and flows, highs and lows, quiet moments like the devastating “5:08” and reckless jams like the epic “Kick the Bucket.” “Four Leaf Clover” bustles and shimmies like the kaleidoscopic dance rock of the Stone Roses, while closer “Hazel Eyes” recalls the elaborate orchestrations of Brian Wilson and the whimsical melodies of Buddy Holly. “We shaped it to showcase our range,” says guitarist Corey Madden. “All the songs were written together as a band. It’s the four of us in a room, and it features all of our voices. It’s one step toward what this band truly is. We spent a lot of time getting our shit together as a band, and now it’s set in stone for me.” Color Green started out as a very different, much more limited kind of group. “Me and Corey worked together in New York scooping coffee beans for a living and putting them into bags,” says Kohll. “I was living in a basement sublet, and he would come over to write and jam and record.” From those casual sessions came a self-titled EP in 2021, full of spectral jams and offerings up to Jerry Garcia, their spiritual guide. The next year they followed it up with a self-titled full-length via Aquarium Drunkard, with various friends helping to round out the songs. “These things happen in an interesting way,” says Kohll. “There’s been a lot of weird synchronization with this band. It’s all very organic. After we put out our first album, we thought, Oh, this needs to be a live band, too.” After running through a few different rhythm sections, they met drummer Corey Rose and bassist Kyla Perlmutter, who not only are kickass players but opened up all new possibilities within Color Green. “Our first practice together, everyone was like, This is so loud,” says Rose. “That became a really important part of the band, and we try to capture that dynamic when we record.” Perlmutter adds, “We all really value each other’s input. It doesn’t feel like there’s an unfair hierarchy in this band. We respect each other’s tastes and recognize that we’re all very, very much in love with music in our own ways.” After sharpening their attack on the road—playing DIY shows in small towns while opening for some of their heroes—the expanded Color Green began writing songs for what they considered a debut album. “One of us will come in with a riff or an idea, and the others will take it up and let it morph into something completely different,” says Perlmutter. “What we come up with together, I don’t think any of us could do by ourselves. The music we make is always surprising me.” The album’s title track, with its snaking guitar lines and parallax instrumental interplay, started out as an eastern jam when Rose came in with a very loose idea: “I wanted to write something in 6/8 time,” she says. “It was super awkward at first, but 40 minutes later, it sounded like Fairport Convention. It took everybody to get there.” Says Madden, “I like when stuff happens and it opens up the door to something else in my brain. We might spend a lot of time working on something and get nothing out of it, but then in the back of my head I’m thinking, if you take this and add it to that… Sometimes it takes hours to figure out two seconds of a song, but it’s always worth it.” The aching heart of Fool’s Parade is “5:08,” a moving expression of grief—not moving through it, necessarily, but simply living with it, moment to moment. “What’s it like, on the other side?” they all sing together, as though consoling one another. “Oh, the longing for the space to peer thru.” Inspired by the death of Madden’s father, it is rooted in a Spiritualized show. “I was going through some gnarly personal stuff,” says Madden, “and it was all hitting me at once, all these emotions. I talked my way through some crazy shit, and by the end of the show I had ‘508’ hashed out in my brain. It’s about losing people very close to you and wanting to communicate with them and not really knowing how.” “It’s the quietest song on the record,” says Rose, “but it’s also the heaviest. We all cried while recording it. Everybody’s singing on it, and everybody’s crying on it. Sometimes we’re like, Let’s not play that song tonight. It all depends on how we’re feeling.” Bandcamp | IG Healing Potpourri Healing Potpourri specialize in effervescent chamber pop that’s all but guaranteed to leave the listener in a better mood. But on their new LP, Paradise, the San Francisco-based band led by vocalist/multi-instrumentalist Simi Sohota offers more than just sonic escapism. The album, written and recorded over the past two tumultuous years, finds Sohota processing the often overwhelming deluge of stress, frustration, and despair that’s become a part of modern life. But rather than being completely deflated, he pushed Healing Potpourri’s sound in new directions, blending warm electronics and elements of vibrant psychedelia into something that’s as eclectic as it is instantly enjoyable. The result is 11 songs that seek to imagine a better world and strive to make it a reality, while also still taking the time to appreciate the moments of brightness that can shine through in hard times. Healing Potpourri’s previous album–and Run For Cover Records debut–Blanket of Calm was released in the spring of 2020 to a very different world than the one it was written in. “When Covid hit, like a lot of people, I got depressed and scared,” Sohota explains. “Our record had just come out but we couldn’t do anything. We weren’t able to get together or play shows. So many people were talking about suddenly having free time to work on things and be creative, but I just wasn’t playing music at all.” After a few months, he decided to combat his creative rut by booking studio time with producer/engineer and longtime friend Jason Kick (Mild High Club, Marinero, Sonny & The Sunsets). “I was just trying to force myself out of it so I started going to the studio with Jason once a week. And it worked! I would bring in fragments that I’d be working on at home and then we would start arranging in the studio. We couldn’t get the whole band together so a lot of it was smaller by necessity.” That purposely tighter circle did have room for one more: producer Sean O’Hagan. Known for his work in Stereolab and The High Llamas, the London-based musician would soon become a key collaborator on Paradise over Zoom. “I’m a huge fan of The High Llamas and I’d reached out to Sean back when we were working on Blanket of Calm,” Sohota says. “We weren’t able to make it happen then, but I got in touch again for this record and he ended up helping tremendously. Jason and I would work on a song and send it to him, he’d add something to it and then we’d get inspired by that. It became this back and forth process. I’ve been so obsessed with his music so it really was working with a hero of mine, but he helped coach me to make a record that sounded like me.” Bandcamp | IG DOORS at 7:00PM | MUSIC at 8:00 PM Tickets

events.title: Trust in the Age of AI: Cross-Industry Perspectives on Risk and Regulation #SFTechWeek
events.description:
🌿 About Event
As AI scales across industries, the rules governing it are shifting rapidly—impacting everything from data privacy to ethical decision-making. Navigating compliance and building user trust can feel overwhelming, and many organizations don't know where the guardrails actually are.
Join us for a cross-industry panel on how healthcare, HR, finance, and government are tackling AI regulation, mitigating risk, and building systems people can actually trust.
🕰 Flow / Schedule
Outline the event's rhythm — people love to know what to expect.
🖋 Example:


👥 Facilitators
Sylvia Bargellini (Lini LLC)  #SFTechWeek
💫 Who This Is For
All are welcome. We recommend this event for:
Founders and executives looking to scale AI responsibly without exposing their business to regulatory risk.
Legal, compliance, and risk management professionals navigating tech adoption.
HR, Finance, and Healthcare leaders tasked with deploying AI in sensitive, high-stakes environments.

👥 Panelists
Aakriti Aggarwal - Technical Recruiter

Aakriti is the founder of nSky Solutions, a Bay Area technical recruiting and career coaching practice. Based in the Bay Area, she works closely with founders and hiring teams navigating a job market that looks nothing like it did even two years ago. She helps with both placing tech candidates at startups, while also coaching individual candidates through resume rewrites, LinkedIn positioning, and interview prep. Before recruiting, she spent five years working as a psychologist, which heavily influences how she understands people and evaluates fit today. She's excited to bring her perspective to this AI panel — how AI is reshaping how companies screen candidates and how candidates need to present themselves to get seen.
Norah Leibow - Product Design Researcher, Government Systems
Norah Leibow is a user-centered designer and researcher who specializes in making complex systems legible. As an early adopter of AI in the design process, she has honed responsible-AI best practices for design in federal environments where trust is critical. For the last four years, Norah has worked at Nava PBC in the federal portfolio delivering simple and effective government solutions. Her work is grounded in research, data collection, and clear communication. She holds a BA from University of California Santa Barbara and an MA in Product Design and Development from San Francisco State University. 

Tiffany Tseng - Healthcare Quality Engineer
Tiffany is a quality engineer with 10+ years of experience in the medical device and IVD space and have supported both new product development and design change projects that require regulatory approvals. I'm excited to talk about the implementation of AI and machine learning into medical devices, and how this impacts the way regulatory agencies view product risk.
Carmen Ye - HR and People Operations
Carmen Ye is a People Operations professional, working at the intersection of education and people-centered HR policy. She has centered her career around building social impact in mission-driven organizations. Previous roles include founding HR Team Lead at Hiba Academy Bay Area, a bilingual Mandarin and English primary school. Head of Operations at Make School in San Francisco, a college that empowered students of all backgrounds to contribute through science and technology innovation. She started her People Operations career at LaunchCode, which provides free education and job opportunities to help people launch careers in technology. A graduate of the University of Michigan, and UC Berkeley, Carmen is a proud San Francisco native.

events.title: Blaque Dynamite
events.location: SFJAZZ Center, 201 Franklin St, San Francisco, CA 94102 — Joe Henderson Lab
events.description: GRAMMY-nominated drummer, producer, and composer Blaque Dynamite has become one of the most dynamic and influential beat masters of his generation, celebrated for a style that merges explosive technical mastery with deep groove, humor, and boundless creativity. Born Mike Mitchell Jr. in Houston, Texas, he emerged as a prodigious talent at a young age, absorbing gospel, jazz, funk, and hip-hop into a singular musical language. His remarkable versatility quickly made him one of the most sought-after drummers in contemporary music. Blaque Dynamite’s résumé spans collaborations with some of the most important artists in modern jazz and beyond, including Erykah Badu, Herbie Hancock, Stanley Clarke, Kamasi Washington, Robert Glasper, and Christian Scott aTunde Adjuah. Equally comfortable anchoring intricate jazz ensembles or driving groove-heavy experimental projects, he has earned widespread acclaim for his improvisational brilliance, rhythmic innovation, and magnetic stage presence. In recent years, Blaque Dynamite has expanded his profile as a bandleader, producer, and multimedia artist, releasing projects that blur the boundaries between jazz fusion, beat culture, electronic music, and comedy-infused performance art. His latest work continues to push contemporary Black music into adventurous new territory, combining virtuosic musicianship with fearless experimentation and unmistakable personality.

events.title: Blaque Dynamite

events.description: GRAMMY-nominated drummer, producer, and composer Blaque Dynamite has become one of the most dynamic and influential beat masters of his generation, celebrated for a style that merges explosive technical mastery with deep groove, humor, and boundless creativity. Born Mike Mitchell Jr. in Houston, Texas, he emerged as a prodigious talent at a young age, absorbing gospel, jazz, funk, and hip-hop into a singular musical language. His remarkable versatility quickly made him one of the most sought-after drummers in contemporary music. Blaque Dynamite’s résumé spans collaborations with some of the most important artists in modern jazz and beyond, including Erykah Badu, Herbie Hancock, Stanley Clarke, Kamasi Washington, Robert Glasper, and Christian Scott aTunde Adjuah. Equally comfortable anchoring intricate jazz ensembles or driving groove-heavy experimental projects, he has earned widespread acclaim for his improvisational brilliance, rhythmic innovation, and magnetic stage presence. In recent years, Blaque Dynamite has expanded his profile as a bandleader, producer, and multimedia artist, releasing projects that blur the boundaries between jazz fusion, beat culture, electronic music, and comedy-infused performance art. His latest work continues to push contemporary Black music into adventurous new territory, combining virtuosic musicianship with fearless experimentation and unmistakable personality.

events.title: Robopsychology Salon: What AI Safety Forgets About You
events.location: 550 Laguna St, San Francisco + Full Studio
events.description:
SF tech week is about what AI can do. This evening is about what the AI race is doing to us — to our minds, our hearts and our bodies.

Psychologist and AI researcher Anna Mikeda works on robopsychology, the psychology of AI minds and of the humans who interact with them. She brings the latest research together, and asks the safety question from the human side: not whether AI turns on us, but what we turn into.

Three movements. Minds: cognitive debt — what we stop doing when the model does it for us. Hearts: AI relationships, loneliness, and what an always-available companion does to our tolerance for other people. Bodies: the build loop as a reward loop — instant answers, a model that always agrees, the next project instead of shipping this one, and why it runs on the same architecture that gaming and social media exploit.

Then the practical part: what to do about this. 

Talk, art, open Q&A, and tools you can use. For builders, users, and anyone who has noticed their own attention changing.

events.description:
Note: while there are many guests listed in the RSVP, most of these are carried over from previous events in this series. We don't expect much more than 30 to attend.

"Imagination without reason is mere fancy, but reason without imagination is sterile. That is partly why scientists and philosophers alike have always used imaginary scenarios to help sharpen their ideas and push them to their limits." - The Pig that Wants to be Eaten, by Julian Baggini

For this meeting (October 7), we'll be discussing arguments for the existence of God.
Please review this very brief primer on the norms of philosophical discussion: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1Gj3HesfWz4A2kEAMSY0x7hNxvJZNtiCexUeilJXVak8/edit?usp=sharing
It is highly recommended to read these:Section 2c of this article, on the fine-tuning argument: https://iep.utm.edu/design-arguments-for-existence-of-god/#SH2c
This article on the Kalam cosmological argument: https://www.qcc.cuny.edu/socialSciences/ppecorino/INTRO_TEXT/Chapter%203%20Religion/CH-3-Documents/ch3-kalam-ont-arg-notes.pdf
Some examples of topics we've discussed at past meetings:
Do you survive being teleported?
Is God required to have morality?
What are the limits of free speech?
Is it moral to breed pigs that want to be eaten?
Should crimes be punished before they happen?
Are there "higher" and "lower" pleasures?
Do immoral people just have bad luck?
Is monogamy unethical?
Is the existence of evil a problem for belief in God?
Should we try to become immortal?
Are we obligated to do much more to the world's poor?
Is it okay to deliberately create a disabled child?
Is it permissible to kill and eat animals?
Should we enter the experience machine?
Is science the only source of knowledge?
Is what is right or wrong a matter of opinion?
On what basis should we care about the environment?
Can we know we are not brains in a vat?
What is a potential person worth?
What is gender?
What is philosophy and how is it done?
Is abortion morally permissible?
Does philosophy make assumptions?
Is evolutionary psychology a legitimate science?
Should paid organ donation be permitted?
Can we have knowledge without certainty?
Is adult consensual incest always immoral?
Is everything we do ultimately motivated by self-interest?
Is it immoral to have children?
Are there good arguments against objective morality?
Should we use genetic therapies to increase intelligence?
Is it morally permissible to select your child's race?
Does free will require the ability to do otherwise?
Do our lives have meaning?
Can dating preferences be irrational or discriminatory?
Is happiness the only thing that matters to one's well-being?
We'll be meeting in the 550 Room. Contact me by text if you're having trouble finding the location.
On the Wednesdays when we're not running this event, we'll often be having similar discussions here: https://lu.ma/shortstories

events.title: Queen Budapest
events.location: Balboa Theatre, 3630 Balboa St, San Francisco, CA 94121
events.description: On July 27, 1986, Queen performed the largest-ever stadium concert at the Népstadion in Budapest in front of 80,000 ecstatic fans. The concert was part of the famed Magic Tour, which was the last time the band toured with lead singer Freddie Mercury. Now, this original concert film has been beautifully rescanned and remastered in 4K alongside a dynamic new audio mix, featuring many of Queen's favorite tracks— "Bohemian Rhapsody,” "Crazy Little Thing Called Love," "I Want To Break Free” and "We Are The Champions." With three years to go before the fall of the Berlin Wall, this was the first Western rock concert performed in a stadium behind the then Iron Curtain. It was of such significance to the Hungarian authorities and film industry that a group of the country’s top film cameramen and technicians were brought together to film it for posterity. events.title: Strategy as an Emotional Act: An Interactive Practice for Changemakers #SFTechWeek
events.location: 550 Laguna St, San Francisco + Full Studio
events.description:
What becomes possible when you design with emotions at the center, not around them?
Most systems change work is technically significant but often lacks an intentional emotional foundation. This 2-hour session treats that as a design challenge. We give you the tools, the frameworks, and the constraints. You bring the real material: your own experience of doing this work, the relational dynamics inside your teams, and the systems you're trying to change.
We move through four design layers: what you're actually feeling, what that creates between people, what emotional conditions make systems genuinely generative, and what all of it means when AI is part of the design.
What you'll takeaway:
Learnings on the language and embodiment of emotions.
Tangible relational tools that you can take back to your org.
Connection that can only come when you lead with vulnerability and emotion.
This event is a part of #SFTechWeek—a week of events hosted by VCs and startups to bring together the tech ecosystem. Learn more at www.tech-week.com.

events.title: How Do I Lead Through Change and Uncertainty?
events.location: 540 Laguna St, San Francisco + 540 Cafe
events.description:
Everyone wants more from you right now. Leadership wants speed, AI, new tools, more output with the same people. Your team wants clarity, a say, and a little more time. You're in the middle, doing most of the deciding, most of the communicating, most of the steadying.
This is a 90-minute working session, not a lecture. A room of managers with the same job as you, working on what's actually on your plate.
WHO IT'S FOR: Managers and team leads taking a team through AI rollouts, restructuring, new systems, fast growth, or priorities that keep shifting. People leaders holding the team's worries while still accountable for delivery.
LEAVE WITH: A clear read of where leadership, you, and your team each sit in the change, and what each one needs. One sentence to say up this week. One thing to give your team. And having been heard by people who do your job.
COME WITH: One real situation you're leading through right now. We work solo first, then in pairs where your partner listens and doesn't advise, then in small groups of five. What's said in the room stays in the room.
About InsightsOut: a San Francisco company working on the human side of AI change and leadership. Workshops for teams, managers, and people whose roles are changing; coaching for founders and leaders. https://insightsout.work
Facilitated by Nima Imani, founder and ICF-certified leadership coach who works with founders, managers, and teams on the human side of AI change.
All workshops: https://insightsout.work/events 
Coaching with Nima (Sample30-minute call): https://insightsout.work/coaching

events.title: !Laloismo! A poetic and musical reimagining of the lyrics  of Lalo Guerrero
events.location: Medicine for Nightmares, 3036 24th St, San Francisco, CA 94110
events.description: Tonight four pochos from different corners and dimensions of Aztlan come together for a poetic and rasquache reimagining of the lyrics of foundational Mexican American singer songwriter Lalo Guerrero. Featuring pendejadas, poetics, y musica from Marisol Medina-Cadena, Louis “El Panadero” Gutierrez, soledad con carne, and Josiah Flores. MC’d by the Pocho poeta Josiah Luis Alderete. This evento is part of the Lalo Guerrero Legacy Festival happening at the Freight and Salvage on November 6th and 7th and is also a PBS(Pocho Broadcasting Company) production. Louis “El Panadero” Gutierrez is a 24th street organic intellectual, Mission poet, and neighborhood archivist. His familia has owned the iconic La Reyna Bakery for over 40 years. Marisol Medina-Cadena is a fourth generation Californian; Bay Area on her mom’s side and LA County on her pop’s side. She is a San Francisco based comedian and storyteller by way of the dirty D, aka Pasadena, California. When she's not being a sad clown she's doing boring things like research and collecting intel of all things pochismo and San Pancho. As a proud member of (PBS) the Pocho Broadcast Service, she takes her duty very seriously to make audiences he-he and ha-ha. soledad con carne is an intergalactic Chicanx punk poet. They are a poet of the root that cracks the concrete on occupied Fernandeño-Tataviam Land: otherwise known as the San Fernando Valley. Part-time poet turned melodic storyteller, Chicano singer/songwriter Josiah Flores puts music to the parts of life most tend to hide from. From the foothills of south San Jose to the foggy avenues of San Francisco, he calls the Bay Area his home. Influenced by the likes of Stoney Edwards, Freddy Fender, and Willie Dunn, if one were to sit in a dimly-lit corner of their local watering hole, hunched over a beer, they would find Josiah’s songs sitting down next to them.

events.title: King Lear

events.description: King Lear by William Shakespeare Directed by Michael Socrates Moran Music composed by Paul Dresher Presented by Oakland Theater Project & New Performance Traditions In the twilight of his rule, a king sets out to divide the kingdom among his three daughters. But in mistaking flattery for love, Lear’s foolish choices usher in a new reign of domination, cruelty and collapse. As a self-styled “bastard” sets out to upend the ruling order, Lear must confront his own part in the kingdom’s downfall. Can he transform in time to reclaim what is sacred before the clown show becomes the new order? Ritual and spectacle collide in Michael Socrates Moran ’s bold, contemporary staging of Shakespeare’s epic tragedy, featuring a cast of 30, including the “irrepressible” ( SF Chronicle ) J Jha ( Angels in America, Mahābhārata ) as Lear; renowned performer, singer, and writer Rinde Eckert ( Ghost Quartet ) as The Fool; and music composed by Paul Dresher and performed live by the Dresher | Davel Invented Instrument Duo .

events.title: Jonah Raskin, Marc Zegans, Larry Beckett read some of their poetry, and Jonah introduces his latest book
events.location: Bird & Beckett Books & Records, 653 Chenery Street, San Francisco
events.description: Jonah Raskin introduces his most recent book of cultural writings, Keeping the Beat (Regent Press, 2026), a collection of original, groundbreaking reviews and essays about the writers of the Beat Generation, plus their contemporaries and fellow travelers. Jonah’s five and a half decades’ output of short and long-form literary/cultural criticism and journalism has traced three-quarters of a century of outsider American socio-political life, with an eye on the American imperial project that frames it. Lately, he’s also produced a fair amount of poetry. Jonah will bring some of his poems to the table to join with poets Marc Zegans and Larry Beckett, who will present some of their own poetry, principally recent work. Larry will also sing a poem of Paul Verlaine, in his own translation, accompanying the poem/song on piano. The Book of Immaculate Perception / Madrigals is a tête-bêche (flip book) by Marc Zegans and Larry Beckett in which two poem cycles, “Madrigals” by Beckett and “The Book of Immaculate Perception” by Zegans can be read from their respective fronts-to-backs in a single spine format. The project developed when Marc sent Larry the manuscript for “The Book of Immaculate Perception,” a micro-chap tracing the circle from raw awareness through life mediated by language to simple awareness regained, and Larry, responding enthusiastically, shared with Marc a thematically resonant series of madrigals inspired by his daughter that trace the life arc forward from conception. The confluence between these poem-cycles extends beyond shared narrative lines to independently formed yet common imagery and complementary methods of composition. In each body of work, you will find compactness of speech, form that liberates line, and an easy flow from poem-to-poem that animates and enriches the experience of reading these two sets of poems in each other’s company. Larry Beckett’s poetry ranges from songs to blank sonnets and 100-page narrative works. His lyric, “Song to the Siren,” is a modern standard. In the years since, he’s written the postmodern epic, “American Cycle,” including the long narratives Paul Bunyan, Wyatt Earp, Amelia Earhart, and he has reinvented Sonnets. “The Book of Merlin” is a recovery and translation of the 6th-century Brythonic poet, and “Romances Without Words / In Solitary” is the first translation of the prison manuscript of Paul Verlaine. “Beat Poetry” is a study of the poets and poetry of the fifties San Francisco Renaissance. These madrigals are to a child from conception on. They’re dedicated to his daughter, Susannah Beckett. Marc Zegans’s seven collections of poems include Lyon Street (Bamboo Dart Press, 2022) and The Snow Dead (Červená Barva Press, 2020). Ghost Book (Kite String Press, 2024), a fine art photo book collaboration with photographer Tsar Fedorsky, is held in the special collections of the Boston Athenaeum, the Getty Research Institute, Yale University’s Haas Family Arts Library, Haverford College, the Peabody Essex Museum, and others. Marc reviews poetry for Liberated Words in his column, “On the Cutting Edge.” Films based on Marc’s poems appear regularly at festivals around the world. He lives by the coast in Northern California.

Tea, Qi Gong & Longevity-Minded Conversation
After a full day—and almost a full week—of building, pitching, networking, and talking AI, come give your brain a break and your body a little attention.
Join us for a relaxed evening of tea, gentle Qi Gong, and unhurried conversation with ambitious people who also care about wellness and longevity. Along the way, pick up a few simple ideas for helping your body handle stress, recover, and stay effective under pressure.
We may be joined by a Chinese medicine practitioner offering optional mini consultations—a glimpse into how Chinese medicine understands your individual constitution and patterns. Come meet thoughtful people, slow down for a moment, and leave feeling clearer, more grounded, and better ready to keep building ambitious things.

Hosted by Yifei https://www.instagram.com/healwithyifei/, a data scientist based in Silicon Valley and a second-generation Traditional Chinese Medicine practitioner. I’m building a community around longevity—sharing practical ways to understand your body, stay well under pressure, and reconnect with your creative mind.
This event is a part of #SFTechWeek—a week of events hosted by VCs and startups to bring together the tech ecosystem. Learn more at www.tech-week.com.

events.title: Angela Johal: Intersecting Colour
events.location: Slate Contemporary Gallery, 5510 College Ave, Oakland
events.description: Join us at SLATE Contemporary Gallery on Saturday, October 10 from 4-6pm for an artist reception in celebration of our newest exhibition, “Angela Johal: Intersecting Colour.” This exhibition invites viewers to explore how hue and tone interact across vividly painted color fields. Johal approaches each painting as a puzzle to solve, seeking balance among dichotomous realms—physical and spiritual, light and dark, vivid and subdued—creating compositions that reveal how each color shifts, responds to, and is transformed by those around it. Steeped in color theory, Johal’s work is deeply informed by the human eye’s natural passage through dimension. This exhibition features abstracted geometric compositions that, when meditated on, transform into natural landscapes, animal-like forms, and shifting light.

events.description: $12 adv / $15 door Co-presented with Left Margin Lit and Vintage Berkeley Back by popular demand, with an all-new lineup! events.title: King Lear
events.location: Z Space's Steindler Stage
events.description: King Lear by William Shakespeare Directed by Michael Socrates Moran Music composed by Paul Dresher Presented by Oakland Theater Project & New Performance Traditions In the twilight of his rule, a king sets out to divide the kingdom among his three daughters. But in mistaking flattery for love, Lear’s foolish choices usher in a new reign of domination, cruelty and collapse. As a self-styled “bastard” sets out to upend the ruling order, Lear must confront his own part in the kingdom’s downfall. Can he transform in time to reclaim what is sacred before the clown show becomes the new order? Ritual and spectacle collide in Michael Socrates Moran ’s bold, contemporary staging of Shakespeare’s epic tragedy, featuring a cast of 30, including the “irrepressible” ( SF Chronicle ) J Jha ( Angels in America, Mahābhārata ) as Lear; renowned performer, singer, and writer Rinde Eckert ( Ghost Quartet ) as The Fool; and music composed by Paul Dresher and performed live by the Dresher | Davel Invented Instrument Duo .

events.title: Artist Talk – Patricia Guthrie: Get Up Stand Up
events.location: Mercury 20 Gallery, 475 25th Street, Oakland
events.description: One purpose of art is to support and communicate political messages. Using color, letters, and shapes, Patricia Guthrie’s abstract quilts deliver political messages relating to the government, international relationships, and global warming. She creates artwork using cotton fabric, wool batting, dyes, and machine stitching. Bio: After retiring as a professor and department chair of Human Development and Women’s Studies at California State University East Bay, Patricia Guthrie decided to actively engage in the visual arts. She began taking community-based art classes: drawing, photography, quilt making, and printing on fabric. Quilt making and all its aspects has become her passion. Guthrie hopes her quilts encourage viewers to move beyond art that is merely pleasing to the eye to seek a deeper meaning. Her work has been shown nationally and internationally including Schweinfurth Memorial, Art Center, Auburn, New York; International Quilt Museum, Lincoln, Nebraska; Philadelphia Museum of Art, Philadelphia, Pennsylvania; and Tuch + Technik Museum, Neumunster, Germany. This is Guthrie’s second solo show at Mercury 20 Gallery. Gallery Hours: Friday and Saturday, 12 – 5 pm (and by appointment) Opening Reception: Saturday, September 12, 3 – 5 pm ﻿Oakland Art Murmur / First Friday: October 2, 5 – 9 pm

events.title: Artist Talk – Tara Esperanza: Close to Home
events.location: Mercury 20 Gallery, 475 25th Street, Oakland
events.description: Tara Esperanza, Guardians, 2026, acrylic-on-panel, 20” x 16”, Photo courtesy of the artist Whether painted in California or Oaxaca, the works in Close to Home begin with the same impulse: to slow down and look closely. Working on a more intimate scale than in her previous work, Tara Esperanza found herself drawn to quiet moments of observation, where familiar plants reveal unexpected beauty through color, form, and light. Created between two places that have become part of her life, these paintings are less about geography than about attention. Though rooted in different landscapes, each painting is shaped by the same curiosity and sense of wonder inspired by the resilience and sculptural elegance of plants. For many years, succulents have been Esperanza’s way of exploring themes of adaptation, diversity, and endurance. Through this body of work, the smaller scale invites viewers to slow down, look closely, and discover that what is closest to us often has the most to reveal. Bio: Tara Esperanza resides in Oakland, California, where succulents thrive year-round. When she is not painting, she enjoys running and capturing images that later inspire her work. Esperanza earned a BFA in Painting, graduating cum laude from the University of Massachusetts Dartmouth, and studied plein air painting in Brittany, France. A representational painter inspired by nature, she has dedicated years to portraying the remarkable beauty and diversity of succulents. She has been a member of Mercury 20 Gallery in Oakland, CA, since 2020. Her work has been shown at the Women’s United Art Movement Virtual Gallery, as well as numerous group exhibitions. In 2025, Esperanza received Best of Show at the Annual National Juried Painting Exhibition at Emerald Springs Art Center in Oregon. Her paintings have been featured in Create! Magazine, New Visionary Magazine, and other publications, and are held in private collections throughout the United States. events.title: Artist Talks: Present Figures – Curated by Laura Malone
events.location: Mercury 20 Gallery, 475 25th Street, Oakland
events.description: Laura Malone, Carnivale, Oil on Linen, 60” x 48”, 2021, Photo courtesy of the artist Present Figures brings together five California painters whose works exist within the figurative language of portraiture, simultaneously expanding and disrupting it. Centered around themes of intimacy, boundaries, and embodied emotion, each artist takes an individual approach to media, scale, and the capacity of the human form to be both a site of identity and a vessel of metaphor. Engaging in profound considerations of what it is to be human—our physicality, sense of self, relationships, consciousness, and creativity, these artists invite us to engage with these shifting, eternal questions and reflect on our own experiences—be they practical, peaceful, disturbing, humorous, fragmented, spiritual, or otherworldly. As individuals, choices that begin with who and what to portray later manifest in stylistic and material communiquès that boldly and poetically reveal themselves to the world. Collectively, the psychologically charged spectrum of the group reminds us of the myriad ways our sentience can be narrated. Like Anais Nin said, “We don’t see things as they are, we see them as we are.” Bio: With Present Figures, Laura Malone expands her practice to curation. Malone invited four artists to show alongside her, chosen for their unique and diverse approaches to representing the figure: two Southern California artists — Cindy Craig and Shannon Rae Fincke — and two from the Bay Area — Nina Katz and Heidi Brueckner. Collectively their work has been shown across the globe in Europe, Asia, and the United States. Malone’s artwork was featured in The Crocker Kingsley National Art Competition and included in “Disrupted Realism,” juried by John Seed, who wrote the book of the same name. Malone currently resides in Oakland, CA and has been a member of Mercury 20 since 2023. Gallery Hours: Friday and Saturday, 12 – 5 pm (and by appointment) Opening Reception: Saturday, September 12, 3 – 5 pm ﻿Oakland Art Murmur / First Friday: October 2, 5 – 9 pm

events.description:
No one knows your heart like a sister.
We're celebrating the release of Sense & Sensibility, in theaters October 16, with a reading party built for sisters, best friends, and everyone in between.
From Focus Features and Working Title comes an irresistible new take on Jane Austen's iconic Sense and Sensibility: a charming, witty, and deeply relatable story of love and sisterhood starring Daisy Edgar-Jones and Esmé Creed-Miles.
Here's what to expect:
Settle in and read your new copy of Sense and Sensibility (or bring whatever else you're currently reading)
Pause for an exclusive first look at the film itself, screened just for our readers
Write "Letters to Your Sister," a short writing prompt and paired discussion
Enjoy a themed drink
Close out the night with conversations
We'll have 50 copies of the special movie tie-in book to give away!
We invite you to bring your book bestie! This event can be fun for a pair! Grab the Book Bestie ticket and bring your sister or your best friend with you. It's $40 for the pair, that's a 20% discount for buying together.

Reading Rhythms is a series of welcoming reading parties designed to make it easy for people to gather and read socially. We invite you to bring any book you want and facilitate silent reading periods, as well as 1-on-1 breakouts, and group discussions to pull on the threads of the books that everyone is engaging with.
In a world that can often feel devoid of interest and meaningful connection, we bring readers together to reconnect with our love of learning, to experience the wonder of beautiful venues and curated music, and to gather amongst all of the people who want to be in that very same room.

events.description: Pay-what-you-can for guaranteed seating; FREE to walk-ups (space depending) Sponsored by Alta Journal Co-presented with First Presbyterian Church of Oakland Poet Claudia Rankine’s work is unfailingly expansive—broadening readers’ understanding of race, social conscience, and the limits of genre. Triage, Rankine’s first book since the groundbreaking “American” trilogy (whose centerpiece, Citizen, was a 2023 Alta California Book Club selection), again defies boundaries. Here Rankine traces a decades-long friendship between two women—the narrator and the theorist—following their evolving relationship against a backdrop of ever-more-turbulent times. Here Rankine creates a politically urgent, uncategorizable mix of essay, criticism, memoir, and photography that Booklist calls “Startlingly original ... A remarkable, soul-stirring work.” In conversation with Cathy Park Hong, whose award-winning nonfiction book Minor Feelings engages intimately with Rankine’s ideas. The Alta Journal team will be on hand to introduce you to upcoming California Book Club selections, and we’ll kick things off with performances by 2026 Oakland Youth Poet Laureate Isaiah Kahn and Vice OYPL Isabel Shen. Doors at 6:30pm.

events.description: On July 27, 1986, Queen performed the largest-ever stadium concert at the Népstadion in Budapest in front of 80,000 ecstatic fans. The concert was part of the famed Magic Tour, which was the last time the band toured with lead singer Freddie Mercury. Now, this original concert film has been beautifully rescanned and remastered in 4K alongside a dynamic new audio mix, featuring many of Queen's favorite tracks— "Bohemian Rhapsody,” "Crazy Little Thing Called Love," "I Want To Break Free” and "We Are The Champions." With three years to go before the fall of the Berlin Wall, this was the first Western rock concert performed in a stadium behind the then Iron Curtain. It was of such significance to the Hungarian authorities and film industry that a group of the country’s top film cameramen and technicians were brought together to film it for posterity. This film can be used with loyalty cards or our 2026 annual CinemaSF passes saturday, September 10 7 PM

events.title: Goldenvoice Presents USA & Canada Tour 2026 Palace with Rollo Doherty
events.location: The Warfield, 982 Market St, San Francisco, CA 94102
events.description:
PALACE ARE BACK WITH “KID” AND MASSIVE TOUR OF USA + CANADA

Palace have been making music together for over a decade. What started out as carefree jam sessions between Leo Wyndham, Rupert Turner and Matt Hodges in an airless studio in North London has burgeoned into a project that has amassed a global audience more akin to a community than a fanbase.

Their early EPs - Lost In The Night (2014) and Chase The Light (2015) - were recorded in the band’s beloved aforementioned studio, The Arch, and established a DIY ethos that remains intrinsic to the spirit of the band to this day. Four albums followed; So Long Forever (2016), Life After (2019), Shoals (2022) and Ultrasound (2024): each one a musical exploration of a particular feeling in a particular place during a particular time; ranging from grief and the loss of a relationship to the emergence of new love and light. Consequently, it's not easy to sonically classify Palace. Their sound varies from the atmospheric and ethereal to the more grounded notes of Blues and Americana, yet in every song there is still something remarkably identifiable as Palace: an ineffability to the feelings conjured up by the music. In a word, transcendent. Perhaps it is this feeling of transcendence which resonates so deeply with their supporters; loyal fans who, by the time Palace had made their Coachella debut in 2024, welcomed them home to a sold-out show at London’s Hammersmith Apollo.

In early 2025, Palace took a career leap that harkens back to their DIY origin. They released the Greyhound EP on their own label, Palace Presents - a collective they'd started in 2016 as a monthly night at The George Tavern in East London, which had quietly grown into something more intentional. A positive and protected space as Leo described it, away from the usual constraints of the music industry. The EP followed a sold-out run across the USA and Canada to growing crowds of dedicated fans.

Kid was released in April 2026, together with the announcement of a 30 date tour of the USA and Canada in the Fall of 2026, culminating in a show at the Greek Theatre in Los Angeles. “Kid is about longing for a child an ocean away. It’s the ache we feel for our people when we’re separated from them. It doesn’t feel like a sadness or heaviness, but more an affirmation of that love, a primal release sung into the sunset as the road flies by."

The journey from an airless studio in North London to the Greek Theatre in Los Angeles is a long one, and by doing things their way, Palace have managed to arrive still recognisably, unmistakably themselves

events.description:
🎉 Public Hours at the Commons 🎉
Every Sunday, the Commons opens to the public — no membership required. Come co-work, connect, create, or just explore the space at your own pace. ✨
🕘 When: Every Sunday, 9 AM – 10 PM
📍 Where: 540 Laguna St, San Francisco (corner of Hayes & Laguna, basement level)
RSVP and we'll email you your entry code ahead of time — so you can let yourself straight in when you arrive.
──────────────────────────────
🧭 A self-guided day
Public Hours are self-guided — come in, settle in, and make the space your own. Weekends are usually unstaffed, so there's no check-in desk or guided tour. Our members are glad to answer questions about the space; for anything else — including guided tours, which we don't offer as drop-ins — email hello@thesfcommons.com ahead of time.
──────────────────────────────
🔭 Getting in
Your entry code comes by email. Once you RSVP, we'll send you a personal QR code — that's your key for the day. Keep it handy on your phone (and check spam if you don't see it).
Find us. We're at 540 Laguna St, on the corner of Hayes & Laguna. Head down the stairs beside Earthbody to the basement level — that's the Commons.
Scan your QR code at the reader to unlock the door. Hold your phone just below the Kisi reader by the door and it'll let you in.
Your access stays active all day, 9 AM – 10 PM, so you can come and go freely.
Can't find your code on the day? No problem — scan the QR posted on the door to check in and get a fresh one on the spot.
We're shoes-off 🧦 — please clean up after yourself, including dirty dishes and mugs, and use only the front entrance. Trouble getting in? Email hello@thesfcommons.com.




The Commons is a modern-day town square for communal meaning-making, personal discovery, and self-expression in the heart of San Francisco. Apply to become a member here__.

events.description: FREE, $10-$15 suggested donation Co-presented with Grace Cathedral’s The Forum “Unlike anything I have read…this book will make a mark.” —Percival Everett, Pulitzer Prize– and National Book Award–winning author. In the wake of George Floyd’s murder and the January 6 insurrection, as America seemed to be falling apart, New York Times bestseller and National Book Award finalist David Treuer decided to hold himself and his family together the only way he knew how: he sat down to write a letter. Ranging from Treuer’s upbringing on the Leech Lake reservation in Minnesota to the experiences of his parents, a Jewish Holocaust refugee and the first American Indigenous woman judge, The Savage Mind reveals the terrifying essence of our nation: frontier violence, which has defined our country, our culture, and our very selves. events.title: Designing Everyday Rituals for Extraordinary Times with Betty Ray
events.location: 550 Laguna St, San Francisco + Full Studio
events.description:
How do we give meaningful shape to the moments and transitions that matter in our lives?
Join us for an interactive Flamekeeper Workshop with Betty Ray, founder of the Center for Ritual Design, exploring how we can create rituals that help us honor important experiences, transitions, and intentions.
Ritual doesn’t have to be religious, elaborate, or handed down to us. Drawing from her work in human-centered ritual design, Betty will help us explore how simple, intentional words, actions, symbols, and gatherings can create meaning, connection, and a sense of transition.
Together, we’ll apply these ideas to concrete moments in our own lives and communities—exploring how we might design rituals for the people and spaces we care for, as well as how ritual can help the Contemplarium honor the human journeys of our neighbors.
Through conversation, reflection, and hands-on exercises, we’ll practice creating rituals that bring deeper meaning to moments that deserve to be marked.
Betty Ray is an educator, facilitator, and founder of the Center for Ritual Design. A 2020 Mira Fellow and former Director of Innovation at the George Lucas Educational Foundation, she has developed human-centered approaches to helping individuals, communities, and organizations create meaningful rituals and rites of passage.
This session is part of the Flamekeeper Workshop series and will be moderated by Seanan Fong, Founding Director of the SF Contemplarium.

events.title: Author talk: No to Nuclear with Linda Pentz Gunter and Eric Wolfe
events.location: Medicine for Nightmares, 3036 24th St, San Francisco, CA 94110
events.description: Please join us for a discussion with the author of No to Nuclear: Why Nuclear Power Destroys Lives, Derails Climate Progress and Provokes War . Linda Pentz Gunter and Eric Wolfe speak in conversation on Sunday, October 11th at 7 pm. Trump is pushing for nuclear power expansion, to enrich himself and his billionaire tech friends. But does anyone else really benefit? In No To Nuclea r, Pentz Gunter moves beyond the science and statistics, centering the stories of the Nuclear Age around the inherent colonialism and corruption of the nuclear industry and the Indigenous communities who have been preyed upon for profit and left to pay a terrible price. She takes us to Native American and First Nations communities, to the nomadic Tuareg of Niger and Aboriginal lands in Australia, where Black, Brown and Indigenous communities, far from the countries who profit, have been forced to mine the uranium that fuels the nuclear industry. She finds similar stories where atomic bombs have been tested, in the Marshall Islands and French Polynesia. And she reminds us that animals, who we disregard so cruelly, are harmed, too. Finally, the book urges us to rediscover the beauty and the miracle that is Planet Earth and to embrace justice first, if we are to have a chance to prevent the worst of the climate crisis and avoid nuclear war. Linda Pentz Gunter is the founder and executive director of the US-based non-profit Beyond Nuclear. She also created and writes for her organization's news platform, Beyond Nuclear International. A former full-time journalist, she continues to contribute feature stories to the Morning Star (UK) and Ralph Nader's Capitol Hill Citizen . Eric Wolfe has been active in peace, environment, and labor issues for 60 years. He helped organize the Clamshell Alliance in 1976 to oppose construction of the Seabrook reactors. Through his puppet show, Burnt Toast: Trouble in the Nation’s Breadbasket , he advocated for non-violent direct action against nuclear power in 20 states, including California. Acres of Clams , his feature-length documentary about the Clamshell Alliance, was released in 2024. Eric has lived in San Francisco since 1988 with his wife, science writer Susan Freinkel.
