events.title: Elephant Gym: More Real Than Dreams (with Band Member Q&A)
events.location: 4-Star Theater, 2200 Clement St, San Francisco, CA 94121
events.description: Elephant Gym successfully completed a world tour spanning 60 cities across 23 countries. However, behind this achievement lay an unseen crisis of disbandment, along with hidden conflicts and struggles. What does it truly mean to be a band? The film was first screened in October 2025 at the Kaohsiung Film Festival, one of Taiwan’s leading film festivals, and will also be shown in theaters in both Japan and Taiwan. While their world tour across 23 countries and 60 cities was a major success, the film reveals the untold story behind it—including a looming breakup crisis during its preparation, as well as the band’s internal conflicts and struggles. “If your dreams were to become reality, what price would you be willing to pay?“ Elephant Gym, an instrumental band from Kaohsiung, Taiwan, has been creating indie music since its formation in 2012. Their sound blends complex rhythms with irregular time signatures and sophisticated melodies. In Taiwan, their avant-garde musical style often raised the question: who would even listen to this? However, in 2024, they embarked on a world tour covering 23 countries and 60 shows, including three performances in the Philippines. They captivated audiences worldwide and firmly established their presence. Yet behind the glamorous stage, there were deep struggles. Between guitarist Tell Chang and bassist KT Chang—who are siblings—there were conflicts between family ties and band dynamics. Drummer Chia-Chin Tu had to make the difficult decision to leave another band. And just before the world tour, the band faced a crisis that nearly led to their breakup—filled with unseen pain and clashes. Still, they chose to believe in their music and in their bond, and continued moving forward. From a niche genre to the global stage, Elephant Gym asks through their musical journey: What is a band made of people with different backgrounds? What does it mean for people to connect? Between dreams and reality, they found their own “truth.” Come witness that answer in theaters. Band member Q&A (over Zoom) to follow the screening! events.title: Builders Night
events.location: 540 Laguna St, San Francisco + 540 Cafe
events.description:
Builders Night is a weekly space where people show up with a project, work side by side, and leave with more momentum than they could have generated alone. It exists because building can be lonely, and the hardest part is often simply showing up consistently.
The tone is focused and warm. Mostly quiet during deep work, with moments of spontaneous connection when someone gets unstuck or discovers something worth sharing. This is not a networking event or a lecture. The work itself is the center of the night.
Flow
6:30–6:45 PM: Arrival and settling in
6:45–6:55 PM: Opening circle: name, what you're working on, one intention for the night
6:55–8:30 PM: Deep work sprint: quiet, side-by-side building
8:30–9:00 PM: Share-back: what you built, learned, or got stuck on. Make an ask, offer what you know, and support each other.
Who This Is For
People working on software, hardware, businesses, creative projects, writing, design, research, art, anything you're trying to make real. Come if you want accountability, momentum, and the energy of working alongside others. First-timers and regulars both welcome.
What to Bring
Laptop, notebook, sketchbook, instrument, whatever tools your project requires. Come with something to work on, or come ready to figure out what that is.
Norms
Respect the deep work sprint by keeping conversation low during focused time. Share-back is how we learn from each other: share what you built, ask for what you need, and offer what you can. Everyone participates.
Rally (rallysf.com) is an AI builder community in SF.

events.title: When Your Role Starts Changing: A Workshop for Navigating AI Change at Work

events.description:

It is changing our roles, our value, our priorities, and sometimes our sense of identity at work.
This interactive workshop is for professionals who are feeling the shift and want space to slow down, reflect, connect, and get clear what is next.
This workshop is a facilitated space to make sense of these questions with others who are navigating similar changes in real time.
Format
Small group, intentionally limited seats
Guided reflection + paired conversation + facilitated group sensemaking
Practical integration you can take with you
Confidential space: stories stay, learning leaves
Please arrive on time. The first 10 minutes matter.
Led by Nima Imani
Nima Imani is an executive coach, founder, and technologist who works with leaders navigating uncertainty, rapid change, and the emotional demands of building.
Nima brings a background in engineering, data, AI, and leadership, combined with ontological coaching, to help people slow down, see clearly, and move forward with more clarity, confidence, and grounded action.

Unrequited yearning, alcoholism, and suppressed desires abound in this 80-minute one-act play that finally examines the forgotten life and dreams of Mrs. Lincoln, through the lens of an idiot (playwright Cole Escola).

events.description: On October 13, join Mike de la Rocha at Medicine for Nightmares in San Francisco’s Mission District for an intimate conversation with Community College Educator Lorena Gonzalez about his USA Today bestselling memoir, Sacred Lessons: Teaching My Father How to Love . Together, they’ll explore masculinity, identity, and healing generational wounds, as Mike shares what he’s learned over the past year bringing Sacred Lessons to communities across the country through his book tour and iHeartMedia-produced podcast. Mike de la Rocha is a bestselling author, entrepreneur, and leading voice in men’s healing and emotional transformation. He’s the co-founder of Revolve Impact , an award-winning creative agency merging art and activism, and Tepito Coffee , a social enterprise creating jobs for formerly incarcerated individuals in partnership with Homeboy Industries. Named one of GOOD Magazine’s top 100 people changing the world, last year Mike released his bestselling memoir, Sacred Lessons: Teaching My Father How To Love (Regalo Press / Simon & Schuster), and hosts the critically acclaimed Sacred Lessons Podcast with iHeartMedia . Lorena Gonzalez is San Francisco born and raised transnationally in SF's TL, La Mission and Michoacan Mexico. Lorena has been a Bay Area community college educator for 27+ years as a counselor, La Raza Studies and Ethnic Studies profesora. She’s passionate about uplifting cultura, community organizing and social justice work. In addition, Lorena is a 20+year Aztec danzante cultural keeper, founding member of Chicano Elegance Foundation, CDMX Chicanx Sin Fronteras community, and is also active in the lowrider scene.

events.description: FREE, $10-15 suggested donation Iron Man triathlete Swetha Amit and outdoor adventure sports veteran Yi Shun Lai–both writers as well as athletes– dig deep into the process of writing about identities and bodies shaped by their dedication to sport. Who are you, when you can no longer compete, or when competing is no longer enough? Are some extremes irrecoverable once they’ve been reached? How might one heal, or insist on being more than just a winner? What does it mean to compete in white and male-dominated sports as Asian American athletes, and how do issues of race and gender play into dominant cultural narratives around individual athletic achievement? In conversation with author and former pro-wrestler Michael Copperman. Doors at 6:00pm.

events.description: Formed in 2019, Anhad Naad Collective is a genre-defying ensemble rooted in the exploration of South Asian musical traditions and their intersections with global genres. The collective had its debut concert in 2020 in San Francisco, led by core members Divya Purohit Vyas and Jun Ishimuro (of Qb Moda Jazz). Initially, their work centered around blending South Asian raga-based music with the soulful textures of jazz, R&B, and Black musical traditions. With a flexible and evolving lineup of collaborating artists, Anhad Naad Collective has performed at notable Bay Area venues including Bird & Beckett, Integral Yoga Institute, the Golden Gate Park Bandstand, and events such as San Francisco’s Summer of Music hosted by Noise Pop. In 2023, the group expanded its focus to delve deeper into South Asian spiritual music, with a special emphasis on Sufi Qawwali traditions. Anhad Naad treats the spiritual dimension of Sufi poetry and music with deep reverence, often seeking guidance from poets and experts from Pakistan and India. Lead vocalist Divya Purohit Vyas has previously been a part of Bay Dervish in Alameda, a spiritual music collective associated with Sufi Way, led by the late Kiran Rana and Jeanne Rana. Anhad Naad Collective Current Members: • Divya Purohit Vyas – Vocals • Irum Aftab – Vocals • Vivek Anand – Vocals, Harmonium • Rajnish Kamat – Vocals • Jun Ishimuro – Flute, Digital Audio Workstation (DAW)

events.title: West Coast Beat: The SF Roots of Rolling Stone
events.location: San Francisco
events.description: $15 (includes museum admission) Sponsored by Reed Schmidt Co-presented with Counterculture Museum Today’s shiny exteriors and inscrutable billboards can’t entirely obliterate San Francisco’s defining role in literature, activism, visual arts, and, yes, music. That storied history includes the 1967 founding of Rolling Stone. As both Peter Richardson and Charles Ponce de Leon relate in recent books, for a decade (before decamping for NYC), the magazine was at the vanguard of West Coast counterculture, launching dozens of journalists’ careers and setting new standards for writing about music and culture. Where better, then, to reunite folks with first-hand knowledge of those SF roots, including Ben Fong-Torres and Marianne Partridge, than at the new Counterculture Museum? Music journalist James Sullivan will take us back in time, as together we compile a scrapbook of the music, writing, and memories that defined the magazine—and the moment. Doors at 6:30pm.

From there, Every Saturday Night pulls audiences back into the 1950s, the vibrant “Harlem of the West,” when the Fillmore pulsed with jazz, community, and possibility.

events.title: Goldenvoice Presents 50 Years of Punk | Anarchy In The U.K. Sex Pistols (Steve Jones, Paul Cook, Glen Matlock) feat. Frank Carter with Starcrawler
events.location: The Warfield, 982 Market St, San Francisco, CA 94102
events.description:
On the afternoon of his first appearance onstage with the Sex Pistols, last summer at Bush Hall, Frank Carter’s peaceful afternoon stroll on the streets of Shepherd’s Bush was interrupted by a stranger sat outside a pub. “Big shoes,” the man shouted; nothing more, nothing less.

“That’s all he said,” Carter reports. “And I just replied ‘thanks for noticing’, and off I walked. But I thought, ‘Fucking hell, we’ve not even played one note yet’. At that point I felt like I was melting. I realised I had to get my shit together here.”

As if the matter was ever in doubt, hours later, he did just that. The stranger’s assertion that anyone stepping up to the microphone with the band who terrorised a nation faces one of the tallest orders in rock and roll – make no mistake, filling big shoes requires big cojones – overlooked the fact that he was speaking to one of the few singers, and perhaps even the <

Such was its success, in fact, that this short series of concerts has blossomed into a busy diary. This year, Carter and the Pistols – drummer Paul Cook, guitarist Steve Jones and bassist Glen Matlock – are set to perform in Australia, New Zealand, Japan, the United States of America, mainland Europe, the United Kingdom, and elsewhere. They’ll headline halls and appear at festivals. In March, the group will top the bill at a Teenage Cancer Trust concert at the Royal Albert Hall, of all places. Much more of this and they’ll be playing at Buckingham Palace.

For anyone who might be wondering, they’re doing these things because, in 2025, the Pistols are sensational once more. And they’re doing it is because they want to.  “What I live by now is, if it ain’t fun, I ain’t doing it,” the always reliably blunt Steve Jones says. “I’m too fucking old to be putting up with a bunch of old shit and acting like everything’s cool just to keep the ball rolling. Those days are gone. If it ain’t fun, honestly, I’m out of here. I ain’t got the energy for any crap any more.”

The credit for bringing Frank Carter into the orbit of the Pistols belongs to Glen Matlock’s youngest son. As a member of the erstwhile group Dead!, Louis Matlock had seen the singer leading the charge while touring the UK as special guests to Frank Carter & The Rattlesnakes. Night after night, he witnessed the fearlessness of a performer who approached live music as if it were a collision sport. Big shoes be damned, if you’re looking for a singer, the son told the father, Frank’s your man.

“Louis said, the guy you need is Frank Carter,” Glen Matlock says. “So I got his number off him and we arranged to have a coffee. I didn’t know much about him but Louis was always going on about him. So we had a play with him and Paul – Steve was out of the country – and Paul liked him, as did I, so we told Steve. I also went to see the Rattlesnakes at the Roundhouse [in Camden Town], where they did two sold out nights, and I was impressed. Then Steve came over [from his home in Los Angeles] and we started rehearsing and that was it.”

Asked to nominate the exact point at which he realised that this new version of the Sex Pistols became a force to be reckoned with, Paul Cook replies that it was during the marching-boots style drum intro to Holidays In The Sun, the first song on the first night at Bush Hall. “As soon as we did Holidays… I thought, ‘Yeah, this is working,” he says. “This is going to be brilliant. This is going to be fantastic.” I was at the back there, looking at Frank with his red hair, and I was kind of getting flashbacks a little bit. I just thought, ‘Wow, this is how it was and how it should be’.”

Naturally, Carter himself needed no introduction to the Sex Pistols. Raised in a home in the satellite town of Watford that groaned from the weight of vinyl LPs, as a 14-year-old, he would listen to his father’s copy of the epochal Never Mind The Bollocks… Here’s The Sex Pistols whenever his parents were out of the house. Smitten by its irresistible mix of fury and wit, blood and thunder, like countless other artists-to-be before him, he was at once captivated. Its guiding light helped lead him to the stage, and, in time, to <

“The one thing I took from the album that I put immediately into the way I perform was just the energy of it,” Carter says. “I’ve heard records that <

So, please, let us not be in any doubt as to his credentials as an MC of chaos. In 2008, 36 years after two members of the Pistols challenged each other to a fight after discovering they were playing different songs onstage at the 100 Club, at the same venue, as the singer with Gallows, Carter chased an audience member who had thrown a pint of lager onstage up the venue’s stairs and out onto Oxford Street <

He even helped orchestrate his own Great Rock and Roll Swindle. In 2009, after Warner Bros. signed Gallows for a million quid, the group handed their new label the pummelling and furious Grey Britain, an album that seemed designed to repel the casual listener. “Britain is fucked,” Carter said at the time. “Grey Britain is all about what’s going on socially, politically and economically in the UK, and how it affects us.”

Sound familiar? As in, there is no future in England’s dreaming? Of course, in 2025, bands and artists are less inclined than they once were to sing about issues that affect and bedevil an entire nation. With social media replacing punk rock as the fastest route into the public bloodstream, rock and roll has entered an introspective phase. Just as well, then, that the Pistols’ State of the Union Address remains as pressing, and as prescient, as ever. Inevitably, in the (almost) half century that has elapsed since a pair of Millwall supporting hot dog vendors in Piccadilly Circus unwittingly provided Steve Jones with the title for his group’s sole bona fide album – “never mind the bollocks,” they would say, meaning “don’t bother with that…” – London and Britain have changed almost beyond recognition. But at street level, the problems and frustrations remain the same.

The Pistols themselves, though, <

It’s different, too, because in 2025 the group’s personnel no longer comprises elements of soap opera, or pantomime. Instead, unity and teamwork are the makings of the new machine; the cohesion of drums, bass, guitar and voice in the service of the songs. In this iteration, the rock and roll itself is allowed to shine, timeless and evergreen. There is no swindle. The people who wrote and played the music back in ’76 and ’77 are able to enjoy it anew.

“Don’t forget, the three of us learned to play together,” Glen Matlock says. “It was all pretty much at a similar level of competency when we started out. And we kind of grew together as musicians.” And now? “Put it this way,” he adds, “someone who is close to the band, I won’t say who, said it’s the first time they’ve seen us coming offstage with smiles on our faces since ’96. Which is good, because life’s too short for all that bollocks, really.”

As for what might come after the Sex Pistols have said hello and goodnight to audiences across the globe, no one is saying because no one seems to know. The promise of new music that was extinguished by a television interview with Bill Grundy and the subsequent shellshock of a young band receiving too much of everything, far too soon for anyone, may never be realised. But who can say for sure? At least for now, there’s no point in asking - you’ll get no reply.  But what we do have, for sure, is Frank Carter and the Sex Pistols whipping up a storm across the globe in a manner that is familiar but fresh, old but new. Catch it while you can, for as long as it lasts. Because we won’t see their kind again.

events.title: Somatic Healing 101: The Missing Link to Lasting Change
events.location: 550 Laguna St, San Francisco + Full Studio
events.description:
A somatic workshop to understand your nervous system, reconnect with your body, and learn practical tools for real transformation...
Have you ever known exactly what you "should" do, but still found yourself stuck in the same patterns?
Maybe you've read the books, listened to the podcasts, journaled, reflected, and tried to think your way into change. Yet anxiety, overwhelm, self-sabotage, emotional reactivity, procrastination, or feeling disconnected from yourself keep showing up.
That's because lasting transformation doesn't happen through the mind alone. It happens through the body.
In this immersive workshop, you'll learn the foundations of somatic healing and nervous system regulation, and why working with your body is often the missing piece when it comes to creating meaningful, sustainable change.
We'll explore how stress, emotions, beliefs, and protective patterns are stored in the body, and why healing becomes more effective when we include the nervous system in the process.
You'll learn:
What somatics actually is (and why it's becoming more popular)
Why mindset work alone isn't enough to create real, lasting change
How your nervous system influences your emotions, behaviors, and daily experiences
Simple somatic tools you can use to feel more grounded, present, and connected
How to work with your body instead of constantly trying to push through or override it
This workshop isn't just educational — you'll also experience somatics firsthand through guided practices, including breathwork, body awareness, grounding exercises, mindful movement, and embodiment practices designed to help you reconnect with yourself and your body's wisdom.
You'll leave with:
A clear understanding of what somatic healing is and how it works
Practical tools you can immediately integrate into daily life to finally feel more calm and present
Greater awareness of your nervous system and stress responses
Simple ways to deepen your connection to your body, emotions, and intuition
A new approach to personal growth that feels supportive, sustainable, and effective

Whether you're completely new to somatics or looking to deepen your understanding of holistic healing, this workshop will give you a strong foundation and simple practices you can return to anytime!
Please bring a journal and water bottle, and wear comfortable clothes.
NOTE: Please be on time for this session — doors will close promptly and there will be NO LATE ENTRIES!
About Anna Bolender:
Anna Bolender is a certified Somatic Embodiment & Intuitive Life Coach, Somatic Breathwork and Quantum Wellness Practitioner, Reiki Master, and lifelong student of holistic health and well-being.
Through her coaching programs and workshops, Anna guides others to return home to themselves — releasing what keeps them stuck, reconnecting with their body and inner wisdom, and creating real, lasting transformation from the inside out.
Blending somatics, energy healing, quantum wellness, and mindset work, she helps clients break free from self-sabotaging patterns, repattern their nervous system, and cultivate simple daily rituals that support a fulfilling, grounded, and aligned life.
Anna’s mission is to empower others to feel connected, alive, and radiant — no matter what life brings.
Instagram: @annaalexbee
Podcast: RADIANT YOU (available on all podcast platforms)
Website: www.annabolender.com

events.title: A 22nd-Century Conservation Ethos for California
events.location: KALW, 220 Montgomery St, Suite 100, San Francisco, CA 94104
events.description: FREE, $10-$15 suggested donation Sponsored by Heyday Books Co-presented with KALW California’s landscapes have long been shaped by deep relationships between people and place. But that relationship has changed dramatically over time, especially with the rise of European American settlement and the erasure of Traditional Ecological Knowledge. Panelists Obi Kaufmann, creator of the California Field Atlas series; Laura Cunningham, award-winning author of A State of Change; and earth scientist and professional mountain biker Dillon Osleger examine how modern society has grown increasingly estranged from the natural world. Together, they imagine a new conservation ethos—one rooted in restoration, resilience, and reciprocity—and ask what it would take for Californians to leave the state healthier, more biodiverse, and more ecologically whole at the end of the 21st century than at its beginning. Moderated by Leslie Carol Roberts. Doors at 6:30pm.

events.title: UNTOLD STORIES Opening Reception
events.location: ARTogether Center, 1200 Harrison Street, Oakland
events.description: What story gets left behind when the world decides whose memory counts? Untold Stories is our attempt to connect the dots, to trigger the memories that complete what’s been erased. As truth seekers from many different walks of life, we’ve made this exhibition a space to hold the true stories so often erased by a system that does not honor immigrants, refugees, Black Americans, queer folks, and those who carry the truth close. This exhibition allows us to rest in the rememory that Toni Morrison left us in the pages of the untold stories she once uncovered. “Untold Stories” is our dedication to that work, as ARTogether’s 2026 Artist-in-Residence Mentorship Cohort: Aylin Ayee, Bronche Taylor, Donny Phan, Jacquie Verbal, Ji Young Lee, Kia Lat, Sabri Tunca, and Tea Sherman. Our work spans mixed media, painting, textile art, installation, and performance, holding space for the stories that have not yet been told. We invite you to join us in dialogue about Untold Stories. **Everything related to this exhibition is fueled by human creativity; no artificial intelligence is condoned.

events.title: Heaven Looks Like Us: Palestinian Poetry
events.location: Telegraph Hill Books, 1501 Grant Ave, San Francisco
events.description: FREE, $10-$15 suggested donation Part of Words Around the World Sponsored by Center for the Art of Translation Poetry has always served as a mode of resistance in Palestinian culture. In defiance of dispossession and decades of military siege, of a nakba that never ended, of historical and cultural obfuscation, of unrelenting violence and thousands of martyred people, the “power to narrate,” as Edward Said wrote, remains a necessary tool for self-determination. As Palestinian history remains haunted by exile, violence, and grief, there’s more here that’s also true: queer and feminist perspectives, eco-poetry, meditations on love and time, and lineages of protest. These poems reclaim that power to narrate, bridging borders, languages, and generations to forge new conversations around resistance and liberation. Featuring Heaven Looks Like Us anthology contributors Zeina Hashem Beck, Janine Mogannam, Deema Shehabi, Jen Siraganian, Priscilla Wathington, and Omar Zahzah. Doors at 6:30pm.

events.description: Other Dimensions in Sound is our Friday music series curated and hosted by Boohaabian multi reed player extraordinare David Boyce. Tonight’s double dose of sonic sustenance is being brought to you by Wandering Clouds & Warm Spell Wandering Clouds is made up of Jaroba on tenor sax and bass clarinet; Kersti Abrams on alto sax and flute; Mike Villarreal on drums; and Eli Pontecorvo on bass. We have collectively and individually been wandering through a variety of sonic worlds over the years, and come together periodically to improvise music reflecting our commonalities and differences. Warm Spell is a vehicle and seeks to melt the experience of their listeners into a shared consciousness for a rare moment in the everyday of space and time, to recognize the possibilities of a life based on collectivity and playfulness. Warm Spell is an improv group consisting of Bay Area musicians who come together infrequently to jive. They will often be: vocalist/percussion (Marina Lazzara), Bass (Brian Lucas), Guitar (Tammy Fortin), Farfisa (JLee), Violin (Kevin Van YserLoo), Richard Marriot (Conch Shell, Flute, Trumpet).

events.description: A Word for Word and Z Space production · Stories by E.L. Doctorow & Tatyana Tolstaya Presented by Word for Word and Z Space Directed by Rotimi Agbabiaka In “Assimilation” by E. L. Doctorow, Ramon is offered a promotion and cash which could pay for grad school – if he agrees to enter a green-card marriage with his boss’s niece. When he agrees, he gets more than he bargained for. “Smoke and Shadows” by Tatyana Tolstaya centers on a Russian professor living in the U.S., navigating her professional life, her intimate relationships, and the mysteries of culture. Told with Tolstaya’s sharp, restrained wit, the story zeros in on the experience of living in a new culture, and the confusions and imbalance that can cause. What does it mean to assimilate? These two writers offer two very different perspectives.

events.description: Mercury Prize and 6-time BRIT nominated singer and songwriter Jessie Ware returns with a phenomenal new album that establishes why Ware is one of the most revered, admired and loved voices at the forefront of British Pop music. That! Feels Good! is the follow-up to Ware’s fourth studio album, 2020’s What’s Your Pleasure . There’s a delicious feeling of freedom to be found throughout Jessie Ware’s new album That! Feels Good! This blissfully joyful record, underscored by a frankly sensational vocal from Ware, radiates self-determination, boundless energy, supremely good vibes and a generosity of spirit. And groove. So. Held during Filipino American History Month, FilBookFest brings together an exciting array of writers, scholars, and creatives from across the globe, including the U.S., Canada, and the Philippines, to the iconic San Francisco Public Library. Keynote speakers for 2026 include Randy Ribay, author of Patron Saints of Nothing & Nest of Tongues; Dr. Robyn Rodriguez, author of Contemporary Asian American Activism: Building Movements for Liberation; and Professor M. Evelina Galang, author of When the Hibiscus Falls and recipient of the inaugural PAWA Lifetime Achievement Award. Other featured authors include Mia Alvar, Marivi Soliven, Mia Manansala (US); Yvette Tan, Jet Tagasa and Jaya Jacobo (Philippines); Candy Gourlay (UK), as well as children’s authors Tracy Badua (US) and Analene Go (Canada). The festival will also feature a bustling marketplace with tables from PAWA Books, Arkipelago Books, Eastwind Books, and Bel Canto Books. events.description: $16 Co-presented with ZYZZYVA and the Roxie For this festival installment of our year-round film series, Andrew Sean Greer introduces a special screening of Amarcord, the dramatic comedy directed by Federico Fellini. Fellini recreates his hometown of Rimini in this carnivalesque film, where the director satirizes his childhood. Winner of an Academy Award for best foreign-language film, Amarcord remains one of the director’s best-loved creations, beautifully weaving together Giuseppe Rotunno’s colorful cinematography, Danilo Donati’s extravagant costumes and sets, and Nino Rota’s nostalgia-tinged score. events.description: FREE, $10-$15 suggested donation Co-presented with Museum of the African Diaspora Dorothy Lazard’s celebrated 2023 memoir What You Don’t Know Will Make a Whole New World traced the beloved Oakland librarian’s coming of age through books. Along the way, she makes a powerful case for the essential role of the public library as a pillar of democratic ideals, and she crafts a tribute to the library workers who have devoted their careers to supporting intellectual freedom as well as to the countless Oaklanders whom she had the privilege of serving. events.title: A Girl Walks Home Alone at Night
events.location: Balboa Theatre, 3630 Balboa St, San Francisco, CA 94121
events.description: Strange things are afoot in Bad City. The Iranian ghost town, home to prostitutes, junkies, pimps, and other sordid souls, is a place that reeks of death and hopelessness, where a lonely vampire is stalking the towns most unsavory inhabitants. But when boy meets girl, an unusual love story begins to blossom...blood red. The first Iranian Vampire Western, Ana Lily Amirpour's debut feature A Girl Walks Home Alone at Night basks in the sheer pleasure of pulp. A joyful mash-up of genre, archetype and iconography, its prolific influences span spaghetti westerns, graphic novels, horror films, and the Iranian New Wave. Amped by a mix of Iranian rock, techno and Morricone-inspired riffs, its airy, anamorphic, black-and-white aesthetic and artfully drawn-out scenes combine the simmering tension of Sergio Leone with the surrealism of David Lynch. events.title: Lalo Guerrero Listening Party and Platica with Jesse "Chuy" Varela
events.location: Medicine for Nightmares, 3036 24th St, San Francisco, CA 94110
events.description: Join us tonight for a listening party and platica celebrating the music of foundational Mexican American singer/songwriter Lalo Guerrero hosted by the Bay’s favorite DJ Jesse “Chuy” Varela! Chuy will be playing us some of his favorite Lalo rolitas for us, as well as discussing the importance of Lalo’s legacy in the Latine musical cannon. Jesse ‘Chuy’ Varela serves as Program and Music Director at KCSM JAZZ 91, the Bay Area’s Jazz radio station. 2025 marks Chuy’s 42nd anniversary in radio. He has worked at KBBF – Santa Rosa, KPFA – Pacifica Radio in Berkeley, KJAZ Radio in Alameda, KBRG – Spanish Language Radio - San Jose, and KCSM JAZZ 91 , as well as a news reporter/stringer for National Public Radio, Latino USA, Radio Bilingüe , and other radio entities. He has served as a consultant for the Smithsonian Institute in Washington DC, Oakland Museum of California, The DeYoung Museum in San Francisco, Grammy Museum in Los Angeles, SFJAZZ, and numerous other organizations. Varela is also a freelance journalist who has written for the San Francisco Chronicle, The Eastbay Express, Latin Beat Magazine, Jazz Times Magazine, El Tecolote Newspaper, and numerous other publications as well as writing liner notes for Verve Records, Concord Records, Arhoolie Records, High Tone Records , and other numerous indie labels. Varela has lectured and taught at UC Berkeley, UC Santa Cruz, Stanford University, City College of San Francisco, The International Association of Jazz Educators Conference, The University of the Sagrado Corazon in Puerto Rico, Habana Jazz Festival, The Kiwanis Club of Oakland , and numerous other schools and organizations. He also serves on the board of directors of The Oaktown Jazz Workshop, a jazz education program for young people in Oakland, as well as a mentor for The Berkeley High School Jazz Band Honors Project. Currently Jesse ‘Chuy;’ Varela hosts The Latin Jazz Show on Sundays from 2pm-6pm and Jazz In The Afternoon Mon.-Weds, 2pm-6pm. In May 2024, Jesse ‘Chuy” Varela celebrated 40 years hosting The Latin Jazz Show, which he began hosting at KJAZ in 1984. This event is part of the Lalo Guerrero Legacy Festival happening at the Freight & Salvage on November 6th & 7th.

events.title: Jean-Baptiste Phou: Coming Out of My Skin
events.location: Telegraph Hill Books, 1501 Grant Ave, San Francisco
events.description: FREE, $10-$15 suggested donation Part of Words Around the World Sponsored by Center for the Art of Translation Co-presented with Villa Albertine Having grown up as a Cambodian immigrant in France, Jean-Baptiste Phou has long explored the challenges and contradictions of the Asian diaspora experience throughout his artistic career. However, up until now, he’s always been careful not to raise issues of sexuality—in particular, his homosexuality. In his recent memoir, Coming Out of My Skin, the artist shifts his focus to examining the role his ethnic origin has played in the construction of his sexual identity and his romantic relationships in a predominantly white environment. An astute observer of the various ways in which his body has been perceived, Phou asks: how does a marginalized person develop emotionally and build, reclaim, and express their sexuality? How does this inform the experience of a queer Asian person navigating predominantly white cultural spaces? In conversation with César Cadabes, Artistic Director for the GLBTQ Asian Pacific Alliance (GAPA) Theatre. Doors at 6:30pm

events.title: Picturing the Past: Graphic Novelists on History and Memory
events.location: Mrs. Dalloway's, 2904 College Ave, Berkeley CA 94705
events.description: FREE, $10-$15 suggested donation Sponsored by Berkeleyside Through memoir, history, fiction, or a combination, these four talented creators use cartoons to give readers a vivid glimpse into the past. Frederick Noland shares the epic story of Major Taylor, the “world’s fastest man,” a global cycling sensation despite the incessant racism the Black athlete encountered. In Armaveni, Nadine Takvorian draws on her own family history to relate the heartbreaking history of the Armenian genocide. Emil Wilson’s The Nightingales blends fact and fiction in a personal story of the 1980s AIDS crisis. And Maria van Lieshout’s graphic novel Song of a Blackbird pairs the stories of two Dutch teens, one contemporary and one bearing witness to Nazi atrocities. Brief visual presentations will be followed by a conversation led by graphic memoirist Briana Loewinsohn. Doors at 6:30pm.

Be transported to San Francisco’s Fillmore District—beginning in the present day, where the echoes of a once-thriving Black neighborhood still shape the streets. From there, Every Saturday Night pulls audiences back into the 1950s, the vibrant “Harlem of the West,” when the Fillmore pulsed with jazz, community, and possibility.

Following two Black boys—one in each era—the musical explores home, belonging, and resilience, revealing how the Fillmore’s past and present are connected by displacement, gentrification, and the enduring fight to stay rooted in the community.

Inspired by true events, this boisterous and heartfelt new work commissioned and presented by San Francisco Bay Area Theatre Company (SFBATCO) celebrates a historic neighborhood while asking urgent questions about who gets to remain in the city today.

events.location: The Warfield, 982 Market St, San Francisco, CA 94102
events.description: Mercury Prize and 6-time BRIT nominated singer and songwriter Jessie Ware returns with a phenomenal new album that establishes why Ware is one of the most revered, admired and loved voices at the forefront of British Pop music. That! Feels Good! is the follow-up to Ware’s fourth studio album, 2020’s What’s Your Pleasure . There’s a delicious feeling of freedom to be found throughout Jessie Ware’s new album That! Feels Good! It’s the sound of a person letting loose and letting go and encouraging everyone else to do the same. This blissfully joyful record, underscored by a frankly sensational vocal from Ware, radiates self-determination, boundless energy, supremely good vibes and a generosity of spirit. And groove. So. Much. Groove. Yet That! Feels Good! also resounds with an ebullient ease; an unforced and unhurried spirit runs throughout each and every one of the 10 tracks.

events.description: A Close Encounter of the Undead Kind! Is it a desperate cry for help…or something far more sinister? After landing on the shadowy planet, the crew members clash with a horde of disembodied, soul-snatching aliens with a diabolical plan beyond their worst nightmares! A dazzling mixture of nerve-shredding suspense, eye-popping science fiction and full-blooded horror from the maestro of the macabre, Mario Bava (Black Sunday, Black Sabbath), Planet of the Vampires inspired decades of space-age shockers and now proudly stands as one of the most electrifying, visually stunning cult classics from Italian cinema’s golden age. events.title: The Commons Public Hours ☕
events.location: 540 Laguna St, San Francisco + Full Space
events.description:
🎉 Public Hours at the Commons 🎉
Every Sunday, the Commons opens to the public — no membership required. Come co-work, connect, create, or just explore the space at your own pace. ✨
🕘 When: Every Sunday, 9 AM – 10 PM
📍 Where: 540 Laguna St, San Francisco (corner of Hayes & Laguna, basement level)
RSVP and we'll email you your entry code ahead of time — so you can let yourself straight in when you arrive.
──────────────────────────────
🧭 A self-guided day
Public Hours are self-guided — come in, settle in, and make the space your own. Weekends are usually unstaffed, so there's no check-in desk or guided tour. Our members are glad to answer questions about the space; for anything else — including guided tours, which we don't offer as drop-ins — email hello@thesfcommons.com ahead of time.
──────────────────────────────
🔭 Getting in
Your entry code comes by email. Once you RSVP, we'll send you a personal QR code — that's your key for the day. Keep it handy on your phone (and check spam if you don't see it).
Find us. We're at 540 Laguna St, on the corner of Hayes & Laguna. Head down the stairs beside Earthbody to the basement level — that's the Commons.
Scan your QR code at the reader to unlock the door. Hold your phone just below the Kisi reader by the door and it'll let you in.
Your access stays active all day, 9 AM – 10 PM, so you can come and go freely.
Can't find your code on the day? No problem — scan the QR posted on the door to check in and get a fresh one on the spot.
We're shoes-off 🧦 — please clean up after yourself, including dirty dishes and mugs, and use only the front entrance. Trouble getting in? Email hello@thesfcommons.com.




The Commons is a modern-day town square for communal meaning-making, personal discovery, and self-expression in the heart of San Francisco. Apply to become a member here__.

events.description: FREE Part of Words Around the World Co-presented with Friends of the San Francisco Public Library, the Filipino American Center at SFPL, PAWA, and the San Francisco Public Library The Filipino American International Book Festival (FilBookFest) returns in October for its 8th iteration, continuing its legacy as the largest Filipino American literary festival in the United States. Held during Filipino American History Month, FilBookFest brings together an exciting array of writers, scholars, and creatives from across the globe, including the U.S., Canada, and the Philippines, to the iconic San Francisco Public Library. Keynote speakers for 2026 include Randy Ribay, author of Patron Saints of Nothing & Nest of Tongues; Dr. Robyn Rodriguez, author of Contemporary Asian American Activism: Building Movements for Liberation; and Professor M. Evelina Galang, author of When the Hibiscus Falls and recipient of the inaugural PAWA Lifetime Achievement Award. Other featured authors include Mia Alvar, Marivi Soliven, Mia Manansala (US); Yvette Tan, Jet Tagasa and Jaya Jacobo (Philippines); Candy Gourlay (UK), as well as children’s authors Tracy Badua (US) and Analene Go (Canada). The festival will also feature a bustling marketplace with tables from PAWA Books, Arkipelago Books, Eastwind Books, and Bel Canto Books. For a full program schedule and author lineup, visit filbookfestival.org.

events.location: City Lights, 261 Columbus Ave, San Francisco
events.description: FREE Co-presented with City Lights How to Exi(s)t: A Poet’s Memoir is an experiment in nonlinear autobiography by the author of the American Book Award–winning Book of the Other, Truong Tran. Beginning in the present—at a writing residency in the aftermath of this success—How to Exi(s)t unpeels the layers between present and past in bursts of brief poetic essays. Unsparing, even caustic in its insistence on racism as a dominant note of American life, but marked by surprising tenderness and humor, How to Exi(s)t is a compelling portrayal of Tran’s pedagogical philosophy as well as an interrogation of a poetic language that conceals as much as it reveals. In conversation with Garrett Caples.

events.title: Menopause Extravaganza: The Science and Culture of a Subject No One Used to Want to Talk About
events.location: Gray Area Theater, 2665 Mission St, San Francisco 94110
events.description: $10 advance / $15 door Co-presented with Gray Area Theater Menopause, a natural consequence of aging, has for centuries been alternately ignored and belittled, seen mostly through a male lens of bafflement, repugnance, and boilerplate misogyny. Now, however, a growing body of women and their doctors are rejecting this traditional view, developing new therapies and strategies as well as ways to appreciate the new freedoms it can offer. This energizing (and overdue) afternoon features Dr. Louann Brizendine, author of The Female Brain, reading from her forthcoming Your Brain on Menopause and joining other panelists in a conversation led by Keli Dailey: Dr. Sarah Isquick (a colleague of Dr. Sally Greenwald, featured in the recent New Yorker article “The Billionaires’ Vagina Club”), psychiatrist Dr. Alecia Greenlee, and menopause doula Lasara Firefox Allen, author of Genderqueer Menopause. events.location: 4-Star Theater, 2200 Clement St, San Francisco, CA 94121
events.description: DELLAMORTE DELLAMORE: CEMETERY MAN (1994) “I’d give my life to be dead…” From director Michele Soavi ( The Church , Stage Fright ) comes a macabre masterpiece, 1994’s CEMETERY MAN , also known aptly as DELLAMORTE DELLAMORE (Of Death, Of Love). This Italian-French-German co-production stars British actor Rupert Everett ( My Best Friend’s Wedding) as Franceso Dellamorte, a graveyard keeper tasked with putting the dead that rise each night. Despite his gristly job, Dellamorte is a romantic at heart. But is he free to find love, or is fate bound to something far darker? And what does the Angel of Death have to do with all of it? Inspired by Tziano Sclavi’s novel Dellamorte Dellamore and his comic character Dylan Dog (who was visually based on Everett), this film is equal parts scary, comedic, and sexy, with surprising surreal and philosophical developments as the plot develops. A must see film, straight from the cold expanse of Hell to ring in Halloween! MEDIA MELTDOWN MOVIE MADHOUSE Gender jesters Piranha Psychotronica and Kafka X bring you a new experience in cinematic depravity… Media Meltdown Movie Madhouse! Prepare yourself to enter into a world of face-flaying forgotten and forsaken films… Made-for-TV, Direct-to-Video, VCR games, underground cinema, and more wiley weirdness than your minds can handle! In a world dominated by AI, CGI, mega streaming platforms, and cinematic universes, Media Meltdown celebrates the amateur, the low-budget, the handmade, the experimental, and the weird! Commit yourself every 3rd Sunday to … MEDIA MELTDOWN MOVIE MADHOUSE! For our Annual Pass Members and Loyalty Card Holders: Tickets for this film can be acquired in-person at the Box Office with loyalty cards or our Annual CinemaSF passes on the day of the show while supplies last. events.title: Builders Night
events.location: 540 Laguna St, San Francisco + 540 Cafe
events.description:
Builders Night is a weekly space where people show up with a project, work side by side, and leave with more momentum than they could have generated alone. It exists because building can be lonely, and the hardest part is often simply showing up consistently.
The tone is focused and warm. Mostly quiet during deep work, with moments of spontaneous connection when someone gets unstuck or discovers something worth sharing. This is not a networking event or a lecture. The work itself is the center of the night.
Flow
6:30–6:45 PM: Arrival and settling in
6:45–6:55 PM: Opening circle: name, what you're working on, one intention for the night
6:55–8:30 PM: Deep work sprint: quiet, side-by-side building
8:30–9:00 PM: Share-back: what you built, learned, or got stuck on. Make an ask, offer what you know, and support each other.
Who This Is For
People working on software, hardware, businesses, creative projects, writing, design, research, art, anything you're trying to make real. Come if you want accountability, momentum, and the energy of working alongside others. First-timers and regulars both welcome.
What to Bring
Laptop, notebook, sketchbook, instrument, whatever tools your project requires. Come with something to work on, or come ready to figure out what that is.
Norms
Respect the deep work sprint by keeping conversation low during focused time. Share-back is how we learn from each other: share what you built, ask for what you need, and offer what you can. Everyone participates.
Rally (rallysf.com) is an AI builder community in SF.

events.title: A Celebration of César Vallejo's Trilce
events.location: City Lights, 261 Columbus Ave, San Francisco
events.description: FREE Part of Words Around the World Sponsored by Center for the Art of Translation Co-presented with City Lights and New York Review of Books First published in 1922, and rich in startling neologisms and other forms of verbal play, Trilce is a blazingly vivid revelation of what poetry can be, at once a love poem, a poem of erotic urgency and frustration, a poem of family life, of political fury, a lament for the dead, a work of intense privacy and an address to the world. In this new edition of Trilce from NYRB—the recipient of the prestigious Premio Valle Inclán for the best translation from Spanish into English—the translators Helen Dimos and William Rowe accompany each poem with a gloss. Their incisive commentary on these legendarily challenging poems opens them up to new understanding while inviting readers to find their own pathways to and through them.

events.description:
Come breathe, release, & reset...
Somatic Breathwork is an embodiment experience designed to take you out of your thinking mind and into the deep intelligence of your body — where true healing, clarity, and release happen. It allows your body to express and discharge stored emotions, stress, and old narratives that may be weighing you down.
Somatic Breathwork uses circular connected breathing together with rhythmic music to produce a cathartic emotional release. This release may be in the form of moving, shaking, yelling, crying, laughing, or simply deep stillness.
It gives your body the opportunity to express emotions or actions that may otherwise be unacceptable in modern social settings, allowing your nervous system to process traumas and restore balance.
Using the breath, you’ll engage your body’s innate ability to heal — sweeping out any defenses, blockages, restrictions, or pains that hold you back from showing up as your truest self.
Many participants experience profound emotional release, newfound clarity, and a grounded sense of calm even after a single session.
This experience is designed to:
Move you out of your mind and into your body's electrical network
Release stuck energy, emotions, or trauma responses
Reset your nervous system into grounded calm and clarity
Break old patterns and reconnect you to your authentic self
Increase compassion, presence, and emotional resilience
Support cathartic release in a safe, guided container
Participants often report:
Deep emotional release
More calm, peace, and clarity
Release of anger, grief, frustration, or stagnant energy
Increased presence, awareness, and intuition
Breakthrough insights about their life, patterns, and purpose
Feeling more open, soft, and connected to themselves and others
What to expect:
✨ Opening Check-In & Introduction
✨ 60-Minute Guided Somatic Breathwork Journey
✨ Integration & Optional Group Sharing
Whether you're seeking release, clarity, a reset, or simply a moment to reconnect with yourself — this session is for you.
Please bring a journal and water bottle, and wear comfortable clothes.
NOTE: Please be on time for this session — doors will close promptly and there will be NO LATE ENTRIES!
About Anna Bolender:
Anna Bolender is a certified Somatic Embodiment & Intuitive Life Coach, Somatic Breathwork and Quantum Wellness Practitioner, Reiki Master, and lifelong student of holistic health and well-being.
Through her coaching programs and workshops, Anna guides others to return home to themselves — releasing what keeps them stuck, reconnecting with their body and inner wisdom, and creating real, lasting transformation from the inside out.
Blending somatics, energy healing, quantum wellness, and mindset work, she helps clients break free from self-sabotaging patterns, repattern their nervous system, and cultivate simple daily rituals that support a fulfilling, grounded, and aligned life.
Anna’s mission is to empower others to feel connected, alive, and radiant — no matter what life brings.
Instagram: @annaalexbee
Podcast: RADIANT YOU (available on all podcast platforms)
Website: www.annabolender.com

events.title: Katie Sanders: Ortiz’s War
events.location: The Commonwealth Club of California, San Francisco
events.description: Peter Ortiz’s path to becoming the most battle-decorated member of America’s first spy agency—and one of the most decorated Marines of World War II—was unlike any other. Born in New York and raised in both California and France, he was a merchant seaman, dude ranch manager, race car driver, lion tamer, circus performer, and Hollywood stuntman and actor. As a teenager, Ortiz ran away from boarding school to join the French Foreign Legion. He fought in North Africa against Saharan tribesmen, and on the front lines against the Germans in 1940, where he was badly wounded and captured.

events.title: Brian Evenson: Phantom Limb
events.location: City Lights, 261 Columbus Ave, San Francisco
events.description: FREE, $10-15 suggested donation Co-presented with City Lights Master of literary horror Brian Evenson returns with a long-awaited follow-up to his 2016 novel, Last Days. After destroying the headquarters of an underground amputation cult, a burned and battered Kline finds himself in a holding cell. When he enlists the help of an ex-cop to commute his prison sentence, Kline inadvertently tangles with a schism of the very cult he sought to destroy. Can Kline investigate the sect’s ritualistic murder spree without getting lured into their ranks? Frigid and precise, Phantom Limb interrogates our notions of wholeness, fate, and the lengths we are willing to go to connect with a higher power. In conversation with Colin Winnette.

events.title: Alain Damasio: Horde of the Counterwind
events.location: Telegraph Hill Books, 1501 Grant Ave, San Francisco
events.description: FREE, $10–$15 suggested donation Part of Words Around the World Sponsored by Center for the Art of Translation Co-presented with Villa Albertine In 2004, Alain Damasio’s Horde of the Counterwind: An Epic Voyage to the Upper Reaches gained acclaim as France’s genre-defining sci-fi odyssey of the 21st century, inspiring the celebrated video game Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 and igniting the imaginations of millions around the world. Now, this seminal work appears in English translation for the very first time, offering even more readers the opportunity to experience a masterpiece of epic scope and visionary world-building in which twenty-three adventurers climb endlessly against the wind that plagues their desolate homeland. Their only purpose: identifying the mysterious source where eight centuries of past climbers have tried and failed. Join Damasio and Horde’s English translator, Alexander Dickow, for a conversation moderated by award-winning writer and translator Edward Gauvin. Doors at 6:30pm.

events.title: Celebrating 50 Years of Publishers Group West
events.location: Clio’s, 353 Grand Ave, Oakland
events.description: FREE, $10–15 suggested donation Sponsored by Publishers Group West From a shoestring investment of $500 in 1976, Berkeley-based Publishers Group West grew, by the turn of the century, into the US’s largest distributor of independent presses. Since then, it’s maintained its focus on resilience, innovation, and a passion for independent publishing—not to mention the value of throwing a really great party. We’ll toast to a half-century of PGW, which continues to distribute books for 150 publisher clients, including some beloved local presses. How does PGW’s history reflect the larger story of Bay Area publishing? And how can lessons learned over the past fifty years inform its future? Join PGW founder Charlie Winton, executive VP Sean Shoemaker, VP of field sales Elise Cannon, and Litquake co-founder Jack Boulware for a walk down memory lane—and stick around to buy a beverage or two from Clio’s on-site bar. Doors at 6:30pm.

As technical mishaps pile up and tempers flare, the cast battles to keep the show on track while everything around them spectacularly falls apart. Lines are forgotten, scenery refuses to cooperate, and rivalries spill onto the stage in real time. From the creators of The Play That Goes Wrong , this riotous comedy delivers nonstop mayhem, perfectly timed chaos, and the kind of theatrical disaster you have to see to believe.

events.title: Memoirs: Writing Against Silence or Erasure
events.location: Mrs. Dalloway's, 2904 College Ave, Berkeley CA 94705
events.description: FREE, $10–$15 suggested donation Co-presented with Memoir Nation These four memoirists are, in different ways, writing into spaces where their experience has been minimized, misread, or actively suppressed. Judy Juanita's California Fever Dream spans sixty years of writing focused on Black activism and feminism. In I Love You So Many, journalist Terria Smith shares lessons learned from a career sharing stories about the richness of Native people’s lives. Elena Dudum's They Told Me Back Home Would Be Beautiful is a call to action against institutional silencing and censorship. Finally, Caroline Paul has spent her career writing women into adventure narratives that historically excluded them, most recently in Why Fly. Brooke Warner and Grant Faulkner, co-founders of the Memoir Nation podcast and online community, will guide a compelling discussion on the power of this truth-telling form. Doors at 6:30pm.

events.title: Pitchapalooza
events.location: Gilman Brewing, 912 Gilman St, Berkeley
events.description: Pay what you can ($15 suggested) for guaranteed seat; FREE to walk-ups (space depending) Pitchapalooza is American Idol for books (only kinder and gentler). Twenty writers, selected at random, will pitch their book for one minute only! Judges (including The Book Doctors, Arielle Eckstut and David Henry Sterry) will help you improve your pitch, not tell you how bad it is. Judges critique everything from idea to style to marketplace potential, and authors gain concrete advice as well as a greater understanding of the publishing industry. Whether potential authors pitch themselves, or simply listen to the critiques, Pitchapalooza is educational and entertaining for one and all. At evening’s end, the judges will pick a winner. Like the dozens of Pitchapalooza winners who have gone from talented amateurs to professionally published authors, this lucky participant will receive an introduction to an agent or publisher. Doors at 6:30pm.

events.location: SFPL — Parkside
events.description: Papel picado is a traditional Mexican folk art featuring colorful tissue paper cut into intricate, perforated designs and hung as festive banners. Artisans typically craft these delicate decorations by layering sheets of paper and punching out shapes with specialized chisels and small mallets. Alternatively, they hand-fold the sheets and use sharp scissors. We will use this hand-folding and scissor technique to create our very own unique designs!Space limited. Reservations required: sign up at the Information Desk or call (415) 355-5770 (starting October 1).

events.title: Nafissa Thompson-Spires: The Four Wives and Five Deaths of Richard Milford
events.location: Museum of the African Diaspora, 685 Mission St, San Francisco
events.description: FREE, $10-$15 suggested donation Co-presented with Museum of the African Diaspora From the author of the multi-award-winning, National Book Award–longlisted, “vivid, fast, funny, way-smart, and verbally inventive” (George Saunders) story collection Heads of the Colored People, comes a sly, spry, literary debut novel. We find ourselves in 1920s Oklahoma, just far enough out of Tulsa, just long enough after the Race Massacre of 1921. For as long as anyone can remember, the Milfords have led plentiful lives on the backs of the townspeople of Newville. On the ominous brink of the Great Depression and at the height of Prohibition, Richard Milford is an infamous moonshiner and womanizer who, it seems, finally crossed the wrong person at the wrong time. He’s dead and buried with only his women to mourn him, but a question remains: Who killed him, and why? Top suspects are his four “wives,” but as their stories burst to light, the very idea of a true story comes apart before our eyes. In conversation with Margaret Wilkerson Sexton. Doors at 5:30pm.

events.description: $15 APAture, the only festival to put the focus on emerging Asian Pacific American artists, returns from Oct. 17th to Dec. 12th for its 27th year. This year's theme, GENERATION, turns our focus toward what we inherit, what we cultivate, and what we pass on—seeding growth for the future health of our communities while honoring the artistic lineages that have brought us to this moment. As we consider what the next generation of artists will hold and shape, we celebrate creative inheritance as an active, collective practice, one that bridges past, present, and future through art. What do you carry forward, and what will you leave behind? This year's literary showcase features writers Alyson Sagala, Bianca Datta, Brandon Vu, Leslie Nguyen-Okwu, Mai-Linh Hong, May-Li Khoe, Monica Korde, Neha M. Sampat, Rose Wong, and Vina Vo. events.title: Artificial Intimacy: Sherry Turkle and A.I.
events.location: YBCA Screening Room, 701 Mission St, San Francisco
events.description: Co-presented with Yerba Buena Center for the Arts Sherry Turkle has spent decades studying how digital technologies isolate us from one another. Now, in her latest book, Artificial Intimacy: Who We Become When We Talk To Machines, the psychologist who pioneered our understanding of human-computer relationships explores the seductive and beguiling nature of chatbots presented as “perfect” companions. How does their popularity point to existing wells of deep loneliness in our current culture, and how does increasing reliance on a one-sided digital ear affect users’ ability to maintain offscreen relationships with other humans? In conversation with New Yorker cartoonist Amy Kurzweil, whose graphic novel Artificial: A Love Story suggests an alternate path in which A.I. isn’t used as a human connection substitute, but rather a tool to support and deepen the real-world relationships we already have. The conversation is part of Free Wednesdays at YBCA, which offers extended gallery hours, hands-on afternoon art-making, and special evening programs—all for free. Doors at 6:00pm.

events.title: Surreal or real? A conversation between two writers on their styles and what inspires them.
events.location: Medicine for Nightmares, 3036 24th St, San Francisco, CA 94110
events.description: A conversation between fiction writers Donna Miscolta and Marianne Villanueva about where stories come from, what scares them and what makes them laugh when they’re creating characters and situations. Marianne Villanueva, author of four books of dystopian, surreal, and fantasy fiction, will pose questions to Donna Miscolta about her new realist novel Ofelia and Norma . Miscolta, author of four books of fiction, will ask Villanueva about her latest story collection Residents of the Deep . Donna Miscolta’s latest of four books of fiction is Ofelia and Norma . Her stories, essays, and book reviews have appeared in dozens of journals and anthologies. A recording of her work is part of the Library of Congress PALABRA Archive, a showcase for Latin American and Latino writers. She recently moved to Spain and blogs monthly at donnamiscolta.com . Marianne Villanueva is the author of the story collections Ginseng and Other Tales from Manila , Mayor of the Roses , The Lost Language , and Residents of the Deep . A recipient of fellowships from Stanford University and the California Arts Council, she is writing her first novel, set in 16th-century Spain and the Philippines. In Ofelia and Norma , large-bodied twin sisters struggle for a sense of self. When Ofelia sheds pounds from long, solo walks, Norma senses their twinness slipping away. She slips away to an out-of-town college, leaving Ofelia for the first time, and each sister confronts alone life as a large person in an anti-large-person world. Ofelia, having previously lost weight without trying, now makes a deliberate effort to do so, resulting in a disaster that shakes her to her senses. Meanwhile, Norma escapes into her solitude by swimming laps in the college pool where she suffers an experience that sends her into emotional retreat. They move into careers, still estranged until a tender moment leads to the sharing of their secrets and revenge for what one of them has suffered. In Residents of the Deep , Marianne Villanueva explores human resilience in moments of extremity through a series of gripping stories. In “Ice,” two men confront their future in a barren, post-apocalyptic world where survival itself becomes the only meaning: “The point is, there is no point. You just keep going.” In Dumaguete, a young boy is forced to protect his mother, a role that threatens to unravel him. The title story follows a ship captain who discovers a submerged city and is thrust into a moral reckoning that challenges his understanding of responsibility. Clear-eyed and unflinching, these stories reveal the raw tenacity and unyielding spirit of humanity, even in the face of profound vulnerability and hardship.

events.title: Vigdis Hjorth: Repetition
events.location: Telegraph Hill Books, 1501 Grant Ave, San Francisco
events.description: FREE, $10-$15 suggested donation Sponsored by Norway House and Center for the Art of Translation Part of Words Around the World From International Booker Prize– and National Book Award–nominated author Vigdis Hjorth comes her latest novel finally translated into English, Repetition. As winter approaches in Norway and the daylight dwindles, a chance encounter prompts a novelist to reexamine her past. The seismic events following her sixteenth birthday return with haunting vividness, exposing a story both utterly familiar and desperately strange. It was the year she first got drunk, the year she first had sex with a boy. She was watched like a hawk by an anxious mother and a silent, distant father. It was a year of typical teenage fixation and typical teenage frivolity, and of all the usual parental fretting. Until something else took hold, and her family made an unspoken decision and a terrible sacrifice. Only now, decades later, can these events come close to being comprehended. In conversation with Daniela Blei.

Riding shotgun is Irena Smith, whose memoir Troika is a modern-day Odyssey set in California’s Central Coast, as three generations of women share profound family stories and create new ones. Doctorow, Ramon is offered a promotion and cash which could pay for grad school – if he agrees to enter a green-card marriage with his boss’s niece. When he agrees, he gets more than he bargained for. “Smoke and Shadows” by Tatyana Tolstaya centers on a Russian professor living in the U.S., navigating her professional life, her intimate relationships, and the mysteries of culture. events.title: Goldenvoice Presents The Valley Girl Problems Tour Kylie Cantrall
events.location: The Warfield, 982 Market St, San Francisco, CA 94102
events.description:
Multihyphenate actress, singer and songwriter Kylie Cantrall played the lead title character ‘Red,’ the daughter of the Queen of Hearts in Disney’s hit film “Descendants: The Rise of Red.” Following the massive success of the film, Kylie performed in “Descendants/Zombies: Worlds Collide Tour,” a live concert experience which sold-out 40 arenas across North America. Kylie returned as ‘Red' to lead the sequel “Descendants: Wicked Wonderland,” which premiered on Disney+ in July 2026.

Last year, Kylie released her highly anticipated debut EP titled “B.O.Y.”  through Artist Partner Group which included her singles “Boy for a Day,” “Goodie Bag,” “Denim,” and “See U Tonight.” In 2026, Kylie kicks off her new partnership with Republic Records, debuting her brand-new EP Valley Girl Problems out July 24th. Produced by Tricky Stewart (Rihanna, Tyla) and written alongside Tayla Parx, the nine-track project marks a bold new chapter for Kylie continuing her evolution as both an artist and a cultural voice for a new generation.

events.description: $15 / $3 early bird discount until October 18th (code: earlybird16) Co-presented with Locus Magazine and SF in SF Celebrate the spooky season with Ellen Datlow, Hugo Award–winning editor of the new horror anthology All Hallows Eve: Stories of Halloween and Other Festivals of the Dead, a chilling lineup of 19 original short stories delving into our worldwide obsession with that time of year when the veil is lifted, spirits come alive, and the boundary between the living and the dead is far too thin. But that’s not all—Datlow will also sit down with Locus Magazine editor-in-chief Liza Trombi to discuss four-plus decades of her legendary career in the horror genre, and the countless authors she’s shepherded to print. Until something else took hold, and her family made an unspoken decision and a terrible sacrifice. Only now, decades later, can these events come close to being comprehended. In conversation with Britta Stromeyer.

events.title: California's Diverse Food and Farming Movements
events.location: Book Club of California, 47 Kearny St, San Francisco, CA 94108
events.description: FREE Co-presented with Book Club of California Californians tend to think and talk a lot about food—not just who has the best farmers’ markets or where to find the latest Instagram-famous pastry, but also about how the ways we grow, harvest, distribute, and consume food can best serve goals related to climate, social justice, and collective well-being. In his new book, North Stars of Emancipation: California’s Diverse Food and Farming Movements, researcher and activist Antonio Roman-Alcalá finds guidance on all these questions in our state’s grassroots food movements, and in the vision of Black, Indigenous, Latinx, and other people who are leading the way. Joining Roman-Alcalá in conversation is one of those leaders, Sara Calvosa Olson, author of Chími Nu’am: Native Californian Foodways for the Contemporary Kitchen. Member/guest reception at 5:30pm.

events.title: Fire, Earth, Air & Water: Nik Sharma on the Science of Better Cooking
events.location: Book Society, 2945 College Ave, Berkeley, CA 94705
events.description: $30 Book Society Members / $45 General Public Sponsored by Chronicle Books Media sponsorship by Berkeleyside Co-presented with Book Society With books like Season and The Flavor Equation, award-winning cookbook author and America's Test Kitchen Editor in Residence Nik Sharma has earned a reputation for blending storytelling and science with recipes that are seasonal, reliable, and delicious. In his fourth cookbook, Fundamentals of Flavor: 100 Recipes for the Science of Better Cooking, this former molecular biologist shows home cooks how four elements—fire, earth, air, and water—shape the way we cook and taste. In conversation with food writer Soleil Ho, Sharma will lead an interactive evening in the spirit of a test kitchen: an intimate conversation with tastings of recipes from the book. Doors at 6:00pm. events.title: Presentation: Destination San Francisco
events.location: SFPL — Main
events.description: Explore how San Francisco became a global tourist destination through decades of promotional campaigns, from evocative travel posters and airline memorabilia to advertising that shaped the city’s image around the world. Quite the opposite: its appeal has been nurtured by decades of promotional efforts to make people from around the world want to come and see what the fuss is all about.

events.title: Peter Pan Goes Wrong
events.location: San Francisco Playhouse, 450 Post St, San Francisco, CA 94102
events.description: The Cornley Polytechnic Drama Society is back, and this time they’re taking on Peter Pan . It’s their most ambitious production yet, complete with flying rigs, sword fights, and a very real crocodile problem. What could possibly go wrong? As technical mishaps pile up and tempers flare, the cast battles to keep the show on track while everything around them spectacularly falls apart. Lines are forgotten, scenery refuses to cooperate, and rivalries spill onto the stage in real time. From the creators of The Play That Goes Wrong , this riotous comedy delivers nonstop mayhem, perfectly timed chaos, and the kind of theatrical disaster you have to see to believe.

events.title: Assimilation

events.description: A Word for Word and Z Space production · Stories by E.L. Doctorow & Tatyana Tolstaya Presented by Word for Word and Z Space Directed by Rotimi Agbabiaka In “Assimilation” by E. L. Doctorow, Ramon is offered a promotion and cash which could pay for grad school – if he agrees to enter a green-card marriage with his boss’s niece. When he agrees, he gets more than he bargained for. “Smoke and Shadows” by Tatyana Tolstaya centers on a Russian professor living in the U.S., navigating her professional life, her intimate relationships, and the mysteries of culture. Told with Tolstaya’s sharp, restrained wit, the story zeros in on the experience of living in a new culture, and the confusions and imbalance that can cause. What does it mean to assimilate? These two writers offer two very different perspectives.

Joined by her hapless but loyal classmate Curtis Mehlberg (Jacob Tremblay), Prue navigates a world of talking animals, bandits, and powerful figures driven by grief and ambition. As the pair is drawn into a conflict threatening the balance of the forest itself, Prue must discover the strength and belief she never knew she possessed. If she hopes to save her brother and protect Wildwood’s fragile future, she will have to risk everything. From Oscar®-nominated and BAFTA®-winning LAIKA, Wildwood is a sweeping adventure about love, sacrifice, and the magic that reveals itself when we dare to look beyond the familiar. events.title: Ben Ehrenreich: Hold Still
events.location: City Lights, 261 Columbus Ave, San Francisco
events.description: FREE Co-presented with City Lights In the months after his mother Barbara’s death, author and essayist Ben Ehrenreich set himself the task of writing a story every day. Leaving open the question of what a “story” might be, some entries ended up fable-like tales involving animals doing surprising things. Others were closer to journal entries, many of them about his daughter, who was nearly three at the time, and who was trying to understand death herself at the same time that she was voraciously exploring the living world. This deeply moving collection of those daily journeys into storytelling—a finely crafted combination of fiction, memoir, and poetic prose—is both profound and satisfyingly whimsical. In conversation with Daniel Gumbiner.

events.title: Chad Harbach: The Brightness
events.location: The Lost Church SF, 988 Columbus Ave, San Francisco
events.description: $15 / $3 early bird discount until October 18th (code: earlybird16) $35 for presale signed book (ticket not included) From the bestselling author of literary sensation The Art of Fielding comes an urgent, deeply felt story of friendship, art, love, and grief, following two young women on the brink of irrevocable change. Parties and weddings, messy hookups and marred friendships, art and love and grief—The Brightness follows the electric, chaotic, everything-can-happen lives of Pella and her best friend, Irma, as they fumble their way out of sleepy, Midwestern Westish College and into a larger world that will upend their connection and everything they thought they understood about their own place within it. In stunning scenes and spectacular characters—each drawn with an almost superhuman vividness and humanity—Chad Harbach captures that specific, shimmering anxiety of your twenties when life still feels wide open, even as hard and irreversible choices start closing in. In conversation with novelist Eirinie Carson. Doors at 7:30pm. Order a signed copy of The Brightness here (note: does not include general admission ticket).

events.location: SFPL Main Branch, Koret Auditorium, 100 Larkin St, San Francisco
events.description: FREE, $10–15 suggested donation, $33 for signed book Co-presented with SFPL In the latest addition to the inimitable Walter Mosley’s Joe King Oliver series, King finds himself accepting (again at his grandmother’s request) a case from Arman Babylon, a powerful Los Angeles gangster now dying from cancer. Babylon’s granddaughter, Twyla Mann, has been missing for years, and he’s desperate to find her before he passes. The search pulls King into the Babylons’ stained past and the cold case of Dalia Shorts, a torch singer who vanished without a trace and whom Arman was once suspected of killing. As King follows her trail from L.A. to New York and back, he’ll realize nothing is what it seems as he uncovers a pattern of violence that has targeted the women around Babylon for decades. How much will King be willing to risk to finally set things right? In conversation with Carvell Wallace. Doors at 6:00pm.

events.location: Telegraph Hill Books, 1501 Grant Ave, San Francisco
events.description: FREE, $10–15 suggested donation Part of Words Around the World Sponsored by Center for the Art of Translation Poet, author, translator, and editor Carolina Pihelgas is a leading literary figure in her home country of Estonia. Now, with The Cut Line, translated by Darcy Hurford, Pihelgas’s “extraordinary” (Estonian Literary Magazine) prose writing is available to English readers for the first time. In fewer than 100 pages, Pihelgas takes readers to a near-future Estonian countryside, plagued by the effects of climate change and poised for an impending conflict. These hints of future violence recall the protagonist’s own troubled history, even as she attempts to find serenity and order in the rhythms of nature and simple work. Joining Pihelgas in conversation is Sasha Vasilyuk, award-winning author of the novel Your Presence Is Mandatory. Doors at 6:30pm.
