events.location: Bird & Beckett Books & Records, 653 Chenery Street, San Francisco
events.description: Lincoln Adler, saxophone Scott Foster, guitar; Kurt Ribak, bass $20 cover charge; byob Students $10 For a reservation, call the bookshop at 415-586-3733 Kurt Rebak’s compositions signify his reach for what happens when “Charles Mingus meets The Meters, and they go to Duke Ellington’s house to jam, with Cachao and Thelonious Monk sitting in.” Kurt has shared the stage with circus performers, preachers and fire-breathing strippers, but never all three at once. He’s performed in venues ranging from Yoshi’s to a club where someone stashed a loaded .45 in his bass bag. When Kurt was about four years old his mother found him dancing to the sound of the dishwasher. More conventional early musical experiences included playing ‘cello and singing in the San Francisco Boys Chorus, which performed with the San Francisco Symphony and Opera. Kurt studied at UC Berkeley, then earned a scholarship to Berklee College of Music, where he graduated with top honors. While at Berklee, he spent many hours transcribing and absorbing the styles of bassists Paul Chambers, Ray Brown, and Charles Mingus, and gained a love of composition and songwriting. Early tunes reflect a strong Thelonious Monk influence, while others reflect his love of the great bassist/composer/bandleader Charles Mingus. Later tunes bring to mind Horace Silver, Lee Morgan, and the South African composer Abdullah Ibrahim. In June 2012 Kurt was in an auto accident, seriously injuring his left hand and forearm. Thirteen operations later he resumed playing, much to the surprise of some surgeons. Kurt notes, “When I was hurt I learned how many people loved me, cared about me. They say it takes a village to raise a child. It also takes a community to heal someone.” In at least one of his tunes, he cheerfully asserts that he’s not adverse to the restorative qualities of a good cocktail. Kurt’s recordings are played on KCSM-FM, KPFA, KZSC, KZFR, KKUP, San Diego’s Jazz 88, PRI and other jazz stations. He leads his group at venues throughout the greater San Francisco Bay Area and beyond, including sold-out appearances at Yoshi’s and SFJAZZ. His group has also performed at the Freight & Salvage Coffeehouse, San Francisco Jazz Festival , San Jose Jazz Festival, Nor-Cal Jazz Festival, Fillmore Street Jazz Festival, and Blue Note Napa…and Bird & Beckett. Kurt’s working trio with Lincoln Adler on saxophone and Greg Sankovich on piano dates back to associations made in his San Francisco Boys Chorus days when he and Lincoln were members, and his subsequent undergraduate years at Berkeley when he and Lincoln encountered Greg. G reg and Lincoln co-produced Kurt’s last three records, “ PAST PRESENT FUTURE ”,” I Got One More! ” and “ ONWARD “. events.description: A Word for Word and Z Space production · Stories by E.L. Doctorow & Tatyana Tolstaya Presented by Word for Word and Z Space Directed by Rotimi Agbabiaka In “Assimilation” by E. L. Doctorow, Ramon is offered a promotion and cash which could pay for grad school – if he agrees to enter a green-card marriage with his boss’s niece. When he agrees, he gets more than he bargained for. “Smoke and Shadows” by Tatyana Tolstaya centers on a Russian professor living in the U.S., navigating her professional life, her intimate relationships, and the mysteries of culture. events.title: Nosferatu: A Symphony of Horror with LIVE SCORE by Dallas Acid & Paz Lenchantin (Presented by folkYEAH!)
events.location: 4-Star Theater, 2200 Clement St, San Francisco, CA 94121
events.description: (((folkYEAH!))) presents: NOSFERATU: A SYMPHONY OF HORROR (F.W. Murnau, 1922) The mysterious Count Orlok summons a happily married real estate agent to his castle, located up in the Transylvanian mountains, to finalise a terrifying deal. with LIVE ORIGINAL SCORE performed by Paz Lenchantin Paz Lenchantin is a musician best known for playing bass in such varied groups as Pixies, Zwan, A Perfect Circle, Silver Jews, and the Entrance Band. In addition to bass, she sings, plays piano, violin, guitar, and drums. She played strings on Queens of the Stone Age’s Songs For the Deaf , Melissa Auf der Maur’s first solo album, and for several scenes in Michael Mann’s 2006 film, Miami Vice . Lenchantin also directed the music video for Pixies’ “Human Crime.” Her debut solo album, Triste , was released in October 2025 on her own label, Hideous Humans Records. — The Creative Independent Spotify | IG Dallas Acid Dallas Acid is a synth-heavy dreampop trio from Austin, Texas and the first new signing to All Saints Records in a number of years. Following previous releases on Flying Moonlight and Olde English Spelling Bee, they join a roster that includes Brian Eno, Harold Budd and Laraaji (who the band previously collaborated with on 2018’s Arrive Without Leaving album). All Saints Records founder Dominic Norman-Taylor comments: “Dallas Acid's unique mix of minimalist electronic music with a big ballad sensibility creates gorgeous, utterly compelling immersive soundworlds. All Saints Records is delighted to release their album The Spiral Arm. Dallas Acid is our first new signing for several years. It’s been worth the wait”. Dallas Acid: “We are honoured and humbled to be a part of the incredible All Saints family, and share label space with so many legendary, talented pioneers whose explorations into the ambient, electronic and avant-garde helped to influence and guide us to the creation of The Spiral Arm.” The sky-gazing wonder of Linda Beecroft’s vocals on the title track recall the breathy intimacy of Mazzy Star, yet draped with almost symphonic banks of synthesizers blinking into infinity, expertly operated by Christian Havins and Michael Gerner, redolent of the deepest end of classic kosmische music. Other tracks such as the instrumental “Circuit Jungle” touch upon the ‘Fourth World’ experiments of Jon Hassell with a mixture of moog abstractions and FX-drenched acoustic percussion. At other points they touch upon the rain-drenched soundtracks of Vangelis and other more mysterious, electronic arthouse film scores. Dallas Acid's inspiration stems from 1970s German and French electronic music, early minimalism and ambient music. Since 2015 they've been performing live in planetariums, galleries, theaters, churches, and many other unconventional spaces. After playing the traveling culinary experience/projection cube Monkeytown, they collaborated with Paz Lenchantin of the Pixies to create an original new score for F. W. Murnau's Nosferatu, which they performed live in 2016 at the Blue Starlite Drive-In Theater on Halloween. In the spring of 2018 Dallas Acid was featured at HBO's Westworld interactive SXSW experience, followed by an east coast tour with Dead Meadow and performances with legendary ambient/new-age musician LARAAJI. An impromptu collaborative recording session with LARAAJI and long-time partner Arji OceAnanda gave birth to a new LP: Arrive Without Leaving, available now on Flying Moonlight Records. Their critically-acclaimed LPs Original Soundtrack (2016) and Spa Hunter (2017) are also available at flyingmoonlight.com. Bandcamp | IG DOORS at 7:00PM | FILM at 8:00 PM Tickets

events.title: LIVE  MUSIC:  Izaak Opatz, Joe Kaplow
events.location: Balboa Theatre, 3630 Balboa St, San Francisco, CA 94121
events.description: Izaak Opatz Izaak Opatz’s music has always been about longing, run through with nostalgia for the passed-by and out-of-reach. His first two albums, Mariachi Static and Extra Medium , were propelled by a longing for specific people and places, made relatable by wry humor, thoughtful simile and close observation. More recently, he’s been writing songs that long for an alternative reality, for different possibilities than the short, doomed menu offered by our tech lords and the current kakistocracy failing to regulate them. Songs that push back against the coercive pressure to indulge in small conveniences at the expense of personal privacy, a 20th-century attention span and the steady drip of a monthly subscription: I spend a lot of my time now, jumping through hoops / asking permission from a little screen convincing a robot that I’m not a robot / this future isn’t all it was cracked up to be Joe Kaplow My music comes from life’s moments — smelling 4 acres of freshly cut grass, watching the steam from a horse’s breath in the early morning, finally holding the neck of my guitar after holding bridles and worn wooden handles all day. 4000 acres of freshly burnt wildfire, watching the steam from the Pacific Ocean’s breath in the early morning, finally holding the neck of my guitar after clutching the worn steering wheel of the tour van all day. Now my reality is in Bonny Doon, CA, where mountains meet the sea. I am in my recording studio, aptly named Hippie Cowboy, every day. Slow and steady; keep it fun, stay engaged. All for the moment when the song finally sounds right. Friday, October 23 Doors at 7 PM/Music at 8 PM

events.title: Every Saturday Night
events.location: A.C.T., 415 Geary St, San Francisco, CA 94102
events.description:
Be transported to San Francisco’s Fillmore District—beginning in the present day, where the echoes of a once-thriving Black neighborhood still shape the streets. From there, Every Saturday Night pulls audiences back into the 1950s, the vibrant “Harlem of the West,” when the Fillmore pulsed with jazz, community, and possibility.

Following two Black boys—one in each era—the musical explores home, belonging, and resilience, revealing how the Fillmore’s past and present are connected by displacement, gentrification, and the enduring fight to stay rooted in the community.

Inspired by true events, this boisterous and heartfelt new work commissioned and presented by San Francisco Bay Area Theatre Company (SFBATCO) celebrates a historic neighborhood while asking urgent questions about who gets to remain in the city today.

🎉 Public Hours at the Commons 🎉
Every Sunday, the Commons opens to the public — no membership required. Come co-work, connect, create, or just explore the space at your own pace. ✨
🕘 When: Every Sunday, 9 AM – 10 PM
📍 Where: 540 Laguna St, San Francisco (corner of Hayes & Laguna, basement level)
RSVP and we'll email you your entry code ahead of time — so you can let yourself straight in when you arrive.
──────────────────────────────
🧭 A self-guided day
Public Hours are self-guided — come in, settle in, and make the space your own. Weekends are usually unstaffed, so there's no check-in desk or guided tour. Our members are glad to answer questions about the space; for anything else — including guided tours, which we don't offer as drop-ins — email hello@thesfcommons.com ahead of time.
──────────────────────────────
🔭 Getting in
Your entry code comes by email. Once you RSVP, we'll send you a personal QR code — that's your key for the day. Keep it handy on your phone (and check spam if you don't see it).
Find us. We're at 540 Laguna St, on the corner of Hayes & Laguna. Head down the stairs beside Earthbody to the basement level — that's the Commons.
Scan your QR code at the reader to unlock the door. Hold your phone just below the Kisi reader by the door and it'll let you in.
Your access stays active all day, 9 AM – 10 PM, so you can come and go freely.
Can't find your code on the day? No problem — scan the QR posted on the door to check in and get a fresh one on the spot.
We're shoes-off 🧦 — please clean up after yourself, including dirty dishes and mugs, and use only the front entrance. Trouble getting in? Email hello@thesfcommons.com.

events.title: Bonding with Bots: AI, Relationships and the Future of Human Connection
events.location: 550 Laguna St, San Francisco + Full Studio
events.description:
Our Theme: Bonding with Bots: AI, Relationships and the Future of Human Connection
27% of U.S. adults who use AI systems for social, emotional and personal purposes, and a third consider their AI as a friend. Once people begin using AI personally, many develop relationships that involve trust, emotional connection, and a sense of being understood.
These tools are arriving at a complicated moment for human connection. Loneliness and social isolation are widespread, and many people, especially young people, report having few or no close friends.
For most of human history, other people have been central to how we understand ourselves, create meaning, navigate difficulty, and experience belonging. But relationships with other people are also challenging. They require patience, repair, and the willingness to encounter another person who may feel differently than us. AI offers something different: connection that can be frictionless and endlessly accommodating.
This salon is a space to ask: As AI becomes more present in our emotional lives, what are the implications for how we relate to one another? How can we preserve and strengthen our human connections?
About Resonance:
Resonance Salons are intimate, in-person gatherings for thoughtful people across tech, art, care, community, and everyday life who want to make sense of how AI is changing everyday life, together. It's for those who feel the world shifting and want a real space to reflect, connect, and explore what kind of future we actually want to shape. Each salon includes a facilitated, Socratic-style dialogue where everyone is invited to participate, share honestly, ask questions, and think together across different perspectives. Dinner and drinks are provided; let us know about dietary needs when you register.

events.location: 4-Star Theater, 2200 Clement St, San Francisco, CA 94121
events.description: Throwin’ Bo’s presents: Resavoir Resavoir is the work of Chicago-born and based musician, composer and producer Will Miller. Miller is a jazz trumpeter and composer by training – first via Chicago Public Schools, then Oberlin Conservatory. As an instrumentalist he’s played on recordings by Chance The Rapper, Lil Wayne, Mac Miller, and for several years was a regular member of the indie band Whitney. But since 2016 he has been moving more and more in the direction of all around “producer” – working with an expanded palette of synths, pianos, live and programmed drums in addition to his MIDI-augmented trumpet, he has developed a signature cinematic soul-jazz sound rooted in hip-hop structures, heard through his work on tracks for Eryn Allen Kane, Whitney, Knox Fortune, and SZA’s recently-released album SOS (which spent 10 weeks as the #1 spot on the Billboard 200 chart). In 2019 Miller released Resavoir’s debut album Resavoir to high praise, including a glowing 8.2 review in Pitchfork. Later that year, Miller and his live version of the Resavoir band (featuring former Noname musical director Akenya, saxophonist/vocalist/MC Sen Morimoto, and others) did their London debut as part of the first Boiler Room Festival. While they were in London, they did a recording session at Total Refreshment Studios. One of those recordings was a cover of the Charles Tolliver song “Plight,” and the track was released by Blue Note Records as part of the compilation Transmissions from Total Refreshment Centre. Miller spent much of the pandemic years in his studio, and much of 2022 on tour with Whitney. This Fall, he will release Resavoir’s second self-titled album. The new Resavoir is a more polished and focused presentation of his evolving skills as a studio producer. His compositional touch is more articulate than ever. The short but sweet album is a subtly-radiant symphony interweaving modern-day soul-jazz with bedroom beats, synth serenades and twilight sonatas. The collection’s eleven tracks feature a massive list of contributors including Elton Aura, Whitney, Akenya, Matt Gold, Eddie Burns, Lane Beckstrom, Jeremy Cunningham, Irvin Pierce, Macie Stewart, Peter Manheim and many more. events.description:
M Is for More: An Essential Ingredients Table is a one-of-a-kind evening bringing menopause, andropause and midlife into the same conversation — in the same room.

Hosted by NextGen Purpose, this live event features a studio podcast recording, expert speakers, an audience Q&A and a cocktail reception at The Magic Theatre in San Francisco.

This isn't just another health talk. It's a space for women, men, partners, families and the broader community to have the conversation that's often missing — openly, honestly and together.

Whether you're navigating midlife yourself, supporting someone who is, or simply curious about a topic that affects everyone, this evening was designed for you.

What to expect: · Live podcast recording with Dr. Lisa Brent and Dr. Justin Mager · Audience Q&A — bring your questions · The Table — an hour to connect with the community · VIP Happy Hour & Meet and Greet (limited to 15 guests)

Justine Reichman is the founder of NextGen Purpose, a conscious living media platform at the intersection of sustainability, wellness, food and purpose-driven business. She is the host of the Essential Ingredients podcast, with over 324 episodes, 1.5 million downloads and listeners in more than 50 countries. A bestselling author and advocate for redefining midlife, Justine created The Primes, a membership community for high-achieving women navigating perimenopause and menopause. M Is for More: Live is her vision to bring the midlife conversation — menopause, andropause and everything in between — into one room, together.

Dr. Lisa Brent is a Naturopathic Doctor, Licensed Acupuncturist and the founder of Be Well Natural Medicine in Marin County, California. With over 25 years of clinical experience, she specializes in women's health, bioidentical hormone therapy, perimenopause and menopause care. A graduate of UC Berkeley and the National College of Naturopathic Medicine, Dr. Brent completed advanced training in holistic gynecology and a residency in women's health and complementary cancer care. She is a sought-after speaker on midlife health, hormones and female longevity, bridging modern medical science with integrative medicine. Her work helps women understand the biological realities of midlife and make informed decisions about their health.

6:00 VIP Happy Hour (VIP only) 7:00 Live taping, about 45 minutes 7:45 Audience Q&A 8:00 The Table — an hour to talk, connect and share with the community 9:00 Close

M Is for More is an edition of the Essential Ingredients Table, a live series recorded in front of an audience for the Essential Ingredients podcast, which reaches listeners in more than 50 countries.

events.description: (((folkYEAH!))) presents: The Wildwoods The Wildwoods, hailing from Lincoln, Nebraska, continue to bring sonic beauty and simplicity to today’s increasingly complicated and cluttered musical landscape. With Dear Meadowlark, the band’s fourth full-length album released on April 11, 2025, The Wildwoods have once again taken the hallmarks of the folk-Americana sound and dressed it in indie sensibilities a la heroes Nickel Creek and Gillian Welch as well as genre mainstays Bon Iver and Mumford & Sons. And yet, at its core, Dear Meadowlark is about three 20-something musicians celebrating the emotional allure of familiarity and comfort. “The main lyrical theme of the album is the appreciation for our home state of Nebraska and the homesickness that can come with long periods spent on the road,” says Noah Gose. The Wildwoods are Noah Gose on vocals, acoustic and electric guitar; his wife, Chloe Gose on vocals and violin; and longtime friend Andrew Vaggalis on vocals and upright bass. Their delicate embrace of the past, present, and future has transformed The Wildwoods into a potent entity. Recently, The Wildwoods were finalists in the 2024 Rocky Mountain Songwriter Contest in Red Lodge, Montana. In 2023, the trio enjoyed being finalists in two high-profile band competitions – FreshGrass Music Festival and VHS “Gems in the Rough.” Also, their songwriting strengths have been recognized by semi-final placements in the International Songwriting competition with tracks such as “Untitled” and “Way of Train.” Bandcamp | IG Support to be announced DOORS at 7:00PM | MUSIC at 8:00 PM Tickets

events.title: Somatic Healing Workshop: Get Out of Your Head & Into Your Body
events.location: 550 Laguna St, San Francisco + Full Studio
events.description:
A somatic healing experience to help you quiet the mental noise, reconnect with yourself, and return to the wisdom of your body.
Do you find yourself constantly overthinking, analyzing, worrying, planning, or second-guessing yourself?
Maybe you know what you should do, but still feel stuck. Maybe you struggle to trust yourself, feel disconnected from your emotions, or find yourself living in your head instead of fully experiencing your life.
You're not alone. Many of us have been taught to rely almost exclusively on our minds while ignoring the wisdom of our bodies. But when we're constantly thinking, analyzing, and trying to figure everything out, we often become disconnected from the very thing that can guide us most: ourselves.
In this immersive somatic workshop, you'll learn how to shift out of overthinking and back into your body through simple yet powerful practices that support nervous system regulation, self-awareness, emotional processing, and deeper connection.
You'll learn:
Why overthinking is often a sign of nervous system dysregulation
How stress and survival patterns keep us stuck in our heads
The connection between the body, emotions, and intuition
Why healing and transformation require more than mindset alone
How to create more presence, clarity, and connection in your daily life

Through guided somatic practices, you'll experience grounding exercises, breathwork, body awareness practices, gentle movement, embodiment exercises, and nervous system regulation techniques designed to help you reconnect with yourself and the present moment.
You'll leave with:
A greater sense of calm, clarity, and inner connection
Practical tools to navigate overwhelm and overthinking
A deeper understanding of your body's signals and needs
More trust in yourself, your intuition, and your inner wisdom
Simple ways to deepen your sense of presence and connection in your daily life
This workshop isn't about fixing yourself or becoming someone new. It's about remembering how to listen to the wisdom that's already within you.
If you're ready to spend less time in your head and more time feeling grounded, present, and fully alive, this experience is for you.
Please bring a journal and water bottle, and wear comfortable clothes.
NOTE: Please be on time for this session — doors will close promptly and there will be NO LATE ENTRIES!
About Anna Bolender:
Anna Bolender is a certified Somatic Embodiment & Intuitive Life Coach, Somatic Breathwork and Quantum Wellness Practitioner, Reiki Master, and lifelong student of holistic health and well-being.
Through her coaching programs and workshops, Anna guides others to return home to themselves — releasing what keeps them stuck, reconnecting with their body and inner wisdom, and creating real, lasting transformation from the inside out.
Blending somatics, energy healing, quantum wellness, and mindset work, she helps clients break free from self-sabotaging patterns, repattern their nervous system, and cultivate simple daily rituals that support a fulfilling, grounded, and aligned life.
Anna’s mission is to empower others to feel connected, alive, and radiant — no matter what life brings.

events.title: What Should Stay Human When Agents Join the Team?
events.location: 540 Laguna St, San Francisco + 540 Cafe
events.description:
Your team works with AI agents now, and nobody has agreed what the agents get to decide. So everyone draws their own line. One person lets the agent send the client email. Another rewrites everything it touches. Someone hides how much they use it. None of it gets said out loud, and slowly the team stops trusting the work, and each other.
This workshop is where a team draws the line together: which calls stay human, which go to the agents, and which the agent drafts and a human decides. What you leave with is a one-page agreement your team wrote, and a monthly practice to keep it current as the work changes.
WHO IT'S FOR: Founders and team leads bringing AI agents into a team, and anyone on a team that already works with them. Heads of HR / People & Culture who want a way to do this across teams.
LEAVE WITH: A one-page team agreement: what stays human, what goes to the agents, what needs a human check. A 45-minute monthly version you can run with your own team.

events.title: Every Saturday Night
events.location: A.C.T., 415 Geary St, San Francisco, CA 94102
events.description:
Be transported to San Francisco’s Fillmore District—beginning in the present day, where the echoes of a once-thriving Black neighborhood still shape the streets. From there, Every Saturday Night pulls audiences back into the 1950s, the vibrant “Harlem of the West,” when the Fillmore pulsed with jazz, community, and possibility.

Following two Black boys—one in each era—the musical explores home, belonging, and resilience, revealing how the Fillmore’s past and present are connected by displacement, gentrification, and the enduring fight to stay rooted in the community.

Inspired by true events, this boisterous and heartfelt new work commissioned and presented by San Francisco Bay Area Theatre Company (SFBATCO) celebrates a historic neighborhood while asking urgent questions about who gets to remain in the city today.

🎉 Public Hours at the Commons 🎉
Every Sunday, the Commons opens to the public — no membership required. Come co-work, connect, create, or just explore the space at your own pace. ✨
🕘 When: Every Sunday, 9 AM – 10 PM
📍 Where: 540 Laguna St, San Francisco (corner of Hayes & Laguna, basement level)
RSVP and we'll email you your entry code ahead of time — so you can let yourself straight in when you arrive.
──────────────────────────────
🧭 A self-guided day
Public Hours are self-guided — come in, settle in, and make the space your own. Weekends are usually unstaffed, so there's no check-in desk or guided tour. Our members are glad to answer questions about the space; for anything else — including guided tours, which we don't offer as drop-ins — email hello@thesfcommons.com ahead of time.
──────────────────────────────
🔭 Getting in
Your entry code comes by email. Once you RSVP, we'll send you a personal QR code — that's your key for the day. Keep it handy on your phone (and check spam if you don't see it).
Find us. We're at 540 Laguna St, on the corner of Hayes & Laguna. Head down the stairs beside Earthbody to the basement level — that's the Commons.
Scan your QR code at the reader to unlock the door. Hold your phone just below the Kisi reader by the door and it'll let you in.
Your access stays active all day, 9 AM – 10 PM, so you can come and go freely.
Can't find your code on the day? No problem — scan the QR posted on the door to check in and get a fresh one on the spot.
We're shoes-off 🧦 — please clean up after yourself, including dirty dishes and mugs, and use only the front entrance. Trouble getting in? Email hello@thesfcommons.com.

events.title: Purpose Alignment Circle
events.location: 550 Laguna St, San Francisco + Full Studio
events.description:
Hi Everyone,
We’re continuing our Purpose Alignment Circle series with a community gathering: Life After the Leap.
You took the leap. You left the job. You took the sabbatical. You made the big change. And now you’re back - and what often goes unspoken is how disorienting this phase can feel.
Coming back isn’t a finish line. It’s its own transition. And most of us are navigating it without a map.
This evening is for career changers, sabbatical-takers, and anyone who has ever wondered: “Okay, I did the brave thing… now what?”
Hosted and facilitated by Bernadette Lagman join us to come together to share real stories, reflect honestly, and find our footing, together.
Come as you are. Bring your questions. And an open mind. You're not alone in this.

Intentional Flow:
Welcome (10 min)
Introduction to the space, intention, and vision
Check-In (10 min)
Name, pronouns, where you're from
Sitting Meditation (10 min)
Guided / silent grounding practice
Big Group Discussion (40 min)
Open reflections and deep listening
What feels most alive or unclear in your current path?
Small Breakout Groups (30 min)
What feels most alive or unclear in your current path?
Accountability Pairing (10 min)
Pair up and share one action step
Align on follow-up/accountability
Closing (10 min)
Final reflections + gratitude What support do you still need?

events.description:
Be transported to San Francisco’s Fillmore District—beginning in the present day, where the echoes of a once-thriving Black neighborhood still shape the streets. From there, Every Saturday Night pulls audiences back into the 1950s, the vibrant “Harlem of the West,” when the Fillmore pulsed with jazz, community, and possibility.

Following two Black boys—one in each era—the musical explores home, belonging, and resilience, revealing how the Fillmore’s past and present are connected by displacement, gentrification, and the enduring fight to stay rooted in the community.

Inspired by true events, this boisterous and heartfelt new work commissioned and presented by San Francisco Bay Area Theatre Company (SFBATCO) celebrates a historic neighborhood while asking urgent questions about who gets to remain in the city today.

events.description:
Come breathe, release, & reset...
Somatic Breathwork is an embodiment experience designed to take you out of your thinking mind and into the deep intelligence of your body — where true healing, clarity, and release happen. It allows your body to express and discharge stored emotions, stress, and old narratives that may be weighing you down.
Somatic Breathwork uses circular connected breathing together with rhythmic music to produce a cathartic emotional release. This release may be in the form of moving, shaking, yelling, crying, laughing, or simply deep stillness.
It gives your body the opportunity to express emotions or actions that may otherwise be unacceptable in modern social settings, allowing your nervous system to process traumas and restore balance.
Using the breath, you’ll engage your body’s innate ability to heal — sweeping out any defenses, blockages, restrictions, or pains that hold you back from showing up as your truest self.
Many participants experience profound emotional release, newfound clarity, and a grounded sense of calm even after a single session.
This experience is designed to:
Move you out of your mind and into your body's electrical network
Release stuck energy, emotions, or trauma responses
Reset your nervous system into grounded calm and clarity
Break old patterns and reconnect you to your authentic self
Increase compassion, presence, and emotional resilience
Support cathartic release in a safe, guided container
Participants often report:
Deep emotional release
More calm, peace, and clarity
Release of anger, grief, frustration, or stagnant energy
Increased presence, awareness, and intuition
Breakthrough insights about their life, patterns, and purpose
Feeling more open, soft, and connected to themselves and others
What to expect:
✨ Opening Check-In & Introduction
✨ 60-Minute Guided Somatic Breathwork Journey
✨ Integration & Optional Group Sharing
Whether you're seeking release, clarity, a reset, or simply a moment to reconnect with yourself — this session is for you.
Please bring a journal and water bottle, and wear comfortable clothes.
NOTE: Please be on time for this session — doors will close promptly and there will be NO LATE ENTRIES!
About Anna Bolender:
Anna Bolender is a certified Somatic Embodiment & Intuitive Life Coach, Somatic Breathwork and Quantum Wellness Practitioner, Reiki Master, and lifelong student of holistic health and well-being.
Through her coaching programs and workshops, Anna guides others to return home to themselves — releasing what keeps them stuck, reconnecting with their body and inner wisdom, and creating real, lasting transformation from the inside out.
Blending somatics, energy healing, quantum wellness, and mindset work, she helps clients break free from self-sabotaging patterns, repattern their nervous system, and cultivate simple daily rituals that support a fulfilling, grounded, and aligned life.
Anna’s mission is to empower others to feel connected, alive, and radiant — no matter what life brings.

events.title: Assimilation
events.location: Z Below
events.description: A Word for Word and Z Space production · Stories by E.L. Doctorow & Tatyana Tolstaya Presented by Word for Word and Z Space Directed by Rotimi Agbabiaka In “Assimilation” by E. L. Doctorow, Ramon is offered a promotion and cash which could pay for grad school – if he agrees to enter a green-card marriage with his boss’s niece. When he agrees, he gets more than he bargained for. “Smoke and Shadows” by Tatyana Tolstaya centers on a Russian professor living in the U.S., navigating her professional life, her intimate relationships, and the mysteries of culture. Told with Tolstaya’s sharp, restrained wit, the story zeros in on the experience of living in a new culture, and the confusions and imbalance that can cause. What does it mean to assimilate? These two writers offer two very different perspectives.

events.title: Imperfect Circles Discussion Group at the Orinda Library
events.location: Orinda Public Library, Orinda
events.description: Are you a person who never tires of talking or thinking about philosophical, scientific or religious theories? Are you interested in psychological insights, or attempts at such insights, into human life? There are many who would insist that being realistic about human life means you should ignore such fundamental questions—starting around the time the ink dries on your diploma. But it is unrealistic to ignore the fundamental explanatory concepts that underlie each successful human civilization—concepts that sometimes help and sometimes hinder us in our pursuit of happiness.

events.title: You Aren't Alone Creative Relief Mini-Retreat
events.location: 550 Laguna St, San Francisco + Full Studio
events.description:
Join the You Aren't Alone Project for a one day Creative Relief Retreat designed for people of all backgrounds to engage in creative expression exercises and discussions as a tool for mental health, self-care, support and solace in a safe and collaborative environment.
Spend the afternoon with us exploring how creativity and mental health intersect to support your overall wellbeing. We'll start with a meditation and movement exercise, then hear from guest artists and mental health and wellness practitioners, and wrap up with a creative mental health workshop for tangible tools you can take with you and use in your daily life.
You do not have to be a practicing artist to attend. We just ask that you come with a creative mindset and an openness to the healing power of art and connection.
The You Aren’t Alone Project is a nonprofit organization dedicated to facilitating & changing conversations around mental health so that no one ever has to feel alone.
We offer community programming, events, and resources that bring people together over shared creative journeys to foster holistic connections and we aim to do it all at a very low to no cost.
By tapping into the power of art and storytelling, we create safe, supportive, and inclusive spaces that encourage positive mental health & wellbeing.
From the founder: While healing is a continuous journey and I am far from done, I have spent the last 10 years building spaces and collecting the tools that I wish I had when I was younger. Through that process, I obtained my Masters in Mental Health Counseling and have used that training to grow YAAP. The project started in Louisiana and I am excited to bring our programs to San Francisco and beyond. I hope you'll join for the first in what we hope to be regularly scheduled gatherings.

events.title: Ben Wolfe Quartet
events.location: SFJAZZ Center, 201 Franklin St, San Francisco, CA 94102 — Joe Henderson Lab
events.description: An artist whose music has been described as “Mingus and Miles Davis meet Bartok and Bernard Herrmann” ( The New York Times ), bassist and composer Ben Wolfe performs music from his most recent album, Any Time After Now , with an all-star quartet of master instrumentalists. A former member of the Jazz at Lincoln Center Orchestra and a veteran of work with Wynton Marsalis, Diana Krall, Harry Connick Jr., Branford Marsalis, Michael Bublé, and Benny Green, Wolfe is a highly regarded bandleader and composer whose work bridges a mastery of modern jazz. The bassist is a two-time recipient of Chamber Music America’s New Works: Creation and Presentation Program Grant through the Doris Duke Foundation and has released a dozen albums including Any Time After Now , his 2026 release for his own Resident Arts Records. Featuring an all-star lineup including vibraphonist Joel Ross, pianist Sullivan Fortner, saxophonist Chris Lewis, and drummer Aaron Kimmel, the album is a masterfully constructed program of original music that further demonstrates Wolfe’s compositional acuity and sumptuous sense of swing. In his liner notes, the eminent drumming great Jeff “Tain” Watts relates, “These great artists have come together and made a beautiful thing.”

events.title: Chris Trinidad’s Chroma Tonic

events.description: Naima Shalhoub, voice/keyboards; Scott Oshiro, flute/quantum electronics; Alex Heigl, guitar/effects; Chris Trinidad, bass/guitar/synth/bass; Cy Thompson, drums/percussion Chris Trinidad’s latest project Chroma Tonic weaves together musicians from wildly divergent backgrounds in order to concoct unique sounds and intriguing groove music. Drawing inspiration from ambient music pioneers Brian Eno and Robert Fripp, the early avant-garde space psychedelia of Pink Floyd, the progressive electronic rock of Tu-Ner, the adventurous electric hybrid experimentations of early seventies Miles Davis, Chris Trinidad’s Chroma Tonic blends these explorations with the influences of the members of the group. Naima Shalhoub provides vocal and synthesizer textures, Alex Heigl plays ambient and looped guitars, Cy Thompson brings an array of Afro-Caribbean percussive elements, Scott Oshiro performs on flute and programs the quantum (!!) electronic improvised live interactions, while Chris Trinidad holds down the foundation on bass guitar and synth bass. $25 cover charge; byob Students $10 For a reservation, call the bookshop at 415-586-3733

events.title: The Commons Public Hours ☕
events.location: 540 Laguna St, San Francisco + Full Space
events.description:
🎉 Public Hours at the Commons 🎉
Every Sunday, the Commons opens to the public — no membership required. Come co-work, connect, create, or just explore the space at your own pace. ✨
🕘 When: Every Sunday, 9 AM – 10 PM
📍 Where: 540 Laguna St, San Francisco (corner of Hayes & Laguna, basement level)
RSVP and we'll email you your entry code ahead of time — so you can let yourself straight in when you arrive.
──────────────────────────────
🧭 A self-guided day
Public Hours are self-guided — come in, settle in, and make the space your own. Weekends are usually unstaffed, so there's no check-in desk or guided tour. Our members are glad to answer questions about the space; for anything else — including guided tours, which we don't offer as drop-ins — email hello@thesfcommons.com ahead of time.
──────────────────────────────
🔭 Getting in
Your entry code comes by email. Once you RSVP, we'll send you a personal QR code — that's your key for the day. Keep it handy on your phone (and check spam if you don't see it).
Find us. We're at 540 Laguna St, on the corner of Hayes & Laguna. Head down the stairs beside Earthbody to the basement level — that's the Commons.
Scan your QR code at the reader to unlock the door. Hold your phone just below the Kisi reader by the door and it'll let you in.
Your access stays active all day, 9 AM – 10 PM, so you can come and go freely.
Can't find your code on the day? No problem — scan the QR posted on the door to check in and get a fresh one on the spot.
We're shoes-off 🧦 — please clean up after yourself, including dirty dishes and mugs, and use only the front entrance. Trouble getting in? Email hello@thesfcommons.com.




The Commons is a modern-day town square for communal meaning-making, personal discovery, and self-expression in the heart of San Francisco. Apply to become a member here__.

events.description: $25 Co-presented with LitCamp You know the feeling. You're moving along, racking up the word count on your novel (or memoir, or creative nonfiction project) when suddenly you hit a wall, a dead end, a what-the-heck-am-I-supposed-to-write-next fork in the road. Call it writer’s block, or a crisis of confidence, or just the universe conspiring against you. But whatever you call it, it's happened to every writer. Join us as four authors, Samina Ali (Pieces You'll Never Get Back), Diana Kapp (The Last Free Women), Jason Roberts (Every Living Thing: The Great and Deadly Race to Know All Life), and Parini Shroff (Some People) share their strategies for pushing past the roadblocks and getting the words flowing again. Moderated by Page Street founder Janis Cooke Newman (A Master Plan for Rescue). Plus, we'll serve complimentary Prosecco, wine, and NA drinks. Tickets support both Litquake and LitCamp. Doors at 3:00pm.

events.title: Jennifer Croft: Notes on Postcards
events.location: City Lights, 261 Columbus Ave, San Francisco
events.description: FREE, $10–15 suggested donation Co-presented with City Lights Bookstore Jennifer Croft may be best known as one of our foremost literary translators, bringing such acclaimed international authors as Olga Tokarczuk and Urszula Honek to English-speaking audiences. She’s also gained acclaim for her own writing, including her novel The Extinction of Irina Rey and her hybrid coming-of-age memoir Homesick, called “stunning and surprising” by the New York Times. Now Croft follows up with a second memoir, detailing her lifelong wanderlust and her habit of both collecting and sending postcards along the way. Notes on Postcards utilizes an innovative format to delve into universal topics: love, loss, parenthood, communication, and connection. We’re thrilled to host the memoir’s official pub-day launch at City Lights, featuring Croft in conversation with Britta Stromeyer. Doors at 6:30pm.

events.title: Somatic Healing 101: The Missing Link to Lasting Change
events.location: 550 Laguna St, San Francisco + Full Studio
events.description:
A somatic workshop to understand your nervous system, reconnect with your body, and learn practical tools for real transformation...
Have you ever known exactly what you "should" do, but still found yourself stuck in the same patterns?
Maybe you've read the books, listened to the podcasts, journaled, reflected, and tried to think your way into change. Yet anxiety, overwhelm, self-sabotage, emotional reactivity, procrastination, or feeling disconnected from yourself keep showing up.
That's because lasting transformation doesn't happen through the mind alone. It happens through the body.
In this immersive workshop, you'll learn the foundations of somatic healing and nervous system regulation, and why working with your body is often the missing piece when it comes to creating meaningful, sustainable change.
We'll explore how stress, emotions, beliefs, and protective patterns are stored in the body, and why healing becomes more effective when we include the nervous system in the process.
You'll learn:
What somatics actually is (and why it's becoming more popular)
Why mindset work alone isn't enough to create real, lasting change
How your nervous system influences your emotions, behaviors, and daily experiences
Simple somatic tools you can use to feel more grounded, present, and connected
How to work with your body instead of constantly trying to push through or override it
This workshop isn't just educational — you'll also experience somatics firsthand through guided practices, including breathwork, body awareness, grounding exercises, mindful movement, and embodiment practices designed to help you reconnect with yourself and your body's wisdom.
You'll leave with:
A clear understanding of what somatic healing is and how it works
Practical tools you can immediately integrate into daily life to finally feel more calm and present
Greater awareness of your nervous system and stress responses
Simple ways to deepen your connection to your body, emotions, and intuition
A new approach to personal growth that feels supportive, sustainable, and effective

Whether you're completely new to somatics or looking to deepen your understanding of holistic healing, this workshop will give you a strong foundation and simple practices you can return to anytime!
Please bring a journal and water bottle, and wear comfortable clothes.
NOTE: Please be on time for this session — doors will close promptly and there will be NO LATE ENTRIES!
About Anna Bolender:
Anna Bolender is a certified Somatic Embodiment & Intuitive Life Coach, Somatic Breathwork and Quantum Wellness Practitioner, Reiki Master, and lifelong student of holistic health and well-being.
Through her coaching programs and workshops, Anna guides others to return home to themselves — releasing what keeps them stuck, reconnecting with their body and inner wisdom, and creating real, lasting transformation from the inside out.
Blending somatics, energy healing, quantum wellness, and mindset work, she helps clients break free from self-sabotaging patterns, repattern their nervous system, and cultivate simple daily rituals that support a fulfilling, grounded, and aligned life.
Anna’s mission is to empower others to feel connected, alive, and radiant — no matter what life brings.

Johnson’s All Boys Aren’t Blue, their bestselling, critically acclaimed YA “memoir-manifesto” about growing up Black and queer, has been, since its 2020 publication, a source of solace and support for young people. It’s also consistently been at or near the top of the ALA and PEN America’s lists of the most challenged and banned books. Undeterred, Johnson continues to practice their fearless form of truth-telling, this time in their first memoir for adults, And If I Die Before I Wake. Here Johnson relates a traumatic 15 years in their life—navigating an HIV diagnosis, alcoholism, loss, and those disheartening and frightening book bans—while relying more than ever on the love of friends, family, and community and finding, against the odds, their most authentic self. events.title: LIVE MUSIC: School Fair, goldenstar, Poor Image (Presented by THROWIN' BO'S)
events.location: 4-Star Theater, 2200 Clement St, San Francisco, CA 94121
events.description: Throwin’ Bo’s presents: School Fair School Fair (Findlay Buchanan, Semisi Ma’ia’i, Hamish Morgan, De Stevens and Rose Pickernell) make music embedded in the human experience. It’s a product of the band’s native New Zealand, a place that remains intimate and remote, where emotion is magnified over both distance and familiarity. The five band members began the project renting out a factory-sized, sub-zero degree Celsius room normally operated by construction workers in the industrial area of Ōtepoti, Dunedin, New Zealand in 2021, recording music on the 4-track tape recorder that would become debut Gorse on a Hill . The album remained the only trace of the band online for a few years, an artifact for those who know where to look. School Fair’s music has this sense of self-discovery when you find it, a sound that feels both recognizable and like the vacant expanse of a country whirring by on a train. Still with little to no self-promotion, the appearance of sophomore effort Bird the Kid online in early 2025 was a new portal to their world of melodic and intricate indie music that retains a kind of atmospheric beauty. Unexpected Violence (Mutual, 2026) is the first record made between geographical places, with the band now split in between London and New Zealand. You can hear this fragmented approach in the patchwork quality and inherent connective tissue of the album. Recorded initially in a studio in East London, it was the first time the band brought in an outside engineer (Syd Kemp?), as opposed to the band’s prior live recordings, where the tendency was to “feed back off each other in quite a messy abstract and complicated way that works for us but isn’t typically structured.” The band then took these recordings and evolved them back home in Dunedin, with the addition of vocals on some tracks by Pickernell adding to the cohesive energy and collective, dialed-in synergy of the quintet. School Fair is built upon the many eclectic mediums from which the band members individually create: time spent repairing old machines, making short films, metalworking and jewelry-making, writing and engineering. All these counterparts bring a kind of industrial electricity to the music where each part feels necessary and agile, as well as perfectly in conjunction. It’s these points beneath the surface where the songs really bloom. The moody transference of guitar lick to guttural vocal and back again, where melody conjoins with surprising inflection and sharp-hued ambiance, littered with both poetic spoken-word and a self-referentiality of clues and repetition that rewards close listening yet remains accessible and immediate. Transportive lyrics shine with the lore and mythology of a world that is both deeply specific and transcendent in its curiosity toward the surrounding environment. Unexpected Violence is filled with resounding descriptors: from “cat runs blind in the smoke / birds slap their wings away / trees thrash and crash / each lonely in their chosen way” (the meandering “Angelika”) or the consequently spellbinding phrasing of “come out to your dead animal river gushing hard / come out to your heart split open and lit up with stars” of “In Boredom You Shoot Your Gun”. It’s a starkly poetic snapshot into the band’s own universe and a showcase in the thoroughfare of language, where the specificity of one person’s memory counteracts with a landscape that blurs and unravels with the passage of time. Unexpected Violence a record that could only be made in a place like New Zealand, yet its vantage point expands far beyond to the vast unwieldiness of human sentiment. “There’s a sense of remoteness to the record, both emotionally but also in the sense of place, broken farms, cast iron beaches, blank midday fires, lost friends.” Or as the band recites in the austere glimmer of “Spirally Staircase Memory”: “memories are just stories that can’t be found.” But School Fair reaches some sort of access point, a way for them to live on. The name Unexpected Violence was born out of Buchanan and Ma’ia’i coming across the genre title in a bookstore in Berlin, and is a fitting discernment of the heartbreak that often comes with the realities of existence. In album highlight “Gussied Up,” the band intones: “I never never never ever / wanna hear you / see you, feel you or touch you.” It’s a harsh statement that feels swept up in the parallel admission that these are relationships you may never fully escape; they have left their mark. We still pass the places they inhabit, and feel the uncanny emptiness even after moving on. It’s fitting that the record ends on a similar contradiction. Just discernable above spirals of drummed up, ambient noise: “I miss you now you’re gone.” For all things can be true at once. Bandcamp | IG goldenstar Montreal’s goldenstar operate within a distinctly fraught strain of the North American musical canon, dancing in (and emerging from) the shadow of beloved forebears like Duster, Sonic Youth, and Sparklehorse. Their self-released 2025 debut EP alongside a sophomore release on OST have established the band as an essential voice on the contemporary slowcore-noise rock continuum. Bandcamp | IG Poor Image Poor Image is a 7 piece emo/americana tinged slowcore band based in the Bay Area. The project came to fruition when members Reid Devereaux, Nick Ferguson, Keenan Lewis, Declan Lewis, Patrick Madden, Tammer Bagdasarian and Nick Ross, who spent their formative years between Silicon Valley, San Francisco, and San Jose participating in the broader bay area music scene, decided to join forces. Poor Image’s recent debut self titled album out on American Death Records is about coming of age strife and trying to “make it” in the age of supersaturation. As written by Nina Protocol, Poor Image’s debut album “...refers back to a micro-glory age of low-stakes indie music in a way that could only come from a band a few generations removed from the source material. It finds a perfect balance between slowcore and Americana; it incorporates a variety of roots-leaning instrumental flourishes when it needs to; it rocks when it needs to”. Featured on Perfectly Imperfect as ones to watch, Poor Image has recently come off national tours opening for Horse Vision & Dutch Interior and are currently recording their second album. events.title: In a Silent Way: Joel Harrison Quintet plays Miles Davis
events.location: Bird & Beckett Books & Records, 653 Chenery Street, San Francisco
events.description: Paul Hanson, reeds; Joel Harrison, guitar; Michael Manring, bass; Scott Amendola, drums Former Berkeley resident, guitarist Joel Harrison, returns to the Bay Area to journey into Miles Davis’ iconic 1970 record, “In a Silent Way.” The band consists of old allies, some of the Bay Area’s finest and most creative musicians—they will also perform some of Harrison’s original music. Harrison recently released a live record from the Big Ears Festival of this music. The band’s approach will be to “make it new.” Guitarist, composer, arranger, lyricist, writer, educator and vocalist Joel Harrison has “created a new blueprint for jazz” (New Orleans Times-Picayune). He has released 27 records, a body of work that connects multiple American traditions. While rooted in jazz, his music moves fluidly through classical, rock, country, and American roots music. The New York Times has described his work as “protean… brilliant.” Harrison is the founder and director of the Alternative Guitar Summit, an annual festival devoted to innovative and unconventional guitar music. The Summit has featured artists such as Fred Frith, Nels Cline, Bill Frisell, Julian Lage, Michael Gregory Jackson, Mary Halvorson and Pat Metheny, who has called it “one of the most interesting and distinguished forums for guitar on the planet.” Harrison is the author of Guitar Talk: Conversations with Visionary Players , Pity the Genius and Modern Jazz Standards for Guitar. https://joelharrison.com/ https://www.paulhansonmusic. com/ https://manthing.com/ https://scottamendola.com/ $25 cover charge; byob Students $10 For a reservation, call the bookshop at 415-586-3733

events.title: The Commons Public Hours ☕
events.location: 540 Laguna St, San Francisco + Full Space
events.description:
🎉 Public Hours at the Commons 🎉
Every Sunday, the Commons opens to the public — no membership required. Come co-work, connect, create, or just explore the space at your own pace. ✨
🕘 When: Every Sunday, 9 AM – 10 PM
📍 Where: 540 Laguna St, San Francisco (corner of Hayes & Laguna, basement level)
RSVP and we'll email you your entry code ahead of time — so you can let yourself straight in when you arrive.
──────────────────────────────
🧭 A self-guided day
Public Hours are self-guided — come in, settle in, and make the space your own. Weekends are usually unstaffed, so there's no check-in desk or guided tour. Our members are glad to answer questions about the space; for anything else — including guided tours, which we don't offer as drop-ins — email hello@thesfcommons.com ahead of time.
──────────────────────────────
🔭 Getting in
Your entry code comes by email. Once you RSVP, we'll send you a personal QR code — that's your key for the day. Keep it handy on your phone (and check spam if you don't see it).
Find us. We're at 540 Laguna St, on the corner of Hayes & Laguna. Head down the stairs beside Earthbody to the basement level — that's the Commons.
Scan your QR code at the reader to unlock the door. Hold your phone just below the Kisi reader by the door and it'll let you in.
Your access stays active all day, 9 AM – 10 PM, so you can come and go freely.
Can't find your code on the day? No problem — scan the QR posted on the door to check in and get a fresh one on the spot.
We're shoes-off 🧦 — please clean up after yourself, including dirty dishes and mugs, and use only the front entrance. Trouble getting in? Email hello@thesfcommons.com.




The Commons is a modern-day town square for communal meaning-making, personal discovery, and self-expression in the heart of San Francisco. Apply to become a member here__.

events.title: Autumn Ingathering
events.location: 550 Laguna St, San Francisco + Full Studio
events.description:
Gather with neighbors at the Autumn Neighborhood Ingathering, where we will come together to honor our encounters with loss and the turn of the season.
In our lives, we all experience loss of all sizes (great and small – people, hopes, chapters of life, etc.) that deserve the space to be honored and held. As our natural world brings shorter days and falling leaves with the turn of the season, we’ll gather together to spend time together to honor these losses. We’ll do this through a mix of thoughtful rituals, and through space to connect and reflect with group or solo options.
Sample schedule:
Intro to the turn of the season
Storytelling reflection
Altar creation ceremony (representing a loss in clay)
Breakout activities (choose your own adventure)
Altar release ceremony (salt and re-membering)
What to bring:
Something to write on/with
Optional: If you want to bring a memento (e.g. a photo or keepsake) of something or someone you have lost as a supplement to the altar creation ceremony, you may do so. Decorations like flowers are also welcome!
An open heart
This will also be the debut event put on by our new Neighborhood Flamekeeper Cohort (https://www.sfcontemplarium.org/fkcohort), a group that supports the neighborhood of Hayes Valley and Lower Haight through skills of emotional support and human connection.
Presented by the San Francisco Contemplarium, a neighborhood institution focused on honoring our human journey through contemplative events, installations, and programs that serve the neighborhood to help people slow down and connect.

events.title: LIVE MUSIC: Todd Day Wait, Mac Cornish
events.location: 4-Star Theater, 2200 Clement St, San Francisco, CA 94121
events.description: Todd Day Wait Todd Day Wait is one of the last real American Workhorse, pedal to the metal, Troubadours by way of Missouri, to California, to New Orleans and now Nashville. The original material of Todd Day Wait, is highly influenced by early American folk, country and blues music from the 1920's through the 1960's, embodying the spirit and authenticity of traditional American music. Todd Day Wait, whom you may have heard of from his millions of spins on GemsOnVHS or WesternAF writes and performs his own style of timeless country music. Harking back to Jimmie Rodgers, Willie Nelson, Wynn Stewart and Kris Kristofferson he keeps the spirit of country music alive. In 2009 he put all his earthly belongings on the curb and hit the road, in his diesel shuttle bus fueled by vegetable oil, for a never ending tour. From busking the streets of New Orleans, to playing in the shadow of European castles, to lighting up the honky-tonk dance floors in Nashville, Todd keeps it 60/50. Bandcamp | IG Mac Cornish Growing up in the shadow of the Santa Cruz mountains in Northern California, Mac spent her days strolling through the redwoods and tracing her footsteps on the grounds of her grandfather's cattle ranch in the North Bay. Such a setting that would provide her with an undying appreciation and respect for all things old in age and of the earth. Mac discovered her love for music digging through her parents' record collection, emerging and adorning herself with not just the tunes, but the entire look and aesthetic of the music Mecca, Laurel Canyon. Drawing inspiration from Linda Ronstadt, Gram Parsons, Jackson Browne and Buffalo Springfield, she began forging her own songs and style from her bouts with love, loss, tragedy and tranquillity. After years away spent in Portland, OR and Nashville, TN, Mac has made her way back to California, where she can be found on the stages of dives and honky tonks, warming the hearts of locals with tales of old pickup trucks and summer drives forever. Inspiring crowds to grab hold of their neighbor, dance and twirl and stomp their feet. When she performs, she pins her heart to her collar and shares her wit and charms that transcend the stage and grab hold of the hearts of all who bear witness. A true gem of the west, heart, mind, body, and soul. Bandcamp | IG DOORS at 7:00PM | MUSIC at 8:00 PM Tickets

events.title: Builders Night
events.location: 540 Laguna St, San Francisco + 540 Cafe
events.description:
Builders Night is a weekly space where people show up with a project, work side by side, and leave with more momentum than they could have generated alone. It exists because building can be lonely, and the hardest part is often simply showing up consistently.
The tone is focused and warm. Mostly quiet during deep work, with moments of spontaneous connection when someone gets unstuck or discovers something worth sharing. This is not a networking event or a lecture. The work itself is the center of the night.
Flow
6:30–6:45 PM: Arrival and settling in
6:45–6:55 PM: Opening circle: name, what you're working on, one intention for the night
6:55–8:30 PM: Deep work sprint: quiet, side-by-side building
8:30–9:00 PM: Share-back: what you built, learned, or got stuck on. Make an ask, offer what you know, and support each other.
Who This Is For
People working on software, hardware, businesses, creative projects, writing, design, research, art, anything you're trying to make real. Come if you want accountability, momentum, and the energy of working alongside others. First-timers and regulars both welcome.
What to Bring
Laptop, notebook, sketchbook, instrument, whatever tools your project requires. Come with something to work on, or come ready to figure out what that is.
Norms
Respect the deep work sprint by keeping conversation low during focused time. Share-back is how we learn from each other: share what you built, ask for what you need, and offer what you can. Everyone participates.
Rally (rallysf.com) is an AI builder community in SF.

events.title: John Proctor Is the Villain
events.location: A.C.T., 415 Geary St, San Francisco, CA 94102
events.description:
In a one-stoplight town in Georgia, in a high school AP English class, five young women begin questioning the stories and the heroes they’ve been taught to believe in, against a soundtrack of pop music and fury. As their class dissects a canonical work of literature, the parallels between the play and their own lives become uncomfortably real, and they begin to re-examine who we deem heroic, who we call a villain, and who gets burned in the process.

In a bold artistic collaboration, three of the nation’s leading regional theaters join forces to bring Kimberly Belflower’s explosive coming-of-age story to the West Coast. Centering young voices, this Broadway sensation and new cult classic ignites the kind of conversation that lingers long after the final bell.

events.title: Poet Kim Shuck: A reading
events.location: Bird & Beckett Books & Records, 653 Chenery Street, San Francisco
events.description: Readings by Kim Shuck from three new books: November Dance Shirt : a new collection of Kim’s poems written in November 2023. American Indian Stories by Zitkala-Ša, re-release, with an intro and new essay by Kim. More on Zitkala-Ša here (Wikipedia) . This Music: Record of a Poet Becoming , Janice Gould’s last and posthumous book which Kim helped to edit. This reading will include poems, prose poems and prose written by Indigenous women from the early 20th century through the present day. This work tracks concerns and conditions for Native women, including joy and whimsy. ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~ Kim Shuck embraces the fool and jester qualities of being a modern poet and artist. She is a devotee of San Francisco, whose hills she wanders nearly always on foot. Her maternal grandparents met at the Polish Hall on Shotwell and she spent many hours with her mother and grandmother wandering the Mission St. Miracle Mile, taking books out of the Mission Branch library and watching aquarium fish on the ground floor of what used to be Hale’s. She firmly believes in carrying a bubble wand, keys, pen and notebook and cats cradle string at all times. Kim, whose poetry draws on her multiethnic background which includes Polish and Cherokee heritage, and her experiences as a lifelong resident of San Francisco, served as San Francisco’s seventh Poet Laureate, from 2017-2021. In 2019, she was awarded an inaugural National Laureate Fellowship from the Academy of American Poets, and a PEN Oakland Censorship Award. Among her many books and chapbooks, Pick a Garnet to Sleep In, one in a long line of poetry collections,was published in 2024, and her book of essays Noodle, Rant, Tangent was published in 2022. In her term as Poet Laureate, she hosted scores of free poetry and art workshops for all ages at neighborhood libraries and schools and worked closely with San Francisco Public Library and the San Francisco Arts Commission to launch major citywide initiatives to honor Native American Indigenous Peoples’ heritage.

events.description: Presented by Opera Parallèle Doors open at 5:30PM Workshop starts at 6:00PM Learn the basics of Gullah Stick Pounding in this free workshop led by Melanie DeMore. We will create a foot stomping, hand-clapping rhythmic community and combine it with singing spirituals and songs of protest and peace. Participants will learn about Gullah/Geechee culture through its dynamic music and rhythmic heart. We will, as a community, turn the whole place into a living, breathing drum. About Melanie DeMore Melanie DeMore is a three-time Grammy-nominated singer, composer, choral conductor, and vocal activist who believes in the power of voices raised together. A sought-after workshop leader and music director, she has led choirs and community groups across North America and beyond. A founding member of the Grammy-nominated Linda Tillery and the Cultural Heritage Choir, DeMore uses music as a tool for healing, connection, and social change, believing that “a song can hold you up when there seems to be no ground beneath you.”

events.title: Magic World Premiere       a Rashomon by Ashley Smiley
events.location: Magic Theatre, Fort Mason Center, San Francisco, CA 94123
events.description:
Home Resident Company- Campo Santo and the Magic Theatre premiere something truly special-

“a Rashomon” for San Francisco. Inspired by the maverick Akira Kurosawa film- a movie whose narrative exploded the way narratives could be told with its multiple conflicting storylines intersecting the same plot. This is a story that seeks multiple truth simultaneously. This version of Rashomon lays  the story on Market Street at the foot of the cable car turnaround, as denizens of our City try to answer how a native son- a Black star dancer- died anonymously in his own City. The project, like the narrative, is layered with a creation of  a diorama of the City, puppets, and original videography. Conceived by Joan Osato and created with writer Ashley Smiley of Dirty White Teslas Make Me Sad , Director Edris Cooper-Anifowoshe , with an incredible cast including: Juan Amador, Nora el Samahy, Britney Frazier, and Jeuneé Simon .

events.title: John Proctor Is the Villain
events.location: A.C.T., 415 Geary St, San Francisco, CA 94102
events.description:
In a one-stoplight town in Georgia, in a high school AP English class, five young women begin questioning the stories and the heroes they’ve been taught to believe in, against a soundtrack of pop music and fury. As their class dissects a canonical work of literature, the parallels between the play and their own lives become uncomfortably real, and they begin to re-examine who we deem heroic, who we call a villain, and who gets burned in the process.

In a bold artistic collaboration, three of the nation’s leading regional theaters join forces to bring Kimberly Belflower’s explosive coming-of-age story to the West Coast. Centering young voices, this Broadway sensation and new cult classic ignites the kind of conversation that lingers long after the final bell.

events.title: LIVE MUSIC: Babehoven, Pileup (Presented by THROWIN' BO'S)
events.location: 4-Star Theater, 2200 Clement St, San Francisco, CA 94121
events.description: Throwin’ Bo’s presents: Babehoven Babehoven is the Hudson, NY based project of singer-songwriter Maya Bon and collaborator Ryan Albert. Since 2017, the band has carved out a sound that blends melodic indie and folk rock with an occasional nod towards country. Bon serves as the project’s principal songwriter and lyricist, while Albert, a multi-instrumentalist and producer, further shapes the sonic world around her songs. Together, they’ve built a body of work that feels both intimate and expansive. "Blue Around You," Babehoven's new single, is a country-flecked stomper. The song finds Bon singing with hard-won resilience: "Yesterday a stranger told me they can see / That I feel levels of pain that could've broken me / And I thought, mmm but I survived it." Recorded at The Chicken Shack and 12 Lb Genius in Upstate NY, Maya and Ryan gathered an excellent crew of musicians with producer Phil Weinrobe at the helm—Oliver Hill, Zosha Warpeha, Dylan Nowik, Jared Samuel, Ellington Peet, and Nick Kinsey. The core of the song was recorded live with no playback or headphones with the feel of the room being as much an instrument as the hardanger fiddle and harmonies that soar overhead. events.title: The Commons Public Hours ☕
events.location: 540 Laguna St, San Francisco + Full Space
events.description:
🎉 Public Hours at the Commons 🎉
Every Sunday, the Commons opens to the public — no membership required. Come co-work, connect, create, or just explore the space at your own pace. ✨
🕘 When: Every Sunday, 9 AM – 10 PM
📍 Where: 540 Laguna St, San Francisco (corner of Hayes & Laguna, basement level)
RSVP and we'll email you your entry code ahead of time — so you can let yourself straight in when you arrive.
──────────────────────────────
🧭 A self-guided day
Public Hours are self-guided — come in, settle in, and make the space your own. Weekends are usually unstaffed, so there's no check-in desk or guided tour. Our members are glad to answer questions about the space; for anything else — including guided tours, which we don't offer as drop-ins — email hello@thesfcommons.com ahead of time.
──────────────────────────────
🔭 Getting in
Your entry code comes by email. Once you RSVP, we'll send you a personal QR code — that's your key for the day. Keep it handy on your phone (and check spam if you don't see it).
Find us. We're at 540 Laguna St, on the corner of Hayes & Laguna. Head down the stairs beside Earthbody to the basement level — that's the Commons.
Scan your QR code at the reader to unlock the door. Hold your phone just below the Kisi reader by the door and it'll let you in.
Your access stays active all day, 9 AM – 10 PM, so you can come and go freely.
Can't find your code on the day? No problem — scan the QR posted on the door to check in and get a fresh one on the spot.
We're shoes-off 🧦 — please clean up after yourself, including dirty dishes and mugs, and use only the front entrance. Trouble getting in? Email hello@thesfcommons.com.




The Commons is a modern-day town square for communal meaning-making, personal discovery, and self-expression in the heart of San Francisco. Apply to become a member here__.

events.title: Builders Night
events.location: 540 Laguna St, San Francisco + 540 Cafe
events.description:
Builders Night is a weekly space where people show up with a project, work side by side, and leave with more momentum than they could have generated alone. It exists because building can be lonely, and the hardest part is often simply showing up consistently.
The tone is focused and warm. Mostly quiet during deep work, with moments of spontaneous connection when someone gets unstuck or discovers something worth sharing. This is not a networking event or a lecture. The work itself is the center of the night.
Flow
6:30–6:45 PM: Arrival and settling in
6:45–6:55 PM: Opening circle: name, what you're working on, one intention for the night
6:55–8:30 PM: Deep work sprint: quiet, side-by-side building
8:30–9:00 PM: Share-back: what you built, learned, or got stuck on. Make an ask, offer what you know, and support each other.
Who This Is For
People working on software, hardware, businesses, creative projects, writing, design, research, art, anything you're trying to make real. Come if you want accountability, momentum, and the energy of working alongside others. First-timers and regulars both welcome.
What to Bring
Laptop, notebook, sketchbook, instrument, whatever tools your project requires. Come with something to work on, or come ready to figure out what that is.
Norms
Respect the deep work sprint by keeping conversation low during focused time. Share-back is how we learn from each other: share what you built, ask for what you need, and offer what you can. Everyone participates.
Rally (rallysf.com) is an AI builder community in SF.

events.title: The Commons Public Hours ☕
events.location: 540 Laguna St, San Francisco + Full Space
events.description:
🎉 Public Hours at the Commons 🎉
Every Sunday, the Commons opens to the public — no membership required. Come co-work, connect, create, or just explore the space at your own pace. ✨
🕘 When: Every Sunday, 9 AM – 10 PM
📍 Where: 540 Laguna St, San Francisco (corner of Hayes & Laguna, basement level)
RSVP and we'll email you your entry code ahead of time — so you can let yourself straight in when you arrive.
──────────────────────────────
🧭 A self-guided day
Public Hours are self-guided — come in, settle in, and make the space your own. Weekends are usually unstaffed, so there's no check-in desk or guided tour. Our members are glad to answer questions about the space; for anything else — including guided tours, which we don't offer as drop-ins — email hello@thesfcommons.com ahead of time.
──────────────────────────────
🔭 Getting in
Your entry code comes by email. Once you RSVP, we'll send you a personal QR code — that's your key for the day. Keep it handy on your phone (and check spam if you don't see it).
Find us. We're at 540 Laguna St, on the corner of Hayes & Laguna. Head down the stairs beside Earthbody to the basement level — that's the Commons.
Scan your QR code at the reader to unlock the door. Hold your phone just below the Kisi reader by the door and it'll let you in.
Your access stays active all day, 9 AM – 10 PM, so you can come and go freely.
Can't find your code on the day? No problem — scan the QR posted on the door to check in and get a fresh one on the spot.
We're shoes-off 🧦 — please clean up after yourself, including dirty dishes and mugs, and use only the front entrance. Trouble getting in? Email hello@thesfcommons.com.




The Commons is a modern-day town square for communal meaning-making, personal discovery, and self-expression in the heart of San Francisco. Apply to become a member here__.

events.title: Builders Night
events.location: 540 Laguna St, San Francisco + 540 Cafe
events.description:
Builders Night is a weekly space where people show up with a project, work side by side, and leave with more momentum than they could have generated alone. It exists because building can be lonely, and the hardest part is often simply showing up consistently.
The tone is focused and warm. Mostly quiet during deep work, with moments of spontaneous connection when someone gets unstuck or discovers something worth sharing. This is not a networking event or a lecture. The work itself is the center of the night.
Flow
6:30–6:45 PM: Arrival and settling in
6:45–6:55 PM: Opening circle: name, what you're working on, one intention for the night
6:55–8:30 PM: Deep work sprint: quiet, side-by-side building
8:30–9:00 PM: Share-back: what you built, learned, or got stuck on. Make an ask, offer what you know, and support each other.
Who This Is For
People working on software, hardware, businesses, creative projects, writing, design, research, art, anything you're trying to make real. Come if you want accountability, momentum, and the energy of working alongside others. First-timers and regulars both welcome.
What to Bring
Laptop, notebook, sketchbook, instrument, whatever tools your project requires. Come with something to work on, or come ready to figure out what that is.
Norms
Respect the deep work sprint by keeping conversation low during focused time. Share-back is how we learn from each other: share what you built, ask for what you need, and offer what you can. Everyone participates.
Rally (rallysf.com) is an AI builder community in SF.

events.description: FREE Co-presented with Green Apple Books Join us when we welcome Jen Siraganian for the release of her debut poetry collection, Everything Has Been Moved, Even the Dead! Siraganian traces a self shaped by history, fragmentation, and memory as she weaves her family’s past in the Middle East with her identity as an Armenian American woman and mother. Whether portraying a grandparent’s survival during the Armenian Genocide, a father’s childhood in 1940s Palestine, or a son’s birth when “death is a neighbor,” Siraganian’s poems interrogate concepts of home, origins, belonging, and displacement.
