events.title: LIVE MUSIC: Dagmar Zuniga (Presented by THROWIN' BO'S)
events.location: 4-Star Theater, 2200 Clement St, San Francisco, CA 94121
events.description: Throwin’ Bo’s presents: Dagmar Zuniga Nicaraguan-American artist Dagmar Zuniga makes music that feels both intimate and expansive: songs drift like disrupted signals, carried by harmony, tape hiss, and a strong sense of touch. Her debut solo album in filth your mystery is kingdom / far smile peasant in yellow music — written and recorded in New York, Norway, and Athens, Georgia over a period of five years on her longtime companion, the Tascam 424 — was released by the People’s Coalition of Tandy on Bandcamp & YouTube in January 2025, accompanied by a small tape run that sold out instantly. The project quickly garnered over two hundred thousand views and the attention of artists such as Mount Eerie, who invited her to tour with them that summer. This year, what was once a jewel of tapped-in algorithms and message boards will meet the world at large, with in filth arriving digitally on March 4 , and physically on April 10 , via AD 93 . in filth is an atmospheric, devotional collage where one voice multiplies into a chorus of selves, sometimes delicate, sometimes severe; an effect created by Zuniga’s masterful layering of texture and complex harmonies. Synths glitter out like spears of sunlight from beneath clouds of moody, time-distorted guitars, and songs spin about themselves like tightly-wound music boxes, making use of a kind of hypnotic repetition, before melting apart into their components or slipping into the following track. Zuniga began recording to tape as a teenager, drawn to the physicality of the medium — how a tape recording is fragile, mutable, and alive. Though her ethereal sound may draw easy comparisons to other female pioneers of psychedelic folk, she is influenced just as much by the darker sounds of Syd Barrett and The Fall. Like Barrett, Zuniga is a painter, and she is interested not only in recording music but in creating a full, self-contained artistic universe: she creates her own artwork, merchandise, music videos, and bootleg tapes of new and unfinished music that she exclusively sells at live shows ( “If something is not material, it does not exist,” she insists). Her world has not gone unvisited, garnering her a monthly show on NTS Radio ‘World of Pain’, as well as a forthcoming appearance at Rewire Festival in April 2026. Though Zuniga’s work explores themes of solitude and suffering, the suffering in her songs is not borrowed or displayed; it is held, then opened outward through empathy — an exacting practice of attention that insists on shared ground. Solitude, in her work, is not withdrawal but a starting point for connection. Likewise, over time, her recording process has become increasingly communal, with in filth featuring musicians across the globe. Newer recordings widen the circle even more. For Zuniga, collaboration is a way to “find a place between worlds,” echoing Badiou’s idea of love as a vision refracted through the prism of difference. Meaning emerges there — in the space between voices, between artist and listener. “I hope my music helps people work through difficult experiences,” she says. “The same way it helps me.” Bandcamp | IG Support to be announced DOORS at 7:00PM | MUSIC at 8:00 PM Tickets

Every Sunday, the Commons opens to the public — no membership required. Come co-work, connect, create, or just explore the space at your own pace. ✨

Public Hours are self-guided — come in, settle in, and make the space your own. Weekends are usually unstaffed, so there's no check-in desk or guided tour. Our members are glad to answer questions about the space; for anything else — including guided tours, which we don't offer as drop-ins — email hello@thesfcommons.com ahead of time.
──────────────────────────────
🔭 Getting in
Your entry code comes by email. Once you RSVP, we'll send you a personal QR code — that's your key for the day. Keep it handy on your phone (and check spam if you don't see it).
Find us. We're at 540 Laguna St, on the corner of Hayes & Laguna. Head down the stairs beside Earthbody to the basement level — that's the Commons.
Scan your QR code at the reader to unlock the door. Hold your phone just below the Kisi reader by the door and it'll let you in.
Your access stays active all day, 9 AM – 10 PM, so you can come and go freely.
Can't find your code on the day? No problem — scan the QR posted on the door to check in and get a fresh one on the spot.
We're shoes-off 🧦 — please clean up after yourself, including dirty dishes and mugs, and use only the front entrance. Trouble getting in? Email hello@thesfcommons.com.

Hi Everyone,
We’re continuing our Purpose Alignment Circle series with a community gathering: Life After the Leap.
You took the leap. You left the job. You took the sabbatical. You made the big change. And now you’re back - and what often goes unspoken is how disorienting this phase can feel.
Coming back isn’t a finish line. It’s its own transition. And most of us are navigating it without a map.
This evening is for career changers, sabbatical-takers, and anyone who has ever wondered: “Okay, I did the brave thing… now what?”
Hosted and facilitated by Bernadette Lagman join us to come together to share real stories, reflect honestly, and find our footing, together.
Come as you are. Bring your questions. And an open mind. You're not alone in this.

Name, pronouns, where you're from

Big Group Discussion (40 min)
Open reflections and deep listening
What feels most alive or unclear in your current path?
Small Breakout Groups (30 min)
What feels most alive or unclear in your current path?
Accountability Pairing (10 min)
Pair up and share one action step
Align on follow-up/accountability

Final reflections + gratitude What support do you still need?

events.title: Builders Night
events.location: 540 Laguna St, San Francisco + 540 Cafe
events.description:
Builders Night is a weekly space where people show up with a project, work side by side, and leave with more momentum than they could have generated alone. It exists because building can be lonely, and the hardest part is often simply showing up consistently.
The tone is focused and warm. Mostly quiet during deep work, with moments of spontaneous connection when someone gets unstuck or discovers something worth sharing. This is not a networking event or a lecture. The work itself is the center of the night.
Flow
6:30–6:45 PM: Arrival and settling in
6:45–6:55 PM: Opening circle: name, what you're working on, one intention for the night
6:55–8:30 PM: Deep work sprint: quiet, side-by-side building
8:30–9:00 PM: Share-back: what you built, learned, or got stuck on. Make an ask, offer what you know, and support each other.
Who This Is For
People working on software, hardware, businesses, creative projects, writing, design, research, art, anything you're trying to make real. Come if you want accountability, momentum, and the energy of working alongside others. First-timers and regulars both welcome.
What to Bring
Laptop, notebook, sketchbook, instrument, whatever tools your project requires. Come with something to work on, or come ready to figure out what that is.
Norms
Respect the deep work sprint by keeping conversation low during focused time. Share-back is how we learn from each other: share what you built, ask for what you need, and offer what you can. Everyone participates.

Come breathe, release, & reset...
Somatic Breathwork is an embodiment experience designed to take you out of your thinking mind and into the deep intelligence of your body — where true healing, clarity, and release happen. It allows your body to express and discharge stored emotions, stress, and old narratives that may be weighing you down.
Somatic Breathwork uses circular connected breathing together with rhythmic music to produce a cathartic emotional release. This release may be in the form of moving, shaking, yelling, crying, laughing, or simply deep stillness.
It gives your body the opportunity to express emotions or actions that may otherwise be unacceptable in modern social settings, allowing your nervous system to process traumas and restore balance.
Using the breath, you’ll engage your body’s innate ability to heal — sweeping out any defenses, blockages, restrictions, or pains that hold you back from showing up as your truest self.
Many participants experience profound emotional release, newfound clarity, and a grounded sense of calm even after a single session.
This experience is designed to:
Move you out of your mind and into your body's electrical network
Release stuck energy, emotions, or trauma responses
Reset your nervous system into grounded calm and clarity
Break old patterns and reconnect you to your authentic self
Increase compassion, presence, and emotional resilience
Support cathartic release in a safe, guided container
Participants often report:
Deep emotional release
More calm, peace, and clarity
Release of anger, grief, frustration, or stagnant energy
Increased presence, awareness, and intuition
Breakthrough insights about their life, patterns, and purpose
Feeling more open, soft, and connected to themselves and others

✨ Opening Check-In & Introduction

Whether you're seeking release, clarity, a reset, or simply a moment to reconnect with yourself — this session is for you.

Anna Bolender is a certified Somatic Embodiment & Intuitive Life Coach, Somatic Breathwork and Quantum Wellness Practitioner, Reiki Master, and lifelong student of holistic health and well-being.
Through her coaching programs and workshops, Anna guides others to return home to themselves — releasing what keeps them stuck, reconnecting with their body and inner wisdom, and creating real, lasting transformation from the inside out.
Blending somatics, energy healing, quantum wellness, and mindset work, she helps clients break free from self-sabotaging patterns, repattern their nervous system, and cultivate simple daily rituals that support a fulfilling, grounded, and aligned life.
Anna’s mission is to empower others to feel connected, alive, and radiant — no matter what life brings.

events.location: Black Bird Bookstore, 4033 Judah St, San Francisco, CA 94122
events.description: Jenny Andrus Children's Book Author and Librarian Elsa's Chessboard Elsa carries her chessboard everywhere, always ready for a game. When World War II forces her from Europe, can chess help make America home? Growing up in 1900s Vienna, Elsa watches her brothers play chess. “No girls!” they tell her when she first asks to learn; but she’s determined, and soon she’s such a pro that they give Elsa her very own special chessboard. From then on, Elsa plays chess whenever she can. When she grows up, she even meets her husband over games in the park. But when World War II grips Europe, the young Jewish family flees to America, where they find themselves surrounded by unfamiliar languages. Luckily, Elsa knows one language that can always bring people together: chess! Based on the life of author Jenny Andrus’s grandmother, with illustrations by award-winning artist Julie Downing, Elsa’s Chessboard is an inspiring and exciting tale, perfect for any reader who's ever found meaning in a special object. events.title: LIVE MUSIC: June McDoom, Eliana Glass (Presented by THROWIN' BO'S)
events.location: 4-Star Theater, 2200 Clement St, San Francisco, CA 94121
events.description: Throwin’ Bo’s presents: June McDoom There is a hush most of us only knew as children, the warm drift between familiar household sounds and being carried to bed, a place that belongs to you and to some self you have not met yet. June McDoom's debut full-length, Follow the Light, lives in that dream space and then keeps walking, slipping out of time and waking somewhere new, barely familiar enough to feel like home yet wholly your own. She came up in a Jamaican household on the edge of the Florida Everglades, an existence built of extended family, communal care, bass and harmonics. Her father, a carpenter and a student of sound, built his own speakers and kept three sound systems going across as many rooms. His low end would rise through her bedroom floor like some wayward cat while she lay above it with folk records, finding harmonies that were new and hers alone. Two musics in one room. Lushness as past and premonition. She found folk on her own, somewhere between the cast recording of The Sound of Music and Simon and Garfunkel, while everyone around her called it sleepy music. She did not mind being the only one. The solitude let her fall for harmony first, before words, before anything else, and harmony is still the thing she reaches for. Generationally speaking, the music was already in the air. Her grandfather, Colin Smith, is a distinguished mento man who played banjo and guitar and built his own rumba boxes, worked to keep Jamaica's oldest acoustic folk form alive. Mento is the root of all of it: ska, rock steady, reggae, dub and everything after. He is the one who put a guitar in her hands. An inheritance, a gift and a map. Even her name is part of it, though she will tell you she landed on it more by feel than reason. She records as June McDoom, born Alyssa, June being a nickname one of her grandmothers, Joan, went by, a name she thought was cool to carry and simply liked the sound of. An etheric channel that reverberates all the same. A dub all its own. Made slowly and by hand with her longtime partner Evan Wright, Follow the Light lays the harmony of folk over the rhythm of dub, with Dionne Warwick, Minnie Riperton, Pentangle and the washed guitars of Cocteau Twins haunting its outer edges. Voice and guitar seeking each other out first, then everything else stacked across long days in the studio they keep at home, restraint kept on purpose. The lead single "Without You" is the whole method surfacing, split open and sparkling like a geode in a creek bed. Angelic heroics, and nothing less. At the heart is family. Her grandmother Aggie, the light behind "Memory," guiding still. And underneath, the quieter truth the record keeps: none of us are only one person, but a continuum of selves, the ones who shaped us and the ones we have yet to meet. Future you is an ancestor your current self gets to greet. Press play and the same invitation is yours: A few minutes out of time, a place that turns familiar the longer you stay until you surface somewhere new and find it was yours all along. Bandcamp | IG Eliana Glass Eliana Glass (b.1997) is a singer, pianist, and visual artist born in Australia, raised in Seattle, and based in New York. She is a graduate of the jazz program at The New School where she studied with such mentors as Andrew Cyrille, Ben Street, Kris Davis, and Jay Clayton. She also holds a degree in Visual Studies and Writing and works freely across multiple mediums. In the past year she has released her debut album, E, an album comprised primarily of piano and voice, via Shelter Press. Her work dedicates special attention to sparseness, voice, and her relationship to the piano, a lifelong entity since she was a kid. Bandcamp | IG DOORS at 7:00PM | MUSIC at 8:00 PM Tickets

events.title: Nashville Honeymoon
events.location: Bird & Beckett Books & Records, 653 Chenery Street, San Francisco
events.description: Lynne Maes, rhythm guitar & vocals; Hank Maninger, lead guitar & vocals; Tim Wagar, bass guitar; Paul Revelli drums You’re in for two sets in honky tonk heaven. Mainstays of the Bay Area Americana scene, and the Bird & Beckett bandstand, for nearly a decade, Nashville Honeymoon has traversed country, rockabilly, bluegrass, and pop across four albums, writing songs that uplift the tangled mess of day-to-day life and investigate universal themes of love and loss – often at the same time. Their latest album, Sidewinder, is true to its title, offering a collection of songs that are grounded in classic country while edging into different sounds, genres, and themes that run through American pop music. This is some of the sweetest, sauciest, and most sincere country music you’ll ever hear. SUNDAY HAPPY HOUR! Grab your partner! Gather your kids! Call a friend! Come on down to the bookshop to get a bit better acquainted with your neighbors and just have a ball before the start of another long hard work week!

events.title: Avotcja & Modúpue: afro-latin jazz and poetry
events.location: Bird & Beckett Books & Records, 653 Chenery Street, San Francisco
events.description: AVOTCJA’s poetry is music and Avotcja’s music is poetry. Both are as hot as fire and as soothing as snow flakes. And in both she brings the best of her talent in Spanish and English. Listen to her. Read her. Enjoy her. Celebrate her.” • Camincha – Peruvian Poet/Novelist; & Pacifica Poet Laureate, 2017-2021. Poet / Playwright / Essayist / Fiction Writer / Multi-Percussionist / Photographer / Teacher, Avotcja is a Bay Area icon and is renowned for her group Modúpue. At Bird & Beckett tonight, Modúpue will be a quintet with Avotcja joined by violinist Sandi Poindexter , saxophonist Francis Wong , bassist Heshima Mark Williams and talking drum master Baba Ken Okolulo . Modúpue was named best jazz group of the year twice, in 2005 and again in 2010, by the Bay Area Blues Hall of Fame. Avotcja herself was named a “Jazz Hero” by the Jazz Journalists Association. Her radio shows on KPFA – Bebop, Cubop & the Musical Truth (Tuesdays, 8-10pm), and KPOO – La Verdad Musical (Fridays, noon-3pm), have been soul satisfying for decades, expressing the boundless joy she always finds in the music. As for her poetry, no one taps deeper wells of humanity than Avotcja! We love her more than we can express. Read here what Linda Tillery, Chuy Varela, Camincha, Greg Landau, Leslie Simon, Ishmael Reed, Lady Bianca, Elaine Cohen, Julian Carroll and Melanie Berzon have had to say in praise of Avotcja! The cover charge for the quintet tonight is $25 cash or venmo, payable at the door. College and high school students – $10. Grade school and younger, free. No one turned away for lack of funds. Wheelchair accessible. Bring your own beverages, but please eat out or at home before or after the show. Lots of good restaurants in the neighborhood, cafes, and grocers!

events.title: The Best Journey in the World: An Antarctic Story with Kim Stanley Robinson
events.location: Grace Cathedral, 1100 California St, San Francisco
events.description: FREE, $10-$15 suggested donation, $49 with signed book Co-presented with Grace Cathedral’s The Forum Interweaving memoir and good old fashioned ice adventure, Kim Stanley Robinson’s latest takes readers along on the journeys that have happened before and those that may never happen again. In May of 1911, Robert Scott and his men said goodbye to the sun and settled in for the long Antarctic winter. When the sun returned in September, they would try to become the first people to reach the South Pole. However, a week past the winter solstice, Scott’s second-in-command decided to take an impromptu sled trip. Chronicled by zoological assistant Apsley Cherry-Garrard, this side trip became The Worst Journey in the World, one of the best adventure books ever written. Robinson first read Cherry-Garrard’s book in his twenties and re-read it again in 1995, as preparation for a research trip to Antarctica for his Mars novels. It was a dream excursion: he traveled around the continent, by snowmobile and helicopter and airplane, and followed in their ill-fated footsteps. Doors at 7:00 PM.

events.title: Chinese Americans: The Most Litigious, Civilly Disobedient Americans
events.location: The Commonwealth Club of California, San Francisco
events.description: David Y. Lei, born in Taiwan, immigrated to the United States in 1956. He began his career as a social worker in San Francisco’s Chinatown in the late 1960s, working with young people involved in Chinatown gangs. In 1981, he entered the business world, exporting consumer products to Mexico. He sold his business in 2003 and retired. Lei served as vice chair of the Asian Art Museum board and directed San Francisco’s Chinese New Year Parade from 1977 to 2006.

events.title: The Lenny Carlson Music Collective
events.location: Bird & Beckett Books & Records, 653 Chenery Street, San Francisco
events.description: The Lenny Carlson Music Collective is a unique chamber ensemble that performs Carlson’s original compositions along with standards. His musical directions converge in the genre of Americana, blending Jazz, pop, folk, and classical. A Los Angeles native and award-winning composer, Carlson has also been an accomplished jazz guitarist, producer, music professor and author. Since 2009, he has been resident composer for Jeff Sanford’s Cartoon Jazz Orchestra. The Collective’s premiere performance at Bird & Beckett on 1/22/27 will feature Kevin Gerzevitz, piano; Michelle Maruyama, violin; Carla Wilson, bassoon and Luke Kirley, tuba/euphonium. Kevin Gerzevitz’s compositions and arrangements will also be performed. Carlson’s recent discography includes the title and three additional selections on Jeff Sanford’s Playland at the Beach CD (2023), available on Spotify and Bandcamp; Down by the Riverside: Theme and Variations CD (2022) on Bandcamp; and Nothing Wrong (2019), a Cartoon Jazz CD comprised entirely of his compositions, on Bandcamp. Carlson’s suite Four Sketches for My Mother (2022) appears in the S.F. Public Library’s 2026 Bay Beats music collection. The Bird & Beckett performance will be streamed live on Bird & Beckett’s YouTube channel and Facebook page. The YouTube stream can be found at this link: https://www.youtube.com/@bird_beckett/streams

events.title: Lizard Boy
events.location: San Francisco Playhouse, 450 Post St, San Francisco, CA 94102
events.description: Trevor has spent years hiding from the world. Ever since a childhood encounter left him with green, scaly skin, he’s become something of a local legend in Seattle, more myth than man. But on the night of Monster Fest, he decides to take a risk. A first date with his crush, Cary, pulls him out of isolation and into a city alive with possibility. When an unexpected encounter hints that the past may not be finished with him, Trevor is forced to confront the part of himself he’s tried to keep hidden. With an electrifying indie-rock score, Lizard Boy has become a cult favorite, celebrated for its originality, heart, and genre-bending storytelling. This bold, offbeat musical is a celebration of identity, connection, and the courage it takes to be seen.

events.title: LIVE MUSIC: @ (Presented by THROWIN' BO'S)
events.location: 4-Star Theater, 2200 Clement St, San Francisco, CA 94121
events.description: Throwin’ Bo’s presents: @ Songwriters Victoria Rose and Stone Filipczak are the creative force behind @, a singular duo whose inventive collaboration has reimagined psychedelic folk for a new generation. On Autosmile, their first album for 4AD, the pair expand on the acclaimed promise of their debut Mind Palace Music, blending timeless songwriting with adventurous arrangements, dense harmonies, and a playful spirit that constantly pushes beyond genre boundaries. Though now based in Philadelphia, Victoria and Stone continue their distinctive songwriting process: working independently before completing each other’s compositions. Recorded largely at home with a humble collection of equipment and enriched by contributions from close friends on cello, violin, and drums, Autosmile transforms lo-fi methods into something remarkably lush, immersive, and emotionally resonant. Across eleven songs, @ balance darkness and wonder with striking confidence. The album moves effortlessly between haunting folk textures, progressive flourishes, indie-pop hooks, and moments of cinematic beauty. Highlights include the expansive title track “Autosmile,” the nostalgic earworm “I Know You Are (But What Am I Thinking),” and the intricately arranged “Punish My Mind,” each exploring themes of change, self-reflection, loss, and acceptance through lyrics that remain deliberately open-ended and deeply relatable. Equal parts mysterious, virtuosic, and playful, Autosmile showcases @ at their most fully realized—an adventurous partnership capable of looking backward and forward at once. It is an album of contrasts: beauty and pain, humor and gravity, intimacy and ambition. In the face of uncertainty, @ offer curiosity, connection, and the possibility of transformation. Guerrero is hailed by The New Yorker as “a master of tradition who dares to deconstruct the art form.”

events.title: Gilles Vonsattel Piano Recital
events.location: Presidio Theatre, 99 Moraga Ave, San Francisco, CA 94129
events.description: The extraordinary pianist Gilles Vonsattel offers a captivating look inside Beethoven becoming Beethoven as we know him, part of a series of special engagements in the Bay Area that see the stunningly original performer take on the composer’s complete piano sonata cycle. With this rare performance of four landmark piano sonatas presented in a single evening, Gilles Vonsattel hands us the keys to unlocking the psyche of a genius. Works to be performed – Sonata no. 1 in F Minor, Op. 2; Sonata No. 21 in C Major, Op. 53 “Waldstein”; Sonata No. 27 in E Minor, Op. 90; Sonata No. 28 in A Major, Op. 101. Presented in partnership with Music@Menlo and Stanford Live.

events.title: Life of Pi
events.location: San Francisco Playhouse, 450 Post St, San Francisco, CA 94102
events.description: Sixteen-year-old Pi Patel sets out on a journey across the ocean with his family, only to find himself alone after a catastrophic shipwreck. Adrift on a lifeboat in the vast Pacific, he must learn to survive alongside a group of unlikely companions, including a hyena, a zebra, an orangutan, and a Bengal tiger. As the days stretch into weeks, reality and imagination begin to blur. Pi is pushed to his limits, confronting fear, faith, and the stories we tell ourselves to endure the unimaginable. Winner of five Olivier Awards including Best New Play, and hailed by The Guardian as “extraordinary and unmissable,” this breathtaking stage adaptation brings Yann Martel’s beloved novel to life through stunning visuals and groundbreaking puppetry. Life of Pi is a theatrical event about survival, belief, and the power of storytelling.

events.title: The Comeuppance
events.location: A.C.T., 415 Geary St, San Francisco, CA 94102
events.description: When a group of millennial classmates meet to pregame for their twentieth high school reunion, everyone is nervous for the night ahead. As alcohol and weed help the self-declared “Multi-Ethnic Reject Group” let their guards down, they begin to reminisce and reveal how their lives have unfolded since graduation. Did their friendships stand the test of time? Why do they remember certain moments from their past differently? From Pulitzer Prize–winning and two-time Tony Award–winning playwright Branden Jacob-Jenkins ( Gloria ) comes a new profound tragicomedy about the reunion that awaits us all.

events.title: Music of Remembrance: Women in the Shadows
events.location: Presidio Theatre, 99 Moraga Ave, San Francisco, CA 94129
events.description: Women in the Shadows explores the inner worlds of women artists overshadowed by history. The featured work, composer Jake Heggie and librettist Gene Scheer’s Camille Claudel: Into the Fire, is a theatrical song cycle that traces the life of the brilliant French sculptor. The creators give Claudel a passionate voice, casting her as more than Auguste Rodin’s muse--a formidable artist in her own right. Mezzo-soprano Nikola Printz brings an intense musical and dramatic presence to the role, praised in the San Francisco Chronicle for performances that are “heartrending, musically resplendent . . . and thrillingly fierce.”

events.title: Life of Pi
events.location: San Francisco Playhouse, 450 Post St, San Francisco, CA 94102
events.description: Sixteen-year-old Pi Patel sets out on a journey across the ocean with his family, only to find himself alone after a catastrophic shipwreck. Adrift on a lifeboat in the vast Pacific, he must learn to survive alongside a group of unlikely companions, including a hyena, a zebra, an orangutan, and a Bengal tiger. As the days stretch into weeks, reality and imagination begin to blur. Pi is pushed to his limits, confronting fear, faith, and the stories we tell ourselves to endure the unimaginable. Winner of five Olivier Awards including Best New Play, and hailed by The Guardian as “extraordinary and unmissable,” this breathtaking stage adaptation brings Yann Martel’s beloved novel to life through stunning visuals and groundbreaking puppetry. Life of Pi is a theatrical event about survival, belief, and the power of storytelling.

events.title: Sweeney Todd: The Demon Barber of Fleet Street
events.location: San Francisco Playhouse, 450 Post St, San Francisco, CA 94102
events.description: Benjamin Barker returns to London a changed man. Now known as Sweeney Todd, the barber comes back to a city that took everything from him, driven by a single, consuming desire for revenge. Above Mrs. Lovett’s struggling pie shop, he sets up a new practice, and together they form a darkly ingenious partnership. As business begins to thrive, the line between justice and obsession starts to blur, with chilling consequences for all who cross their path. Winner of eight Tony Awards including Best Musical, Stephen Sondheim’s Sweeney Todd: The Demon Barber of Fleet Street is a thrilling and unforgettable tale of vengeance, morality, and the cost of losing one’s humanity.

events.description: Benjamin Barker returns to London a changed man. Now known as Sweeney Todd, the barber comes back to a city that took everything from him, driven by a single, consuming desire for revenge. Above Mrs. Lovett’s struggling pie shop, he sets up a new practice, and together they form a darkly ingenious partnership. As business begins to thrive, the line between justice and obsession starts to blur, with chilling consequences for all who cross their path. Winner of eight Tony Awards including Best Musical, Stephen Sondheim’s Sweeney Todd: The Demon Barber of Fleet Street is a thrilling and unforgettable tale of vengeance, morality, and the cost of losing one’s humanity.

events.title: Black Bird Writing Club
events.location: Black Bird Bookstore, 4033 Judah St, San Francisco, CA 94122
events.description: *When purchasing your ticket, please specify the date you are signing up for* Time and space to write in community with fellow writers. Self-guided, bring your own pen and paper, laptop or journal. No instruction. We meet, we write for an hour, and then we mingle over wine, tea, and snacks. $10 entry. Reserve your spot with a ticket. Tea, snacks, + wine provided.
